Oṃ 3 aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ—at the ankle of the right foot; Oṃ 3 klīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ—at the sole; Oṃ 3 sauḥ sakalahrīṃ—at the tip; Oṃ 3 aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ—at the ankle of the left foot.
Oṃ 3 klīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ—at the soles; Oṃ 3 sauḥ sakalahrīṃ—at the tips of the feet; Oṃ 3 aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ—at the base of the right foot;
(p. 58) Oṃ 3 klīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ—at the thigh; Oṃ 3 sauḥ sakalahrīṃ—at the knee.
Oṃ 3 Aiṃ Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ—at the base of the left foot; Oṃ 3 Klīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ—at the thigh; Oṃ 3 Sauḥ Sa Ka La Hrīṃ—at the knee.
O Goddess of the Gods, one should thus perform the placement upon the limbs according to the sequence of withdrawal (saṃhārakrama).
Know that the Supreme Goddess indeed knows through the very process of emanation.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ—salutation to the heart for the sake of omniscience;
klīṃ, svāhā to the head for the sake of eternal contentment; sauḥ, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock for the sake of beginningless non-obstruction;
aiṃ, huṃ to the armor for the sake of absolute sovereignty; klīṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes for the sake of eternal imperishability.
*Sauḥ*, for the state of infinite power (*ananta-śaktitā*), *astrāya phaṭ*. Thus is the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*).
*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ namaḥ śrīmahātripurasundarī māṃ rakṣa hṛdayāya namaḥ*;
*Oṃ 3 aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ namaḥ śrīmahātripurasundarī māṃ rakṣa śirase svāhā*.
9 Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, protect me! Vaṣaṭ for the crest-lock (śikhā). 9 Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, protect me! Huṃ for the armor (kavaca).
9 Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, protect me! Vauṣaṭ for the three eyes (netratraya).
"O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, protect me! *Astrāya Phaṭ*—this is another [method for] the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). (p.
59) *Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ*, O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, obeisance to the heart, the abode of the power of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-śakti-dhāman*)."

4 *hasakahala* hrīṃ, to the abode of the power of eternal contentment, Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, svāhā to the head; 4 *sakala* hrīṃ, to the abode of the power of consciousness, Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, vaṣaṭ to the crest-lock; 4 *ka e ī la* hrīṃ, to the abode of the power of sovereignty, Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, huṃ to the armor.
4 *hasakahalahrīṃ* Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, to the abode of the power of eternal imperishability, *vauṣaṭ* to the three eyes;
4 *sakalahrīṃ* Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, to the abode of infinite power, *phaṭ* to the weapon (*astra*).
One should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) for the Goddess by repeating [the mantra] twice in due order.
In the case of one born under Śaila, [the groups] are three, two, one, and ten, according to the number three and two.

Another set of six limbs is given in the *Mantramahodadhi*: "Astrāya Phaṭ. Having visualized nine yonis—square and circular—in the *mūlādhāra*, *svādhiṣṭhāna*, *maṇipūra*, *anāhata*, *viśuddhi*, *ājñā* wheels, and at the forehead, the parting of the hair (*sīmanta*), and the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), facing oneself, starting from their own tips...
One should mentally meditate upon the three previously mentioned seed-syllables in a clockwise sequence.
(p. 60) Now, the placement of the five wombs (*pañcayoninyāsa*):
on the head—*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ namaḥ*.
In the secret place—4 *hasakahalahrīṃ* namaḥ;
in the heart—4 *sakalahrīṃ* namaḥ; in the right eye—4 *ka e ī la hrīṃ* namaḥ.
To the left eye: 4 *hasakahalahrīṃ* namaḥ; to the forehead: 4 *sakalahrīṃ* namaḥ;
to the right ear: 4 *ka e ī la hrīṃ* namaḥ.
In the left ear—4 *hasakahalahrīṃ* namaḥ;
in the mouth—4 *sakalahrīṃ* namaḥ; in the right arm—4 *ka e ī la hrīṃ* namaḥ.
On the left arm—4 *hasakahalahrīṃ* namaḥ;
on the back—4 *sakalahrīṃ* namaḥ; on the right knee—*ka e ī la hrīṃ* namaḥ.
On the left knee: *4 hasakahalahrīṃ namaḥ*;
at the navel: *4 sakalahrīṃ namaḥ*. This is the placement of the five *yoni*s (*pañcayoninyāsa*). Now follows the placement of the four principles (*catustattvanyāsa*):
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ namaḥ. Salutation to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades the *ātmatattva*.
One should cause [the mantra] to pervade from the feet to the navel and from the navel to the feet.
4. Klīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ namaḥ. Salutation to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades the *vidyātattva*. [One should cause it to pervade] from the navel to the throat.
One should pervade [the body] from the throat down to the navel.
With "sauḥ sakalahrīṃ namaḥ śivatattvavyāpikāyai śrīmahātripurasundaryai namaḥ," one should pervade from the throat to the top of the head and from the top of the head back to the throat.

4. Aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ klīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ sauḥ sakalahrīṃ. Salutation to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades all principles (*tattva*); one should cause [the mantra] to pervade from the feet to the end of the hair and from the hair to the end of the feet. This is the *catustattvanyāsa*.
Now, the *śṛṅkhalānyāsa*:
One should touch the external limbs; thus ends the internal placement of the nine-yoni (*navayoninyāsa*).
Now, O Great Goddess, I shall describe the supreme placement of the *Śrīvidyā*.
One should contemplate the complete Vidyā, glowing with a reddish luster, within the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).

One should meditate upon her who flows with nectar, consisting of sixteen syllables, and bestows great good fortune. Then, O Dear One, one should brandish the Staff of Good Fortune at the left shoulder and place the Mudrā that seizes the tongues of enemies at the base of the foot.
Thinking, "I am the creator of the three worlds," one should apply the *tilaka*.
Thus one should apply the *mahāsaubhāgya* [mantra].
Again, with the *sampūrṇā* [mudrā], one should then place it upon the body from the throat upwards; again, with the *sampūrṇā*, as an encircling [gesture] upon the body.

One should perform the placement [of mantras] starting from *mala* and ending with *pāda*. At the conclusion of the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*), having cast the *yonimudrā* into the mouth and offered salutation, this is the *trilokakṣobhakanyāsa*.
This placement, which is the perfect form of Śrīvidyā, increases good fortune.
O beloved, having rotated it around the ring finger, one should carry it all the way to the top of the head.
O Goddess, one should cast [the mantra] into the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra) and then place it on the wrist;
the wise one, while recollecting the sixteen-syllable mantra, should apply it to the forehead with the ring fingers.
O Goddess of the Gods, this placement (nyāsa) called Sammohana causes agitation;
while meditating on the three worlds as crimson, one should remember Śrīvidyā within the mind.
(p. 62) *Truṭi* is written at the tip of the leaf.

Now follows the *saṃhāranyāsa*, which is the prerogative of renunciants (*sannyāsins*): *Śrīṃ* on the feet; *Hrīṃ* on the shanks; *Klīṃ* on the knees; *Aiṃ* on the hips; *Sauḥ* on the *liṅga*; *Oṃ* on the back; *Hrīṃ* on the navel; *Śrīṃ* on the sides; *Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ* on the breasts.

*Hasakahalahrīṃ* on the two shoulders; *sakalahrīṃ* on the two ears; *sauḥ* in the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*); *aiṃ* on the face; *klīṃ* on the eyes; *hrīṃ* on the generative organ; *śrīṃ* on the regions of the ears. One should contemplate: "I am the destroyer of all. This is the *saṃhāranyāsa*. *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ e aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ rablūṃ*
*Vaśinīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ*—on the head;
4 *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ kalahrīṃ*, *Kāmeśvarīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ*—on the forehead;
4 *caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ nklīṃ*, *Bhedinīvāgdevatāyai namaḥ*—on the mouth.
4 ṬAṂ ṬHAṂ ḌAṂ ḌHAṂ ṆAṂ YLŪṂ, obeisance to Vimalā-Vāgdevatā—at the throat; 4 TAṂ THAṂ DAṂ DHAṂ NAṂ JMRĪṂ, obeisance to Aruṇā-Vāgdevatā—at the heart;
4 PAṂ PHAṂ BAṂ BHAṂ MAṂ, obeisance to Jayinī-Vāgdevatā—at the navel.
4 yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ jhmryū, salutation to Sarveśvarī Vāgdevatā—at the *ādhāra*;
4 śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ kṣmrīṃ, salutation to Kaulinī Vāgdevatā—at the *vyūhaka*, from the root [cakra] to the tips of the feet.
Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the eight goddesses of speech.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*;
4 hasakahalahrīṃ to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*; 4 sakalahrīṃ to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*.
4 *ka e ī la hrīṃ* to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*; 4 *hasakahalahrīṃ* to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*;
4 *sakalahrīṃ* to the palms of the hands, *namaḥ*. In this manner [the assignment] for the heart and other limbs is performed. This is the six-limbed ritual (*kara-ṣaḍaṅga*).

Now, the sixfold placement (*ṣoḍhānyāsa*): *Oṃ*, for this sixfold placement beginning with Gaṇeśa, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*), the venerable Mātṛkā-sundarī is the deity (*devatā*),
and its application (*viniyoga*) is in the placement as a limb of Śrīvidyā.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ āṃ aiṃ, *namaḥ* to the heart;
4 iṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ īṃ klīṃ, *svāhā* to the head;
4 uṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ūṃ sauḥ, *vaṣaṭ* to the crest-lock.

4 *eṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ aiṃ sauḥ* for the armor (*kavaca*), *huṃ*; 4 *oṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ auṃ klīṃ* for the three eyes (*netratraya*), *vauṣaṭ*; 4 *aṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ aḥ aiṃ* for the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*.
She possesses the luster of a thousand rising suns, with full and elevated breasts;
she is adorned with red garlands, garments, ointments, and red ornaments.
Her four hands shine with a noose, a goad, a bow, and an arrow;
she has three red eyes, and her beauty is illuminated by a golden crown.
I bow to the Goddess, the supreme Mātṛkā Sundarī, who consists of the sacred seats (pīṭha), and who takes the form of Gaṇeśa, the planets, the lunar mansions, the Yoginīs, and the zodiac signs.

Thus, having meditated upon the collective form, [of this Śrī Gaṇeśanyāsa]: Gaṇaka is the seer (ṛṣi), Nicṛdgāyatrī is the meter (chandas), the deity is Gaṇapati, and the application (viniyoga) is in the Gaṇeśanyāsa.
Gāṃ, gīṃ—thus are the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga).
Resembling the rising sun, with the faces of elephants and three eyes,
holding nooses, goads, gestures of granting boons and protection, and endowed with spears;
they are the color of vermilion and adorned with all ornaments.
Having meditated thus: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gaṃ aṃ* to Vighneśvara, to Śrī, *namaḥ*—on the head;
*āṃ* to Vighnarāja, to Hrī, *namaḥ*—on the face; *iṃ* to Vināyaka, to Tuṣṭi, *namaḥ*—on the right eye.
5 *Īṃ* to Śivottama, to Peace (*śānti*), obeisance—on the left eye;
5 *Uṃ* to Vighnahṛt, to Nourishment (*puṣṭi*), obeisance—on the right ear; 5 *Ūṃ* to Vighnakartṛ, to Sarasvatī, obeisance—on the left ear.
5 *ṛṃ* obeisance to Vighnarāja and Rati—at the right nostril; 5 *ṝṃ* obeisance to Gaṇanātha and Medhā—at the left nostril;
5 *ḷṃ* obeisance to Ekadanta and Kānti—at the right cheek.
5 ḶṂ, salutation to the two-tusked one, the passionate one—on the left cheek;
5 EṂ, salutation to the elephant-faced one, the deluding one—on the upper lip;
5 AIṂ, salutation to the stainless one, the matted hair—on the lower lip.
(p. 66) 5 Oṃ, obeisance to Kapardin and Tībrā—on the upper row of teeth; 5 Auṃ, obeisance to Dīrghavaktra and Jvālinī—on the lower row of teeth;
5 Aṃ, obeisance to Śaṅkukarṇa and Nandā—on the head.
5 Aḥ, salutation to Vṛṣadhvaja and Surasā—at the throat;
5 Kaṃ, salutation to Gaṇanātha and Kāmarūpiṇī—at the base of the right arm;
5 Khaṃ, salutation to Gajendra and Śubhrā—at the elbow.
5 Gaṃ, obeisance to Śūrpakarṇa and Jayinī—at the wrist; 5 Ghaṃ, obeisance to Trinetra and Satyā—at the base of the fingers;
5 Ṅaṃ, obeisance to Lambodara and Vighneśī—at the tips of the fingers.
5 CAṂ, salutation to Mahānāda, who is Surūpinī—on the root of the left arm; 5 CHAṂ, salutation to Caturmūrti, who is Kāmadā—on the elbow;
5 JAṂ, salutation to Sadāśiva, who is Madavihvalā—on the wrist.
5 *Jhaṃ* Amodāya Vikaṭāyai namaḥ—at the base of the fingers;
5 *Ñaṃ* Durmukhāya Ghūrṇāyai namaḥ—at the tips of the fingers;
5 *Ṭaṃ* Sumukhāya Bhūtyai namaḥ—at the base of the right foot.
5 Ṭhaṃ, obeisance to Pramoda, the Bhūmi—on the knee; 5 Ḍaṃ, obeisance to Ekapāda, the Mati—on the ankle;
5 Ḍhaṃ, obeisance to Dvijihva, the Ramā—on the base of the toes.
5 ṇaṃ śūrāya mānuṣyai namaḥ—at the tips of the fingers; 5 taṃ vīrāya makaradhvajāyai namaḥ—at the base of the left foot;
5 thaṃ ṣaṇmukhāya vikarṇāyai namaḥ—at the knees.
5 *daṃ* to Varada-Bhṛkuṭī, salutation—at the ankles; 5 *dhaṃ* to Vāmadeva-Lajjā, at the base of the fingers;
5 *naṃ* to Vakratuṇḍa-Dīrghaghoṇā, salutation—at the tips of the fingers.
5 *paṃ* dviraṇḍāya dhanurdharāyai namaḥ—on the right side;
5 *phaṃ* senānye yāminyai namaḥ—on the left side;
5 *baṃ* grāmaṇyai rātryai namaḥ—on the back.
5 BHAṂ, obeisance to Mattā and Candrikā—at the navel;
(p. 67) 5 MAṂ, obeisance to Vimattā and Śaśiprabhā—at the belly; 5 YAṂ, obeisance to Mattavāhana and Lolā—at the heart.
5 RAṂ JAṬINE CAPALĀYAI NAMAḤ—on the shoulders;
5 LAṂ MUṆḌINE RDDHYAI NAMAḤ—on the hump of the back;
5 VAṂ KHAḌGINE DURBHAGĀYAI NAMAḤ—on the armpits.
5 Śaṃ Vareṇyāya Subhagāyai Namaḥ—from the heart to the right hand; 5 Ṣaṃ Vṛṣakatava Śivāya Namaḥ—from the heart to the left hand;
5 Saṃ Bhakṣapriyāya Durdharāyai Namaḥ—from the heart to the right foot.
5 *haṃ* gaṇapāya guhakāyai namaḥ—from the heart to the end of the left foot;
5 *laṃ* meghanādāya kālikāyai namaḥ—in the abdomen; 5 *kṣaṃ* gaṇeśvarāya analajihvāyai namaḥ—as the all-pervading (*vyāpaka*).
Thus ends the Gaṇeśanyāsa.
Now, the placement of the *grahas*:
one should contemplate [them] as red, white, likewise red, dark-blue, yellow, pale-white,
smoke-colored-black, black-smoke-colored, and smoky-grey.
[He saw] those whose chief was Ravi, who could assume any form at will, adorned with all ornaments,
with their left hands resting on her thighs and their right hands granting boons.
The Śaktis should also be known in the same way, with hands granting boons and fearlessness.
Having meditated thus, one should perform the nyāsa:
oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ.
*Sūryāya reṇukāmbāyai namaḥ*—at the base of the heart; *4 yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ candrāya amṛtāmbāyai namaḥ*—between the eyebrows;
*4 kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ maṅgalāya dharmāmbāyai namaḥ*—in the eyes.
4 caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ, salutation to Budha and Jñānarūpāmbā—on the heart;
4 ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ, salutation to Bṛhaspati and Yaśasvinyambā—at the throat;
4 taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ, salutation to Śukra and Śākambharī—in the center of the heart.
4 *paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ* to Śanaiścara and Śakti-ambā, salutation—at the navel;
4 *śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ* to Rāhu and Kṛṣṇā-ambā, salutation—at the mouth;
4 *laṃ kṣaṃ* to Ketu and Dhūmrā-ambā, salutation—at the feet. Thus ends the placement of the planets (*grahanyāsa*).
Now, the ritual placement of the constellations (*nakṣatran nyāsa*):
Resembling the blazing fire of time (*kālāgni*), adorned with all ornaments,
with hands in the gesture of salutation, the constellations headed by Aśvinī have hands granting boons and fearlessness.
Having meditated thus, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*): *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ āṃ aśvinyai namaḥ*—on the forehead;
*iṃ bharaṇyai namaḥ*—on the right eye.
4 Īṃ Ūṃ Kṛttikāyai namaḥ—on the left eye; 4 Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Rohiṇyai namaḥ—on the right ear;
4 Eṃ Mṛgaśīrṣāya namaḥ—on the left ear.
4 Aiṃ, obeisance to Ārdrā—on the right nostril; 4 Oṃ Auṃ, obeisance to Punarvasu—on the left nostril;
4 Kaṃ, obeisance to Puṣya—at the throat.
4 khaṃ gaṃ, obeisance to Āśleṣā—on the right shoulder; 4 ghaṃ ṅaṃ, obeisance to Maghā—on the left shoulder;
4 caṃ, obeisance to Pūrvāphālgunī—on the right elbow.
4 chaṃ jaṃ, salutation to Uttarāphālgunī—at the left elbow; 4 jhaṃ ñaṃ, salutation to Hastā—at the right wrist;
4 ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ, salutation to Citrā—at the left wrist.
4 Ḍaṃ, salutation to Svātī—on the right hand; 4 Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ, salutation to Viśākhā—on the left hand;
4 Taṃ Thaṃ Daṃ, salutation to Anurādhā—at the navel.
4 *dhaṃ* Jyeṣṭhāyai namaḥ—on the right hip; 4 *naṃ paṃ phaṃ* Mūlāyai namaḥ—on the left hip;
4 *baṃ* Pūrvāṣāḍhāyai namaḥ—on the right thigh.
4 Bhaṃ, salutation to Uttarāṣāḍhā—on the left thigh; 4 Maṃ, salutation to Śravaṇā—on the right knee;
4 Yaṃ Raṃ, salutation to Dhaniṣṭhā—on the left knee.
4 *laṃ* śatabhiṣāyai namaḥ—on the right calf; 4 *vaṃ śaṃ* pūrvābhādrapadāyai namaḥ—on the left calf;
4 *ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ* uttarābhādrapadāyai namaḥ—on the right foot.
4. *Laṃ kṣaṃ aṃ aḥ*, salutation to Revatī—on the left foot.
This is the Nakṣatra-nyāsa. Now follows the Yoginī-nyāsa:
One should contemplate them as white, whitish-red, tawny, variegated, and yellow;
they have four arms, faces that are even, and are adorned with all ornaments.
Having meditated thus, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*):
*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ḍāṃ ḍīṃ ḍamalavarayūṃ ḍākinyai namaḥ; aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ yaṃ rakṣa rakṣa tvagātmane namaḥ*—at the throat.
4 *rāṃ rīṃ ramalavarayuṃ rākinyai namaḥ* (p. 70); *kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ raṃ rakṣa rakṣa asṛgātmane namaḥ*—in the heart;
4 *lāṃ līṃ lamalavarayūṃ lākinyai namaḥ*; *ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ*.
*Laṃ* rakṣa rakṣa *māṃsātmane namaḥ*— in Maṇipūra;
*kāṃ kīṃ kamalavarayūṃ kākinyai namaḥ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ rakṣa rakṣa medātmane namaḥ*— in Svādhiṣṭhāna.

4 Śāṃ Śīṃ Śamalavarayūṃ, obeisance to Śākinī; Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ Śaṃ, protect, protect! Obeisance to the self of bone—at the *mūlādhāra*. 4 Hāṃ Hīṃ Hamalavarayūṃ, obeisance to Hākinī; Haṃ Kṣaṃ Ṣaṃ, protect, protect! Obeisance to the self of marrow—[at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*].

4 daṃ, obeisance to the goddess Sarvamaṅgalakāriṇī; 4 dhaṃ, obeisance to the goddess Sarvakāmapradā;
