4 PAṂ, obeisance to the goddess Sarvamṛtyupraśamanī; 4 PHAṂ, obeisance to the goddess Sarvavighnanivāriṇī;
4 BAṂ, obeisance to the goddess Sarvāṅgasundarī.
4 Bhaṃ, obeisance to the Goddess Sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī. 4 Hsaiṃ Hsklīṃ Hsauṃ, obeisance to Tripurāśrīcakreśvarī.
4 Saḥ, one should display the Sarvonmādinī mudrā.
At the *ājñācakra* between the eyebrows: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ maṃ* obeisance to the goddess Sarvajñā;
4 *yaṃ* obeisance to the goddess Sarvaśakti; 4 *raṃ* obeisance to the goddess Sarvaiśvaryapradāyinī.
4 Laṃ, obeisance to the Goddess whose nature is all-knowing wisdom; 4 Vaṃ, obeisance to the Goddess who destroys all diseases;
4 Śaṃ, obeisance to the Goddess whose essential form is the support of all.
4 ṢAṂ, obeisance to the Goddess Sarvapāpaharā; 4 SAṂ, obeisance to the Goddess Sarvānandamayī;
4 HAṂ, obeisance to the Goddess Sarvarakṣāsvarūpiṇī.
4 KṢAṂ, obeisance to the Goddess who bestows all desired fruits.
4 HRĪṂ KLĪṂ BLEṂ, obeisance to Tripuramālinī, the Mistress of the Cakra.
4 KROṂ, one should display the Mahāṅkuśa mudrā.
On the forehead: Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ Rablūṃ, obeisance to Vaśinī Vāgdevatā; 4 Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Kalahrīṃ, obeisance to Kāmeśvarī Vāgdevatā.
4 caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ nblīṃ, obeisance to Modinī, the goddess of speech; 4 ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ ylūṃ, obeisance to Vimalā, the goddess of speech;
4 taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ jmrīṃ, obeisance to Aruṇā, the goddess of speech.
4 paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ hslvyūṃ, obeisance to Jayanī Vāgdevatā;
4 yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ jhmryūṃ, obeisance to Sarveśvarī Vāgdevatā; 4 śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ kṣmrīṃ, obeisance to Kaulinī Vāgdevatā.
4 hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ, obeisance to Tripurāsiddhācakreśvarī.
4 hskhphreṃ, one should display the Sarvakhecarīmudrā.
At the hair-parting (sīmanta): 4 hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ strīṃ, obeisance to the deity Jṛmbhaṇakāmeśvarabāṇa.
4 drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ, obeisance to the arrow-deity Jṛmbhaṇakāmeśvarī;
4 yaṃ, obeisance to the bow-deity Mohanakāmeśvara;
4 dhaṃ, obeisance to the bow-deity Mohanakāmeśvarī.
4 Āṃ, obeisance to the deity of the noose of Vaśaṅkara Kāmeśvara; 4 Hrīṃ, obeisance to the deity of the noose of Vaśaṅkarī Kāmeśvarī;
4 Kroṃ, obeisance to the deity of the goad of Stambhana Kāmeśvara.
4. *Kroṃ*, obeisance to the deity Aṅkuśa, the Mistress of Desire who paralyzes;
*Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ*, *aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ*, *ka e ī la hrīṃ*, obeisance to Kāmeśvarī, the Śakti of Rudra.
4 kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ hasakahalahrīṃ, obeisance to Vajreśvarī, the power of Viṣṇu;
4 thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ sakalahrīṃ.
Salutation to Bhagamālinī, the power of Brahmā;
4 hsraiṃ hsklīṃ hsrauṃḥ, salutation to Tripurāmbā, the Mistress of the Cakra.
4 hsauṃ, one should display the seed-syllable mudrā of all.
In the thousand-petaled lotus at the aperture of Brahma (*brahmarandhra*): *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ haṃ kṣaṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ sakalahrīṃ mahātripurasundaryai namaḥ*;
[four times] *ka e ī la hrīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ sakalahrīṃ śrīmahātripurasundarīcakreśvaryai namaḥ*.
4 Aiṃ—One should display the Sarvayonimudrā. This concludes the Cakranyāsa. Now follows the Sthitinyāsa:
Śrīṃ—at the two thumbs.
Hrīṃ—on the two index fingers; Klīṃ—on the two middle fingers;
Aiṃ—on the two ring fingers.
Sauḥ—on the two little fingers; uṃ—in the aperture of Brahmā;
hrīṃ—in the mouth.
Śrīṃ—on the heart;
Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ Namaḥ—from the navel to the ends of the feet;
Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Namaḥ—from the throat to the navel.
*Sakalahrīṃ namaḥ*—from the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) down to the throat;
*sauḥ*—on the two thumbs;
*aiṃ*—on the two index fingers.
Klīṃ on the two middle fingers, Hrīṃ on the two ring fingers, and Śrīṃ on the two little fingers.
At the conclusion of the worship of Subhagā, the sequence is withdrawal, emanation, and maintenance. This is the *sthitinyāsa* (placement of maintenance).
Thereafter, one should perform the *sṛṣṭinyāsa* (placement of emanation), which bestows all spiritual accomplishments (*siddhis*).
*Śrīṃ*—in the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).
Hrīṃ on the forehead;
Klīṃ on the two eyes; Aiṃ on the two ears.
Sauḥ—at the nose;
Ūṃ—at the two lips; Hrīṃ—at the rows of teeth.
Śrīṃ—on the tongue; Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ—in the pit of the stomach; Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ—on the back.
*Sakalahrīṃ*—on all limbs;
*sauḥ*—in the heart;
*aiṃ*—on the breasts.
*klīṃ*—in the belly; *hrīṃ*—in the generative organ;
*śrīṃ*—pervasive.

The practitioner of mantra should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the syllables of the Śrīvidyā upon the Goddess for the sake of all prosperity. Thus ends the *sṛṣṭinyāsa*. One should pervade [the body] three times with the root mantra.
Having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) over all the limbs three times with the root mantra, it is likewise stated in the Tantra:
"Thereafter, one should perform the Tripurā-nyāsa for the attainment of all desires and goals."
By the mere knowledge of this, a person becomes Sadāśiva.
Now, the placement of Tripurā (Tripurānyāsa):
Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ, salutation to Kāminī Tripurā—on the head;
4 Āṃ, salutation to Mālinī Tripurā—on the perimeter of the mouth.
4 *Iṃ* Madanātripurāyai namaḥ—on the right eye; 4 *Īṃ* Unmādinītripurāyai namaḥ—on the left eye;
(p. 86) 4 *Uṃ* Drāviṇītripurāyai namaḥ—on the right ear.
4 ŪṂ Khecarītripurāyai namaḥ—on the left ear; 4 ṚṂ Ghaṭikātripurāyai namaḥ—on the right nostril; 4 ṜṂ Kulāvalītripurāyai namaḥ—on the left nostril.
4 Ḷṃ, salutation to Kledinī Tripurā—on the right cheek; 4 Ḹṃ, salutation to Śivadūtī Tripurā—on the left cheek;
4 Eṃ, salutation to Subhagā Tripurā—on the upper lip.
4 Aiṃ Bhagāvahā Tripurāyai namaḥ—on the lower lip;
4 Oṃ Vidyeśvarī Tripurāyai namaḥ—on the upper row of teeth; 4 Auṃ Mahālakṣmī Tripurāyai namaḥ—on the lower row of teeth.
4 Aṃ, obeisance to Kaulinī Tripurā—at the palate; 4 Aḥ, obeisance to Kāmeśvarī Tripurā—at the mouth; 4 Kaṃ, obeisance to Kulamālinī Tripurā—at the base of the right arm.
4 Khaṃ, obeisance to Vyāpinī Tripurā—at the elbow;
4 Gaṃ, obeisance to Subhagā Tripurā—at the wrist;
4 Ghaṃ, obeisance to Vāgeśvarī Tripurā—at the base of the fingers.
4 Ṅaṃ Kālikātripurāyai namaḥ—on the tips of the fingers; 4 Caṃ Piṅgalātripurāyai namaḥ—at the base of the left arm;
4 Chaṃ Bhagasarpiṇītripurāyai namaḥ—at the elbow.
4 JAṂ, salutation to Sundarī Tripurā—at the wrist; 4 JHAṂ, salutation to Nīlapatākā Tripurā—at the base of the fingers;
4 ÑAṂ, salutation to Siddheśvarī Tripurā—at the tips of the fingers.
4 *Ṭaṃ* Mahāsiddheśvarī Tripurā, salutation—at the root of the right foot; 4 *Ṭhaṃ* Amoghā Tripurā, salutation—at the two knees; 4 *Ḍaṃ* Ratnamālā Tripurā, salutation—at the [shanks].
4 ḍhaṃ maṅgalātripurāyai namaḥ—at the base of the fingers;
(p. 87) 4 ṇaṃ bhagamālinītripurāyai namaḥ—at the tips of the fingers;
4 taṃ raudrītripurāyai namaḥ—at the base of the left foot.
4 THAṂ Yogeśvarītripurāyai namaḥ—at the knees;
4 DAṂ Ambikātripurāyai namaḥ—at the ankles;
4 DHAṂ Aṭṭahāsātripurāyai namaḥ—at the bases of the toes.
4 Naṃ Vyomavyāpinītripurāyai namaḥ—on the tips of the fingers;
4 Paṃ Vajreśvarītripurāyai namaḥ—on the right side;
4 Phaṃ Kṣobhiṇītripurāyai namaḥ—on the left side.
4 BAṂ Śāmbhavītripurāyai namaḥ—on the back; 4 BHAṂ Aṅganānaṅgātripurāyai namaḥ—on the navel;
4 MAṂ Lokeśvarītripurāyai namaḥ—on the abdomen.
4 *yaṃ* raktātripurāyai namaḥ—on the heart; 4 *raṃ* susthātripurāyai namaḥ—on the right shoulder; 4 *laṃ* śuklātripurāyai namaḥ—on the left shoulder.
4 Vaṃ, obeisance to Aparājitātripurā—on the back of the neck; 4 Śaṃ, obeisance to Śarvātripurā—on the right shoulder; 4 Ṣaṃ, obeisance to Vimalātripurā—on the left shoulder.
4 Saṃ, obeisance to Aghorā Tripurā—up to the right hand and foot; 4 Haṃ, obeisance to Bhairavī Tripurā—up to the left hand and foot;
4 Laṃ, obeisance to Amoghā Tripurā—at the belly and face.

4 *KṢAṂ* salutations to Tripurā, the accomplisher of all; this is the pervasive [mantra]. Thus, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of each of the fifty Tripurās in the locations of the Mātṛkās.
*Oṃ*, salutations to the form of the venerable Guru, O Heramba.
Now, the placement of saffron encapsulated by the *parā* [mantra]:

*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ laṃ* to Indra, lord of the gods, who holds a thunderbolt in his hand, whose vehicle is Airāvata, and who is accompanied by the retinue of Tripurasundarī; *namaḥ sauḥ*—on both big toes.

4 Sauḥ Raṃ, salutation to Agni, the lord of splendor, who holds a spear in his hand, whose vehicle is a ram, and who is accompanied by Tripurasundarī and her retinue— Sauḥ— at the right knee. 4 Sauḥ Yaṃ, salutation to Yama, the lord of spirits, who holds a staff in his hand, whose vehicle is a buffalo, and who is accompanied by Śrī Tripurasundarī and her retinue.

On the right side: 4 *sauḥ* *kṣaṃ* obeisance to Nirṛti, the lord of the Rākṣasas, who holds a sword in his hand, whose vehicle is a corpse, and who is accompanied by the retinue of Śrī Tripurasundarī;
*sauḥ*—on the right shoulder.
4 *sauḥ* vaṃ, obeisance to Varuṇa, lord of the waters, who holds a noose in his hand, whose vehicle is a water-bearer, together with Śrī Tripurasundarī and her retinue—
*sauḥ* on the head; 4 *sauḥ* yaṃ, obeisance to Vāyu, lord of the vital breaths, who holds a goad in his hand, whose vehicle is the wind, together with Śrī Tripurasundarī and her retinue.
Namaḥ sauḥ— on the left shoulder; 4 sauḥ kuṃ, obeisance to Kubera, who holds a mace in his hand, whose vehicle is a palanquin, the lord of the Yakṣas, together with the retinue of Śrī Tripurasundarī,
sauḥ— on the left side.

4 *sauḥ* *haṃ*, obeisance to Īśāna, the lord of space (*viyat*), who holds a trident in his hand, whose vehicle is a bull, and who is accompanied by Śrī Tripurasundarī and her retinue; *sauḥ*—on the left knee.
4 *sauḥ* *ūṃ*, obeisance to Brahmā, the lord of the worlds, who holds a lotus in his hand, whose vehicle is a swan, and who is accompanied by Śrī Tripurasundarī and her retinue.
Sauḥ—on the crown;
4 Sauḥ Vaṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇu, the lord of the netherworld (pātāla), who holds a discus in his hand, whose vehicle is Garuḍa, together with the retinue of Śrī Tripurasundarī;
Sauḥ—at the foundation (ādhāra).
Regarding this, the Sūtra states:
"On the two big toes, on the sides of the knees, and on the tops of the heads;
on the left shoulder, and on the sides and knees—on these bases, one should place the World-Protectors."
Thus ends the *kuṅkumanyāsa*.
Salutations to the illustrious Gaṇeśa! O Heramba, be gracious!
One should fashion the limbs of the dissolution (*layāṅga*) upon the body of the Supreme Goddess.
One should meditate upon the one who is free from all affliction, who deludes the three worlds. || 1 ||
Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ!
[I bow to] the Supreme Mistress, who possesses the luster of a thousand rising suns and the radiance of the pomegranate flower, and who is the sovereign of all sixfold worldly activities. (2)
The Supreme Goddess, who resembles the hibiscus flower, possesses the luster of a ruby gem;
she has the brilliance of a mass of lightning and the hue of molten gold.
Her two lotus-feet, adorned with anklets fashioned from priceless jewels, are graced by the shape of red lotus petals.
Adorned with the radiant splendor of jewels set in her anklets, her thighs were as delicate and soft as the graceful trunk of a plantain tree. (5)
Adorned with shimmering red garments upon her rounded hips,
she was graced by the playful tinkling of the *maṇikya* bells fastened to her girdle.
Her waist was unmarked [by folds], beautified by a deep lotus-like navel, and endowed with great breasts like fruits upon the creeper of the line of body hair. || 7 ||
Well-proportioned, adorned with a pair of firm and lofty breasts,
and resplendent with the weight of a magnificent necklace of priceless pearls.
Her neck-ornament was the finest of jewels, shining with the luster of the nine gems;
she was enchanting with ear-ornaments and beautiful with lovely cheeks.
Resembling the rising sun, with the radiance of her face enhanced by her earrings,
she had a face like the full moon, a lotus-like countenance, and a nose as straight as the sky.
She possessed beautiful eyebrows like the quivering bow of Love, lotus-like eyes,
and was marked by a tilaka of excellent gems shining upon her forehead.
She whose breast-region is adorned with bells set in pearls and rubies,
who wears a crown shimmering with a crescent moon, and who possesses three eyes;
she whose four creeper-like arms are radiant with coral vines.
[She is] four-armed, holding a sugarcane bow, a flower-arrow, a noose, and a goad. ||13||
The Mother who consists of all the gods, beautiful with every auspiciousness,
divine and composed of all sacred fords, the fulfiller of all desires.
The Goddess who consists of all fields, who is beautiful as the abode of all, who is composed of all bliss, who is the abyss of knowledge, and who is the supreme bestower of siddhis. || 15 ||
She was adorned with red flowers and graced by red ornaments;
her lotus-feet were illuminated by the crest-jewels from the heads of Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
Meditating thus upon the Great Goddess who dwells in the Kadamba forest,
he should place the Supreme Sovereign upon the lap of Śiva, the Lord of Desire.
O Dear One, accompanied by the invocation-formula and a salutation,
one should properly present perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains, and other offerings to the Goddess.
Having worshipped the Supreme Deity with the sixteen services (*upacāra*) and having meditated thus,
one should display the fifteen mudrās.
Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
One should perform the Ūrdhvāmnāya, which is difficult to attain even for Brahmā and the other gods,
as well as the supreme placement (paranyāsa) of the Śrīprāsāda and the Parāprāsāda itself.
Thereafter, one should perform the Mahāśaktinyāsa. Having thus performed the ritual bath at the sacred ford (tīrthasnāna), one should perform the Śaktinyāsa.
Now, the Mahāśaktinyāsa:
for this mantra of the venerable Mahāśaktinyāsa, the Seer (ṛṣi) is Ādiprakṛti, the metre (chandas) is Anuṣṭubh, the Deity (devatā) is the venerable Ādiśakti, and the seed-syllable is the Praṇava.

The seed-syllable is *ajapā-śakti*, and the *kīlaka* is *nāda*. The application (*viniyoga*) is for the purpose of attaining success through the grace of my venerable Guru-deity during the recitation (*japa*).
Having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) with the three *tāra*s and the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) beginning with the fingers, it is said in the *Śaktikulārṇava*:
the Śrī Devī said—
Now, therefore, O Lord of the Gods, I shall fully explain the deposition of the powers (śaktinyāsa),
by which, when applied to the body, a person becomes equal to Śakti herself.
By the mere act of placement (nyāsa), a divine body is produced;
when enraged, the yogin brings about even the downfall of the three worlds. || 2 ||
O Śaṅkara, a hero endowed with the deposition of power (śaktinyāsa), by means of this salutation, directly effects the shattering of stone images and the like. (3)
A triangle measuring one cubit (hasta) shall be the seat of the deposition of Śakti;
it should be constructed according to the prescribed ritual from wood dyed with red sandalwood.
A square, a hexagon, and above that a triangle—
this is declared to be the seat for the deposition of Śakti (śaktinyāsāsana), fashioned from red sandalwood.
If even sandalwood is unavailable, one should instead use a *tilaka*;
otherwise, for the ritual placement of power (*śaktinyāsa*), a great seat should be made from fine linen and similar materials.
May Jayā, Vijayā, Jayantī, Aparājitā, Ajitā, and Saṅgamārambhā—may these [goddesses] abide upon my seat. || 7 ||
One should worship one's own head in seven ways upon the body with red flowers, using one's own *karavīra* blossoms, or otherwise with saffron-colored *kesara* flowers.
Having thus performed the fumigation of the image upon his head, the worshiper,
having seated himself there, should become intent on meditation.
Facing north, the mantra-practitioner, adorned with red garments and ornaments, [should anoint himself] with red sandalwood, camphor, as well as vermilion and saffron. (10)
With his limbs smeared with red flowers and adorned with three garlands, the wise one [should remain thus], O Mahādeva; so it was spoken by Rudra. 11.
Then, once established in this state, the yogi becomes like Śaṅkara;
he perceives the Guru, whose nature is Śiva and Śakti, within the space of consciousness at the end of the twelve.
One should meditate upon the Supreme, consisting of pure light, for the attainment of the happiness of worldly enjoyment and liberation;
there is no protector equal to the Guru, and no deity higher than Śaṅkara.
There is no yoga higher than Kaula; there is no knowledge equal to Traipura;
there is no wisdom superior to initiation; and there is no happiness greater than peace.
There is no placement equal to Śakti, nor is there any knowledge equal to the Ṣoḍaśī.
Therefore, O Lord of the Gods, I shall now fully explain the placement of Śakti.
The placement of the *śakti* as well as the mantra should be performed with the seed-syllables of the names;
first the placement with the seed-syllables, and immediately after that with the names. 16.
The name should be in the place of the sprout, while the seed-syllable (*bīja*) is in the place of the seed;
for in this world, the attainment of fruit is seen to arise from the seed and the sprout. (17)
For instance: Aiṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Lady of the Triangle.
Having thus placed [the mantras] upon the support (ādhāra), one should place *hrāṃ hrīṃ hruṃ* in the womb (*yauni*),
*klāṃ klīṃ kluṃ* in the navel region, and *lhāṃ lhīṃ lhuṃ* on the feet after having placed them on the two arms.
One should assign *sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ* to the two cheeks, *hrāṃ hrīṃ hruṃ* to the two ears,
*drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ* to the two eyes, and *lāṃ līṃ lūṃ* to the two nostrils.

Placing *sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ* upon the chin, one should then place them upon the head. Form the seed-syllable *a* within the circle of the *haṃsa*; place all the phonemes within the body and the life-force. O God, dissolve that into where it is perceived—know that to be the sixfold *kāmakalā*.
Just as butter resides in milk and oil in sesame seeds,
so is the letter *a* proclaimed to reside within all the classes of consonants.
In this world, the letter *a* is said to be the Mātṛkā, the Mother of the Universe;
he who knows [the sequence] from the letter *a* to the letter *kṣa* is a true teacher (*deśika*).
The speech-illusion (*vāṅmāyā*) preceded by *kamalā* is proclaimed as all the mantras:
*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ namaḥ*—at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*);
*4 āṃ namaḥ*—at the palate (*tāluka*); *4 iṃ namaḥ*—at the nose (*nāsikā*).
4 *Īṃ* Namaḥ—to the *liṅga*; 4 *Uṃ* Namaḥ—to the *gudī*;
4 *Ūṃ* Namaḥ—to the back; 4 *Ṛṃ* Namaḥ—to the junction of the hips; 4 *Ṝṃ* Namaḥ—to between the testicles; 4 *Ḷṃ* Namaḥ—to the spinal column.
4 ḶṂ namaḥ to the uvula; 4 EṂ namaḥ to the upper row of teeth; 4 AIṂ namaḥ pervading all the limbs; 4 OṂ namaḥ to the cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa);
4 AUṂ namaḥ to the resonance (nāda); 4 AṂ namaḥ to the end of resonance (nādānta).

4 Aḥ Namaḥ—at the throat; 4 Kaṃ Namaḥ—in the heart-lotus; 4 Khaṃ Namaḥ—in the space of consciousness (cidākāśa); 4 Gaṃ Namaḥ—in the shanks; 4 Ghaṃ Namaḥ—in the breasts; 4 Ṅaṃ Namaḥ—at the tip of the nose.
4 Caṃ namaḥ — [at the heart], 4 Chaṃ namaḥ — on the left side of the abdomen, 4 Jaṃ namaḥ — on the right side of the abdomen, 4 Jhaṃ namaḥ — at the base of the feet,
4 Ñaṃ namaḥ — on the row of teeth, 4 Ṭaṃ namaḥ — on the tongue.
4 Ṭhaṃ namaḥ—in the middle of the face; 4 Ḍaṃ namaḥ—in the belly;
4 Ḍhaṃ namaḥ—in the joints of the bones; 4 Ṇaṃ namaḥ—in the chest; 4 Taṃ namaḥ—in the elbows; 4 Thaṃ namaḥ—in the cheeks.
4 daṃ namaḥ—at the root of the anus; 4 dhaṃ namaḥ—in the cavity of the ear; 4 naṃ namaḥ—in the two eyes; 4 paṃ namaḥ—in the upper lotus;
4 phaṃ namaḥ—in the middle lotus; 4 baṃ namaḥ—in the lower lotus.

4 BHAṂ namaḥ—to the pair of eyebrows; 4 MAṂ namaḥ—to the pair of cheeks; 4 YAṂ namaḥ—to the lunar orb; 4 RAṂ namaḥ—to the palate; 4 VAṂ namaḥ—to the tongue; 4 ŚAṂ namaḥ—to the center of the *śaṅkhinī* [channel].
4 ṢAṂ namaḥ—to the pores of the skin; 4 SAṂ namaḥ—to the seven joints;
4 HAṂ namaḥ—to the aperture of Brahmā; 4 LAṂ namaḥ—to all the limbs;
4 KṢAṂ namaḥ—to the fingers.

O Śaṅkara, the syllable Oṃ is Kuṇḍalī in the mouth, and Kuṇḍalī also resides in the Great Lineage (Mahākula); she should be visualized as dissolving [into the breath] through the utterance of the phonemes.
O Virūpākṣa, understand that while dissolving into the supportless Great State,
the immeasurable syllable *ka*, you should form the *kuṇḍalī*.
Having uttered the letters from 'a' to 'kṣa', one should place the *praṇava* (oṃ) in between.
Having thus deposited the seed-syllables, may the wielder of the trident protect, protect [me].
The lord of practitioners should say: "O Goddess Tripurā, bestower of joy upon the three worlds, protect me! O Sovereign of Tripura, protect me! (4)
Protect me, protect me, O Goddess! This body is mine.
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ! O Samayinī, beautiful with the bliss of wine, saluted by all gods and demons;
O Śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ, whose lotus-feet are worshipped by the garlands of crowns of serpent-kings; O Vikaṭadantī, who dwells within the mass of matted hair—[protect] my body.

Protect, protect, O Supreme Goddess! *Huṃ phaṭ svāhā*. *Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā*, *oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā*, *oṃ svaḥ svāhā*, *oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ svāhā*. O you adorned with a garland of ornaments of human entrails; O Great Kaulinī; O Proclaimer of Brahman; O you who cause the intoxication of great wealth; O Bestower of great enjoyment: make our body adamantine, *kuru kuru*! Slay the wicked, *han han*! Agitate the rulers of the earth!
"Agitate the enemy's army! Break, break! O Victor-maker, O you who move in your course, O Mistress of the Three Worlds!
*samalavarayarūṃ ramalavarayarūṃ yamalavarayarūṃ bhamalavarayarūṃ kṣamalavarayarūṃ*. O Śrī Bhairavī, be gracious, be gracious! Svāhā!"—having thus pervaded [the field].
This knowledge is a great knowledge, equal to the Samaya, most powerful,
possessing exceeding heroism, and having a radiance equal to ten million fierce suns.
O Supreme Goddess, O divine-limbed one who bestows enjoyment, may you protect my entire family and my own divine body, O noble lady.
Protect me, protect me, O Goddess, Supreme Sovereign; protect my body from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head, which is filled with the bliss of wine.
O Lord of the Gods, dissolving into the great reality which is without support,
one should then utter the syllable *huṃ* and worship upon the mandala of the earth.
At the conclusion of the worship, one should mutter the threefold *hrīṃ* mantra with the left hand;
thereafter, O Śaṅkara, [one should recite] the root mantras of the Tripura mantras.
The sequential recitation should be performed according to the procedure for the *mālāmantra*:
*aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ namaḥ tripurasundari hṛdayadevi śirodevi* and so forth, ending with *mahāśrīcakranagarasāmrājñī namaste namaste svāhā*. This is the *śuddhaśaktimālāmantra*.
Having consumed [the offering] with *kāmarāja*, [one recites]: *aiṃ bhagavati trikoṇāya namaḥ*.
The Great Goddess known as Tripurā bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation, especially among all philosophical systems and heretics.
The Great Goddess of divine form is the Supreme Sovereign everywhere;
now, therefore, I shall fully proclaim this supreme king of mantras.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ! O You who dwell in the midst of the sacred seats (pīṭhas) and secondary seats (upapīṭhas), in the sky, on the mountain, in the world, and in Gokula; Oṃ! O You who distinguish the Kula and Kaula traditions, O You who cause delight to the minds of all people! May Ekabhairavī accomplish for me a hundred desired tasks. May the Supreme Goddess purify [me], O You who rejoice in the circle of passion (madanamaṇḍala)!
O Supreme Goddess of the seventy million mantras! Svāhā!
This great mantra of Tripura is proclaimed by all yogis;
this mantra is the Goddess of the Lord of Gods, whose nature is the bliss of humanity.
She bestows the fruit of all accomplishments upon those who lie in the hero’s posture (vīraśāyana),
as well as the yogic attainments and whatever rites exist upon the earth.
O Śaṅkara, all those [rites] are accomplished by means of this mantra;
having pervaded [the body] with this as well, one should then place the other mantra.

Aiṃ! Salutations to the Blessed One, who dwells within the triangle, whose three syllables are manifold, adorned with the great *liṅga*, the cause of the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the three worlds; *sahala hrīṃ*, O giver of the bliss of Kandarpa... [O Goddess] whose lines are like the staff of Brahmā... [O Goddess] whose lotus is like lightning... adorned with the noose and the goad; speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Śrīṃ! O bestower of kingdoms upon fallen monarchs! Aiṃ! O You whose hands rest upon the granting of boons! O cause of joy for all people! Klīṃ Klīṃ!
Upon the seat of the seed-syllable of the King of Desire: *drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ*. Agitate, agitate, O Agitator! *hsrauḥ* *hsauḥ* *hsrā*. Burn, burn! *sauḥ*.

O Bestower of Fearlessness, four-armed, three-eyed, seated upon a corpse, adorned with a garland of skulls, having the crescent moon as your crest-jewel, O Tripurā, bestower of the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation! *aiṃ oṃ namaḥ siddhaṃ*.
Having recited the letters from *ā* to *kṣa*, and from *kṣa* to *ca*, [one recites]: *aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ*;
*kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ*.

Haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ kṣaṃ laṃ haṃ saṃ ṣaṃ śaṃ vaṃ laṃ raṃ yaṃ maṃ bhaṃ baṃ phaṃ paṃ naṃ dhaṃ daṃ thaṃ taṃ ṇaṃ ḍhaṃ ḍaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭaṃ ñaṃ jhaṃ jaṃ chaṃ caṃ ṅaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ khaṃ kaṃ aḥ aṃ auṃ oṃ aiṃ eṃ ḹṃ ḷṃ ṝṃ ṛṃ ūṃ uṃ īṃ iṃ āṃ aṃ haṃ syai namaḥ. Thus [it is said].
One should place [the mantra] pervading all limbs:
*oṃ aiṃ sarvabījamātaḥ śrīsamayini mama manorathaṃ dehi dehi svāhā śrīmantrarājāya namaḥ*— thus at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).
*Aiṃ śīṃ śīṃ sakalahrīṃ śrīṃ hsrauṃ tripurabhairavyai namaḥ*—at the center of the eyebrows.
*Aiṃ hrīṃ sauḥ aiṃ kroṃ tripurāyai namaḥ*—in the heart.
*Hsrauṃ klīṃ mohinyai namaḥ*—at the navel.
Aiṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ, salutation to Bhrāmarī Tripurā—on the *liṅga*.
Hsrauṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ preṃ, salutation to Trailokyasvāminī—at the *mūlādhāra*. Aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ, salutation to Caṇḍikā—at the hips.
"Oṃ Aiṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ, salutation to Tripurā, the dweller in the sprout of the skull"—thus [one should place this] on the two feet.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) in this manner, one should mutter "Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haṃ Saṃ" according to one's capacity. Then, endowed with meditation, one should contemplate these very white seeds as follows: "Aiṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ."
At the conclusion of the meditation, the practitioner of the Śrī Mahārudra mantra should recite one hundred verses.
O Tripurā, make my body consist of Śakti and Rudra;
O Goddess, Queen of Gods, Eternal One, grant me eternally that which I desire. (1)
May the goddess Maṅgalā protect the head, Kulasundarī the forehead,
Mahākālī the pair of eyes, and Kuṇḍalī the ears.
May Kapālī protect the ear-cavities, Kamalāvalī the two cheeks, Cāmuṇḍā the teeth, and Meruvāsinī the chin. || 3 ||
May Bhuvaneśvarī protect my space between the eyebrows and the region of the throat; may Sarasvatī protect my tongue, and she who dwells in the palate protect that cavity.
May Kamalā rest upon my shoulder; may Kulamālinī rest upon your shoulder. May Vināyakī reside in my belly; may Jayā and Nandā dwell upon my two breasts.
Mahālakṣmī resides in the pit of the throat, Caṇḍabhairavī in the heart,
Brahmāṇī in the region of the navel, and Jvālāvalī remains in the anus.
Liṅgaprabhā is in the Liṅga, Muṇḍinī is in the Medamaṇḍala;
Mahāvegā is in the Nāḍicakra, and Udbhaṭā is in the right hand.
Mahāmāyā resides in the left hand, and on the fingers of that hand;
Vaiṣṇavī, equipped with her discus weapon, should stand upon the left foot.
Likewise, on the right foot is Ekapātparameśvarī;
in the toes of the foot is Kauberī, and in the pores of the skin is Mahodbhavā.
Maṇḍalī is at the roots of the nails; Vārāhī is at the base of the penis;
Jālandharī is in the region of the water (the bladder); Kāmākṣī is situated in the middle of the organ of desire.
Udbhaṭā resides at the end of the penis, Jayā is located at the tip of the nose in the Pūrṇapīṭha,
the goddess Jayā is on the spinal column, and Carcikā is in the joints of the bones.
May the highly illustrious Carmadhārī always abide upon my penis;
and may Haṃsinī, ending with "namaḥ," always abide within my blood.
Māheśvarī and Kumārī—these two shall remain as my limbs;
the wise-eyed one [shall be] on the left and right, and [the others] at the joints of the hips.
May the Goddess protect my body, and may she who dwells in the lineage protect my head; likewise, may earth, water, fire, air, and space [protect me]. 14.
May she who is the mistress of the five elements always protect my family;
may Indrāṇī grant me sovereignty, and Prajāpati likewise grant me progeny. (15)
May Māyā always grant me wealth, grain, and likewise fame—in battle, in the royal court, amidst enemies, and in the great forest. || 16 ||
May the Great Goddess Raktanetrā fulfill my intention;
may Samayā protect the pledge, and Vidyā [protect] the Vidyā in the Kula tradition. 17.

O Lord of the World, you who bestow the fruits of worldly enjoyment and liberation upon practitioners, may you, the victorious one, grant me complete success and happiness throughout the three worlds. (18)
And may Ghaṇṭālī, the Great Vidyā, who is the leader of seven thousand million mantras, protect my throat. (19)
May that goddess Sureśvarī always grant me success;
may Ulkāmukhī reside in my mouth, and Mārjārī in the joints of my body.
May that Vidyā who is Bhadrakālī abide in my abode of Śiva;
and may the supreme Traipura-cakra, which is triangular and threefold in its circle, [abide there].
May that multiform Tripurā-śakti, previously described, who arises from Manmatha, abide eternally at my head and at its extremity. (22)
Overwhelmed by the bliss of wine, they agitate the entire world;
O divine yoginī, take up residence within my body now. (23)
Come, come, O Great Goddess, Siddhayoginī, to my family;
you who grant enjoyment to living beings for the purpose of slaying enemies. (24)
O Mahāyoginī, always make your abode in this body:
Māhendrī is at my crest, and Gaṇeśvarī is in the center of the yoni. 25.
May she who is renowned by the name Pretākṣī bring me well-being;
may the Ḍākinī in the eastern quarter grant me happiness. (26)
May Sākinī in the western quarter, Rākinī in the south, and Mahāmāyā in the left quarter grant me well-being. (27)
May Bhairavī always abide upon my head and protect me;
may the large-eyed goddess, stainless and free from all impurity, reside upon my forehead. (28)
May that Yoginī, the Great Yoga, Śrī, who is fashioned by Time as Kālī and is called Kālarātri, abide upon my head. (29)
May that Yoginī of great yoga, Śrī, the night-walker honored by kings, remain upon my head. (30)
May that Yoginī, the Great Yoga, Śrī, abide upon my head—she who is beautiful, with hair standing erect, wrathful, and with disheveled locks. (31)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is celebrated as Vīrā, the bestower of victory upon heroes, abide as Śrī upon my head. (32)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is known as Mālinī and who bears a garland of dots upon the tip of her nose, abide as Śrī upon my head. (33)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, whose body is formidable with a skeleton and who wears earrings made of the skull of the moon, abide as Śrī upon my head. (34)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, Śrī, Pracaṇḍā, Virūpākṣī, Virūpā, and Viśvarūpiṇī abide upon my head. (35)
That Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is called Khaṭvāṅgī and is worshipped by Rudra as Raudrī, let her abide upon my head as Śrī. (36)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is renowned as Śrī and is celebrated in the world as the Kulayoginī in the Kali age, abide upon my head. (37)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is called Pretākṣī and who roars with a multitude of hissing sounds, abide as Śrī upon my head. (38)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is proclaimed as Dhūmrākṣī in this Yoginīmata scripture, abide as Śrī upon my head. (39)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the Great Goddess who is described as being of terrible form in the Kula scriptures, abide upon my head as Śrī.
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the Śrī who is of universal form, especially bestow protection upon my head. (41)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is described in the Vaiṣṇava Āgama as O Mahādevī, "Fear is destroyed," abide upon my head as Śrī. 42.
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is endowed with a garland of skulls and who is the goddess bearing severed heads, remain as Śrī upon my head. (43)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the goddess named Bhairavī of terrifying prowess and formidable stride, abide as Śrī upon my head. (44)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who dwells in the banyan tree and is praised by the gods, remain as Śrī upon my head. (45)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is Bhīṣaṇā and Bhairavī, and who is praised by the eight Bhairavas, abide as Śrī upon my head. (46)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the goddess Śrī, whose eyes are like those of a ghost, who has long, drooping lips, and who is Mahāmāyā of great power, abide upon my head. (47)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the great power who wields the khaṭvāṅga and delivers one from the ocean of worldly existence, remain as Śrī upon my head. (48)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is proclaimed among all mantras as Mantravādinī, abide upon my head as Śrī. (49)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the Supreme Goddess who is called Kālaghnī at the end of the age, abide upon my head as Śrī. (p. 109) 50.
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, known as Gṛhiṇī by the gods, asuras, and great serpents, abide upon my head as Śrī. (51)
That Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is called Cakriṇī, one-footed and three-eyed, dwells as Śrī upon my head. (52)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the goddess who has arms reaching everywhere, the virtuous beloved of Viśvanātha, remain as Śrī upon my head. (53)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the Goddess of the World who is worshipped in all philosophical systems, abide as Śrī upon my head. (54)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is known in the scripture as Kaṇṭakī for the purpose of piercing the thorns [of obstacles], abide upon my head as Śrī. || 55 ||
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is called Kīlikī, seven-cubit tall and possessed of great strength, remain as Śrī upon my head. (56)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, who is called Mahāmārī when she is the Great Goddess in battle, abide as Śrī upon my head. (57)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, renowned as Yamadaṃṣṭrā and well-worshipped by gods and demons, abide upon my head as Śrī.
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the goddess Karālinī, who is Mahāmāyā of great power, abide as Śrī upon my head. (59)
May that Yoginī Mahāmāyā, the Great Goddess Lalitāmbā, the sole leader of all cakras, abide upon my head as Śrī. (60)
May that Yoginī of great yoga, Śrī, abide upon my head;
may Kaulinī abide at the tip of my nose, and likewise Madanākṣī in my mouth.
In the hair-follicles, on the cheeks, and in the palate are Āpadhāriṇī, Drāviṇī, Kṣobhiṇī, Stambhinī, and Mohinī. (62)
Raudrakarmā, Mahāghaṇṭā, Ḍāmarī, Tvaritā, Mati, Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Kulamātā, and Kākadṛṣṭi who looks downward. 63.
May Kapālakuṇḍalā, Kapālī, and Kulamālinī—the Goddess—protect my limbs; may Kulamālinī protect my head. May earth, water, fire, air, and space likewise [protect me].
May the Mistress of the Elements always protect my family within the five elements. || 65 ||
May Aindrī grant me sovereignty and progeny rich with offspring;
may Māyā grant me eternal wealth, grain, and great fame.
In battle, in the royal court, in the midst of enemies, or in great waters, may the Great Goddess, with blood-red eyes, accomplish my desire. (67)
One should guard the pledge through the pledge, and the vidyā through the vidyā, according to the family tradition;
O Lord of the World, may that [tradition] grant the fruit of accomplishment to practitioners. (68)
Dvijaṭī, Trijaṭī, Kandalī, Lalitākhilā, Gāyatrī, Ambikā, Tārā, Pārvatī, Kamalā, and Prabhā. || 69 ||
Modinī, Madanonmādā, Sundarī, Madanāturā, Viṣaṇā, Bhīṣaṇā by name, and Pretasiddhavibhīṣaṇī. (70)
Hunger, thirst, as well as sleep, luster, growth, and radiance; twilight, pleasure, and patience—these are recited incessantly. (p. 112) 71.
In the city, she is renowned as Suranāthā, the deity of the city;
she is indeed the village goddess, the presiding power, and is known as Pīṭheśvarī in every sacred seat (pīṭha). || 72 ||
The Kāverī, the Narmadā, the Gaṅgā, and the Yamunā,
as well as the highly meritorious Godāvarī and Arundhatī, are thus proclaimed.
"Even in the three worlds, she who is celebrated by the name of 'Woman' is the Great Goddess;
one should recognize her as the Goddess Śrī, so that she may abide upon my head. (74)
That which is called the Golden Pen is indeed said to be the Vidyā;
may she, who uproots the serpents, grant me happiness. (75)
She who is renowned as Kurukullā, born from the lineage of the king of birds—that Vidyā of great form—may she always abide upon the tip of my tongue. 76.
Known as Oṃkāriṇī, may she always abide within my body—
she who is the lore that removes obstacles and tears asunder the form of the Kali age.
May Bheruṇḍā protect my throat; may Totalā abide upon my head;
likewise, may Subalarekhā also always abide at my base.
May this knowledge, which destroys wild poisons, grant me the perfection of speech;
it is the science that bestows all accomplishments and yields the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. (79)
May Maṅgalā abide on the forehead; may Vijayā abide on the head;
may Ekākṣī be on the right shoulder and Trilocanā on the left.
May Jayantī abide in my belly; may Kandarpamohinī be in my waist; may Mālinī be at the junction of my penis; and may Samādhinī abide in my heart. (81)
Ambikā stands upon the spinal column, while Medinī remains on both sides;
Nāgendrī is on the tips of the fingers, and Diggajī is at the joints of the nails.
Vyāghrī and Cakrī reside in the shanks; Mahī is in the soles of the feet;
Amṛtā and Śaṅkhinī are in the cavities [of the ears]; and Vilāsinī is in the eyes. 83.
May Kālindī protect the root of the tongue, and may Raktinī protect the blood; may Lāṅgalī protect against poison from snakes, and Asthinī protect the joints of the bones.
May Śukreśvarī protect my marrow and marrow of the body, as well as my semen;
may Vetālī, the destroyer of disease, protect my skin. (85)
May Udbhaṭā always bring peace to my body;
may Padmāpā stay at my feet and Panthinī protect me on the road. (86)
May Bhairavī protect [us] from the fear of thieves, fire, kings, and serpents;
and may Bandhinī always effect the binding of the sight of the wicked. (87)
May that lore named Capeṭā grant me auspiciousness—Markaṭī, Ghaṭakarṇā, Hanumantī, and Rāvaṇī. (88)
I praise the fourfold Vidyā, renowned as Ghurghurī;
the Ceṭakā Vidyā which bestows knowledge, and the Kaumārī Caraṇāvalī. 89.
Known as the daughter of the Lords of Obstacles (Vighnarāja), she is contented and takes the form of progeny;
she is the Swan (Haṃsī) abiding in the Root-Space (Mūlākāśa), uplifted by the crushing of sinners.
May these ten mantra-sciences remain upon my head;
may the auspicious Yoginī stand before me and remain at my right side.
And at the time of sexual union, Śṛṅkhalā should remain on my left side as the fifth;
Śaṅkhinī is my crest-lock, while the auspicious Vastravatī has cast off her speed. (92–93)
She who is armor when there is armor, who brings delight to the eyes when there are eyes, she who is both manifest and concealed, the terrifying Bhairavī, the auspicious Śivā. (93) (94)
Saṃbhramā, Jayinī, Haṃsā, Subhagā, Jaladevatā, Yakṣiṇī, Cūḍakanyā, and likewise Ākāśagāminī. || 94 ||
Bhūcarī, Carakumbhī, and Sakalāgamadevatā; O Lord, Raṅgiṇī, Maitrī, and the renowned Madirālikā. (95)
Worshipped for the sake of all accomplishments in this scripture of the Yoginīmata, she who dwells in the Forest of Bliss is called "The Abiding One" by the virtuous. (96)
O Goddess who is the support of the sixty-four [arts], who bestows the aims of the three goals of life—homage be to you, O Sovereign of the World; homage be to you, O Mistress of the Universe. 97.
Homage to the goddess who bestows enjoyments; homage to the goddess Maheśvarī;
homage to her who dwells beyond destruction; homage to the giver of nirvāṇa. || 98 ||
"Homage to you, O Great Goddess; homage to you, the savior from saṃsāra!
O Mahāśambhu, those yoginīs by whom these [mantras] have been contemplated... (p. 116) 99.
But that yogi who dissolves into the Ādhāra becomes a knower of yoga;
for the forms of the Yoginīs abide within the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile. (100) [101]
May all those Yoginīs make my body firm;
I am Brahmā, I am Viṣṇu, and I alone am Maheśvara.
I am the abode of all beings in this world, the contemplator of power;
O gods and asuras, by means of this body through which power has been deposited, [I act]. 102.
O Śaṅkara, by the mere mention of their names, let them always carry out my command; whatever form of Yoginī exists within the three worlds, [let them obey]. (103)
All that remains within the body once the placement of power (śaktinyāsa) has been performed;
indeed, whatever placement fashioned from power a passionate woman performs as well. (104)
They know that goddess, who abides in a divine form, as the Tripura of saṃsāra; it should be given to sons and especially to devotees. (105)
This deposition of power (śaktinyāsa) should be given, but it must not be given to just anyone;
for human beings in this world, it bestows the fruit of their desired objects. (106)
O All-pervading Lord, he who performs my Nyāsa, augmented by the Ṣoḍhānyāsa,
shall live in the form of Śakti, capable of uprooting the three worlds.
If anyone should cause agitation to the living being during the performance of the deposition of power (śaktinyāsa),
whether by deed, mind, or speech, his head shall fall off.
Having thus performed the deposition of the powers (*śaktinyāsa*), one should perform the deposition of the Great Mistress of the Wheel (*mahācakreśvarīnyāsa*).
As before, preceded by meditation on the heart, hands, and the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), one should recite the mantra according to one's capacity and offer the recitation as before.
Of this *Prāsāda* mantra, which is both supreme and non-supreme (*parāpara-prāsāda*), Saccidānandabhairava is the seer (*ṛṣi*) and the consciousness-nature (*cinmaya*) is the meter (*chandas*).

Śrīparāmbā is the deity (devatā), *haṃ* is the seed-syllable (bīja), *oṃ* is the power (śakti), and *saḥ* is the pin (kīlaka). My application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of attaining the grace of Parāmbā through this recitation (japa).
*Ṛṣi*: Salutation to the Seer (*ṛṣi*) upon the head; *Chandas*: Salutation to the Metre (*chandas*) upon the mouth.

In the heart: *devatāyai namaḥ*; on the right breast: *bījāya namaḥ*; on the left breast: *śaktaye namaḥ*; at the navel: *kīlakāya*; [the application is] on the feet. The six-limbed ritual placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) of the hands begins with *hsāḥ śām* and so forth.
*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ īśānāya namaḥ*—*namaḥ* to both thumbs.
6 *tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*—salutation to the index fingers; 6 *aghorāya namaḥ*—salutation to the middle fingers;
6 *vāmadevāya namaḥ*—salutation to the ring fingers.
6 *sadyojātāya namaḥ*—*namaḥ* to both little fingers.
At the head: 6 *haṃ namaḥ*; at the mouth: 6 *yaṃ namaḥ*; at the heart: 6 *raṃ namaḥ*; at the navel: 6 *vaṃ namaḥ*.
At the *mūlādhāra*: "6 laṃ namaḥ"—this should be performed twice.
At the head: "6 īśānāya namaḥ"; at the mouth: "6 tatpuruṣāya namaḥ";
at the heart: "6 aghorāya namaḥ"; at the navel: "6 vāmadevāya namaḥ".
At the *mūlādhāra*: 6 *sadyojātāya namaḥ*.
At the *mūlādhāra*: 6 *sadyojātāya namaḥ*; at the navel: 6 *vāmadevāya namaḥ*;
at the heart: 6 *aghorāya namaḥ*; at the mouth: 6 *tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*.
On the head: *6 īśānāya namaḥ*. Having meditated upon the thousand-petaled lotus, [offer] *6 īśānāya namaḥ* to the upper face, and *6 tatpuruṣāya namaḥ* to the eastern face.
6 Aghorāya namaḥ, obeisance to the southern face; 6 Sadyojātāya namaḥ, obeisance to the western face;
6 Vāmadevāya namaḥ, obeisance to the northern face.

Having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) beginning with *hsāṃ śāṃ* and so forth, one should perform the Great Sixfold Placement (*mahāṣoḍhānyāsa*). As it is said in the *Kulaprakāśatantra* (p.

119): "Then, with a concentrated mind, one should perform the placement called the Great Sixfold [Placement] according to the procedure to be described, for the sake of attaining the state of the deity."
This has not been told to anyone at all; out of affection for you, I shall speak of it:
the phenomenal world, the embodied mantras, the deities, and the Mothers.
The rite of placement known as Mahāṣoḍhā is the most excellent among all rites of placement. Its application is as follows:
*Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsauṃḥ Shauṃḥ Aṃ*, salutation to Śrī, who is the form of the phenomenal world—on the head.
4 hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ āṃ, obeisance to Māyā in the form of the island—at the mouth; 4 hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ iṃ, obeisance to Kamalā in the form of the ocean—at the right eye;
4 hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ īṃ, obeisance to Viṣṇuvallabhā in the form of the mountain—at the left eye.
4 hsauṃ shauṃ uṃ, obeisance to Pattanarūpā, the bearer of the lotus—at the right ear;
4 hsauṃ shauṃ ūṃ, obeisance to Pīṭharūpā, the daughter of the ocean—at the left ear; 4 hsauṃ shauṃ ṛṃ, obeisance to Kṣetrarūpā, the mother of the world—at the right nostril.
The seed-syllable of supreme grace (*parā-prasāda-bīja*) should first be joined with *prāsāda-parā*.
6 *ṛṃ* vanarūpāyai kamalavāsinyai namaḥ—on the left nostril;
6 *ḷṃ* āśramarūpāyai indirāyai namaḥ—on the right cheek.
6 Ḷṃ, obeisance to Māyā in the form of a cave—on the left cheek;
6 Eṃ, obeisance to Ramā in the form of a river—on the upper lip; 6 Aiṃ, obeisance to Padmā in the form of a crossroads—on the lower lip.
6 Oṃ, obeisance to her whose form is born from sprouts, the beloved of Nārāyaṇa—on the upper teeth; (p. 120) 6 Auṃ, obeisance to her whose form is born from sweat, Siddhalakṣmī—on the lower teeth;
6 Aṃ, obeisance to her whose form is born from an egg, Rājalakṣmī—on the mouth.
6 Aḥ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī in the form of the viviparous—on the face; 6 Kaṃ, obeisance to Āryā in the form of Time (Kāla)—on the right armpit;
6 Khaṃ, obeisance to Anā in the form of a moment (tuṭi)—on the elbow.
6 Gaṃ, obeisance to Caṇḍikā in the form of Kalā—at the wrist; 6 Ghaṃ, obeisance to Durgā in the form of Kāṣṭhā—at the base of the fingers;
6 Ṅaṃ, obeisance to Śivā in the form of Nimiṣa—at the tips of the fingers.
6 CAṂ, salutation to Aparṇā in the form of breath—on the left armpit;
6 CHAṂ, salutation to Ambikā in the form of the ghaṭikā (twenty-four minutes)—on the elbow;
6 JAṂ, salutation to Satī in the form of the muhūrta (forty-eight minutes)—on the left wrist.
6 JHAṂ, salutation to Īśvarī, whose form is the watch (prahara), at the base of the fingers;
6 ÑAṂ, salutation to Śāmbhavī, whose form is the day, at the tips of the left fingers;
6 ṬAṂ, salutation to Īśānī, whose form is the twilight (sandhyā), at the base of the right foot.

6 Ṭhaṃ, obeisance to Pārvatī in the form of the night—at the knees; 6 Ḍaṃ, obeisance to Sarvamaṅgalā in the form of the lunar day—at the ankles; 6 Ḍhaṃ, obeisance to Dākṣāyaṇī in the form of the day of the week—at the base of the fingers.
6 ṇaṃ, obeisance to Haimavatī, who is the form of the lunar mansions—at the tips of the fingers; 6 taṃ, obeisance to Mahāmāyā, who is the form of yoga—at the base of the left foot;
6 thaṃ, obeisance to Māheśvarī, who is the form of the instruments of action—at the knee.
6 daṃ, obeisance to Mṛḍānī in the form of the lunar fortnight—at the ankles; 6 dhaṃ, obeisance to Rudrāṇī in the form of the months—at the bases of the fingers;
6 naṃ, obeisance to Śarvāṇī in the form of the zodiac signs—at the tips of the fingers.
4. *Paṃ* to the Supreme Sovereign (*parameśvarī*) in the form of the seasons, salutation—on the right side;
(p. 121) 6. *Phaṃ* to Kālī in the form of the solstices (*ayana*), salutation—on the left side; 6. *Baṃ* to Kātyāyanī in the form of the year (*saṃvatsara*), salutation—on the back.
6 BHAṂ, salutation to Gaurī, whose form is the Yuga—on the navel; 6 MAṂ, salutation to Bhavānī, whose form is dissolution—on the stomach;
6 YAṂ, salutation to Brāhmī, whose form is the five elements—on the heart.

6 *raṃ* to Vāgīśvarī, who is the form of the five subtle elements (*tanmātras*), salutation—on the right shoulder; 6 *laṃ* to Vāṇī, who is the form of the five organs of action (*karmendriyas*), salutation—on the left and right shoulders;
6 *vaṃ* to Sāvitrī, who is the form of the five organs of knowledge (*jñānendriyas*), salutation—on the back of the neck.
6 Śaṃ, salutation to Sarasvatī in the form of the five vital breaths—on the right armpit; 6 Ṣaṃ, salutation to Gāyatrī in the form of the three qualities (guṇas)—on the left armpit;
6 Saṃ, salutation to Vākpradā in the form of the fourfold internal organs—extending from the right hand to the foot.
6 Haṃ, salutation to Śāradā, whose form consists of the three states—up to the end of speech, hands, and feet;
6 Laṃ, salutation to Bhāratī, whose form consists of the seven constituents—at the belly and the mouth;

6 Hsauḥ Shauḥ Kṣaṃ, salutation to her who consists of the three humors and the three Vedas—the pervasive [seed-syllable]—thus one should perform the placement upon the locations of the Mātṛkā. Then...

Having recited the Mātṛkā from *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ aṃ āṃ* and so forth up to *kṣam*, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with: "Salutation to the Goddess Parāmbā, who is the supreme form of the entire phenomenal universe (*sakalaprapañca*); hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ. Thus ends the Prapañcanyāsa.
(p. 122) Now, the assignment of the worlds (*bhuvananyāsa*):

*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ aṃ āṃ iṃ*. Salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who dwells in the world of Atala, accompanied by hundreds of millions of Yoginīs beginning with Guhyā, and joined by the Root Deity, [to her] at the feet.

6 *īṃ uṃ ūṃ* obeisance to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in the Vitala world, who is accompanied by the root deity and hundreds of millions of most secret Anantayoginīs— at the two ankles; 6 *ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ* obeisance to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in the Sutala world, who is accompanied by the root deity and hundreds of millions of exceedingly secret and inconceivable Yoginīs— at the [two ankles].

In the two calves: 6 ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ, salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in the world of Mahātala, who is accompanied by hundreds of millions of independent great secret Yoginīs and the root deity. In the two knees: [6 ḷṃ eṃ aiṃ].

6 Oṃ auṃ, salutation to Ambādevī, the foundational power (ādhāraśakti) conjoined with the primordial deity (mūladevatā), the Yoginī of Supreme Secrecy (paramaguhya-icchāyoginī) residing in the world of Talātala— on the two thighs. 6 Aṃ aḥ, salutation to Ambādevī, the foundational power (ādhāraśakti) conjoined with the primordial deity, the Yoginī of Secret Knowledge (rahasyajñānayoginī) residing in the world of Rasātala.
The buttocks:

6 kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ. Salutation to Ambā Devī, the power of the support (ādhāraśakti), who is joined with the root deity, the secret practitioner of the yoga of action (kriyāyoginī) of the hundred million [deities] residing in the Pātāla-loka. — At the *mūlādhāra*.

6 caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ, salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in the Bhūrloka, who is accompanied by hundreds of millions of most secret Ḍākinīs and Yoginīs, and who is the primordial deity— at the Svādhiṣṭhāna; 6 ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ, [salutation to the Mother Goddess] Rākinī, who resides in the Bhūvarloka and is accompanied by hundreds of millions of Mahārahasya Yoginīs.

Salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, accompanied by the Root Deity, in Maṇipūra— taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ; salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, accompanied by the Root Deity, [who is] Lākinī Yoginī, the supreme secret of the hundred million [deities] residing in Svarloka, in Anāhata.

6 paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ, homage to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in Maharloka, accompanied by the primordial deity and the hundred million secret Kākinī-yoginīs— at Viśuddhi. 6 yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ, homage to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in Janoloka, accompanied by the primordial deity and the hundred million more secret Śākinī-yoginīs.

*Namaḥ*— at the *ājñā-cakra*: 6 *śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ*, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in the world of *tapas*, who is accompanied by hundreds of millions of most secret *hākinī-yoginīs*, and who is the primordial deity (*mūladevatā*),
at the forehead.

*Laṃ kṣaṃ*, salutation to the Mother Goddess, the Supportive Power (*ādhāraśakti*), who resides in the Brahma-aperture (*brahmarandhra*), accompanied by the primordial deity (*mūladevatā*) and the hundred million great secret *yoginīs* and *yākinīs* of the realm of Truth (*satyaloka*).
Having uttered the *mātṛkā* from *a* to *kṣa*: *hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ*, salutation to the venerable Mother Parā (*śrīparāmbādevī*), the sovereign of the fourteen worlds.
One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*). Thus ends the placement of the worlds (*bhuvana-nyāsa*). Now follows the placement of the forms (*mūrti-nyāsa*):
*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ aṃ*, salutation to Keśava and Akṣarī on the head.
6 Āṃ Nārāyaṇa Ādyābhyāṃ namaḥ—on the face; 6 Iṃ Mādhava Iṣṭadābhyāṃ namaḥ—on the right shoulder;
Oṃ Īṃ Govinda Īśānībhyāṃ namaḥ—on the left shoulder.
6 *Uṃ* Viṣṇu-umābhyāṃ namaḥ—on the right side; 6 *Ūṃ* Madhusūdana-ūrdhvanayanābhyāṃ namaḥ—on the left side;
6 *Ṛṃ* [Ṛddhi-]ṛddhibhyāṃ namaḥ—on the right hip.
6 *Ṛṃ* obeisance to Vāmanarūpiṇī—on the left hip; 6 *Ḷṃ* obeisance to Śrīdhara and Luptā—on the right thigh;
6 *Ḹṃ* obeisance to Hṛṣīkeśa and Lūnadoṣā—on the left thigh.
6 Eṃ Padmanābha Ekanāyakābhyāṃ namaḥ—on the right knee;
6 Aiṃ Dāmodara Aiṃkāriṇībhyāṃ namaḥ—on the left knee; 6 Oṃ Vāsudeva Oghavatībhyāṃ namaḥ—on the right shank.
6 Oṃ, obeisance to Saṅkarṣaṇa and Arkamālā—on the left calf;
6 Aṃ, obeisance to Pradyumna and Añjanaprabhā—on the right foot; 6 Aḥ, obeisance to Aniruddha and Asthimālādharā—on the left foot.
6 *kaṃ bhaṃ* to Bhavakara and Bhadrā—salutation to the tip of the right foot; 6 *khaṃ baṃ* to Śarva and Khagabala—salutation to the tip of the left foot;
6 *gaṃ phaṃ* to Rudra and Garimādiphalapradā—salutation to the right side.
6 *ghaṃ paṃ* — obeisance to Paśupati and Ghaṇṭāpadmā—on the left side; 6 *ṅaṃ naṃ* — obeisance to Ugra and Ānandā—at the base of the right arm;
6 *caṃ dhaṃ* — obeisance to Mahādeva and Candradharā—at the base of the left arm.
6 *chaṃ* *daṃ*, obeisance to Bhīma and Chandomayī—at the throat;
6 *jaṃ* *thaṃ*, obeisance to Īśāna and Jagatsthāna—at the upper face on the head;
6 *jhaṃ* *taṃ*, obeisance to Tatpuruṣa and Balabhārā—at the eastern face on the mouth.
6. *Ñaṃ* *ṇaṃ*, obeisance to Aghora and Jñāna—at the right face;
(p. 125) 6. *Ṭaṃ* *ḍhaṃ*, obeisance to Sadyojāta and Dharā—at the western face;
6. Below the crest, *Ṭhaṃ* *ḍaṃ*, obeisance to Vāmadeva and Ṭhaṅkārakṛtiḍāmarī—at the northern face.

6 Vāmakarṇe: 6 *Yaṃ* to Brahman and Yakṣiṇī, salutation—at the *mūlādhāra*; 6 *Raṃ* to Prajāpati and Añjanī, salutation—at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*; 6 *Laṃ* to Vedhas and Lakṣmī, salutation—at the *maṇipūra*.
6 *vaṃ*—homage to Parameṣṭhin and Vajriṇī—at Anāhata;
6 *śaṃ*—homage to Pitāmaha and Śaśidhara—at Viśuddhi; 6 *ṣaṃ*—homage to Vidhātṛ and Ṣaḍādhāralaya—at Ājñā.
6 Saṃ, obeisance to Viriñci and Sarvanāyikā—on the forehead;
6 Haṃ, obeisance to Sraṣṭṛ and Hasitānanā—on the parting of the hair;
6 Laṃ, obeisance to Caturānana and Lalitā—on the crown of the head.
6. *Śaṃ* to Hiraṇyagarbha and Kṣamā—*namaḥ* at the *brahmarandhra*.

Having uttered *hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ* and the complete *mātṛkā*, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with the words: *namaḥ* to the Supreme Goddess Ambā, whose essence is the Trinity (*trimūrti*). This is the placement of the forms (*mūrtinyāsa*).
Now, the ritual placement of mantras (mantranyāsa): Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ aṃ āṃ iṃ,

to the presiding deity of all mantras, whose essence consists of single-syllabled mantras beginning with the Praṇava and comprising one hundred thousand times ten million varieties, the bestower of all fruits.
Salutation to Ekakūṭeśvarī Ambā Devī—at the Mūlādhāra.

6. *Īṃ ūṃ ūṃ*. Salutation to Dvikūṭeśvarī Ambā Devī, the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of two syllables such as Haṃsa, who comprises two hundred thousand crores of divisions, and who bestows all fruits—at the Svādhiṣṭhāna.

6 Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ. Salutation to the Mother Goddess Trikūṭeśvarī Ambā, the presiding deity of all mantras whose nature consists of the three syllables beginning with Fire (*vahni*) and comprising three million times ten million divisions; she who bestows all fruits—at Maṇipura.

6 Ḷṃ Eṃ Aiṃ. [Salutation] to the presiding deity of all mantras whose nature consists of the four syllables beginning with the Moon (*candra*) and comprising four million times ten million divisions; she who bestows all fruits.
Salutation to the Goddess Ambā, Mistress of the Four Peaks—at the Anāhata [cakra].

6. Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ. Salutation to the Goddess Ambā, Mistress of the Five Peaks, the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of the five syllables beginning with Sūrya, who comprises fifty-five million distinct forms, and who bestows all fruits—at the Viśuddha [cakra].

6 Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ [Oṃ]—salutation to the Mother Goddess Ṣaṭkūṭeśvarī, the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of the six syllables beginning with *skanda* (which have sixty million times six varieties), the bestower of all fruits; [this is] in the Ājñā [cakra].

6 Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Caṃ [Oṃ]—[salutation] to the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of the seven syllables beginning with *gaṇeśa* (which have seventy million times seven varieties), the bestower of all fruits.
Salutation to the Mother Goddess Saptakūṭeśvaryambā—on the *bindu*.

6. *Chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ* — Salutation to the Mother Goddess Aṣṭakūṭeśvaryambā, who is the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of the eight classes of *vaṭukas*, the eight *saras*, and the [eight] divisions of eighty million *lakṣas*, and who bestows all fruits—on the half-moon (*ardhendu*).

6 ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Navakūṭeśvarī, who is the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of the nine syllables beginning with Brahmā and their nine million billion variations, and who bestows all fruits— [at] Rodhinī; 6 ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ, [obeisance to the Mother Goddess] who is the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of the ten syllables beginning with Viṣṇu and their ten million billion variations, and who bestows all fruits.
Salutation to the goddess Daśakūṭeśvaryambā— [at the *nāda*].

Salutation to the goddess Ekādaśakūṭeśvaryambā, who consists of the eleven syllables beginning with Śaiva (the eleven Rudras), who is the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of eleven-lakṣa-koṭi divisions, and who bestows all fruits— [at the end of the *nāda*].

6 Dhaṃ naṃ paṃ—salutation to the Mother Goddess Dvādaśakūṭeśvarī, the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of twelve syllables such as Vāṇī and others, divided into twelve hundred thousand crores of varieties, the bestower of all fruits; [this is] in Śakti.
6 Phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ—[salutation] to the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of thirteen syllables such as Lakṣmī and others, divided into thirteen hundred thousand crores of varieties.
Salutation to the Mother Goddess Trayodaśakūṭeśvarī Ambā, the bestower of all fruits—at Vyāpikā.

6. Maṃ Yaṃ Raṃ. Salutation to the Mother Goddess Caturdaśakūṭeśvarī Ambā, who consists of the fourteen syllables beginning with Gaurī and the deities of all mantras divided into fourteen lakṣa and koṭis, the bestower of all fruits—at the station of Samānā.

6 Laṃ Vaṃ Śaṃ: Salutation to the Mother Goddess Pañcadaśakūṭeśvarī Ambā, who consists of the fifteen syllables beginning with *durga* and comprising fifteen million billion variations, who is the presiding deity of all mantras, and who bestows all fruits—[this is] in Unmanī.
6 Hsauṃḥ Shauṃḥ Saṃ Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ Kṣaṃ.

Salutation to Ambā Devī, the Sovereign of the Sixteen Peaks (Ṣoḍaśakūṭeśvarī), who consists of the sixteen syllables beginning with Traipura, who possesses sixteen million billion divisions, who is the presiding deity of all mantras, and who bestows all fruits— at the station of Śiva, within the Dhruvamaṇḍala,
the locations of the ten cakras beginning with Bindu are situated one finger-breadth each above the Ājñācakra.
They stand one above the other. In the *dhruvamaṇḍala*, the ground culminating at the *brahmarandhra* is the abode of Sadāśiva; this means the Great Bindu (*mahābindu*).

Then, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with: *hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ aṃ āṃ* and so forth, ending with *kṣaṃ*, saying: "Salutation to Parāmbā Devī, the Sovereign of all Mantras. This is the mantra-placement (*mantranyāsa*).

(p. 128) Now, the deposition of the deities (*daivatanya-āsa*): *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauṃḥ shauṃḥ aṃ āṃ*, salutation to the goddess Nibṛtyambā, who is served by a multitude of thousands of crores of ṛṣis—on the big toe of the right foot.

6 iṃ īṃ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Pratiṣṭhāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of the Yoga-kula—on the big toe of the left foot; 6 uṃ ūṃ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Vidyāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of the Tapas-kula—on the right ankle;
6 ṛṃ ṝṃ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Śāntyambā, served by a thousand koṭis of the Śānta-kula—on the left ankle.
6 Ḷṃ Ḹṃ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Śāntyatītāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of the assembly of sages—on the right shank;

6 Eṃ Aiṃ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Hṛllekhāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of the assembly of gods—on the left shank; 6 Oṃ Auṃ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Gaganāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of the assembly of rākṣasas—on the right knee.

6 aṃ aḥ, obeisance to the goddess Raktāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of Vidyādhara clans—at the left knee; 6 kaṃ khaṃ, obeisance to the goddess Mahocchuṣmāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of Siddha clans—at the right thigh;
6 gaṃ ghaṃ, obeisance to the goddess Karālikāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of Sādhya clans—at the left thigh.

6 ṄAṂ CAṂ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Jayāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of the host of Apsarases—on the right hip; 6 CHAṂ JAṂ, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Vijayāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of the host of Gandharvas—on the left hip;

At the *brahmarandhra*, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with: "Oṃ, Āṃ," and so forth, up to "Kṣāṃ," [saying]: "Salutation to the Supreme Mother Goddess (*parāmbā-devī*), the sovereign of all the Mothers and Bhairavas.

Then, having performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) with the six long seed-syllables *hsāṃ*, *shauṃ*, *hsīṃ*, *shīṃ*, *haḥ*, and *saḥ*, one should meditate upon the deity.
Regarding meditation, it is said in the *Mahākulaprakāśatantra*:
"The Goddess, whose body has been thus consecrated, should meditate on the deity with undistracted mind."
Situated in the midst of the ocean of nectar, upon a delightful island of jewels.
Seated upon a lotus on a majestic throne made of the nine precious gems, within a pavilion of fresh rubies situated in the midst of a forest of wish-fulfilling trees.
Seated within a triangle, possessing a splendor joined with the moon and the sun,
united with the half-form of Ambikā, and adorned with distinct ornaments.
Possessing the beauty of ten million Cupids, eternally sixteen years of age,
with a lotus face graced by a gentle smile, three eyes, and the moon as his crest-ornament.
Adorned with divine garments, garlands, and unguents, and decorated with celestial ornaments,
he holds in his hands a drinking vessel, the *cinmudrā*, a trident, and a book.
He who bears knowledge in his assembly, whose face and eyes are ever-blissful,
and who is served by the entire host of deities arisen from the Great Sixteen.
Thus, one should meditate upon Śiva as Ardhanārīśvara within the lotus of the heart;
or one may remember him as the male deity, or contemplate him in female form.
Alternatively, one should meditate upon the partless [form], whose body is existence, consciousness, and bliss;
divine, consisting of all splendor, and embodying the entire universe of moving and non-moving beings.
Then the Supreme Goddess should display the ten mudrās:
the four mudrās consisting of the Yoni, the Liṅga, the Surabhi, and the Heti.
One should recite the garland-mantra, the great mudrā, and also the space-mudrā in succession;
likewise, one should recite the root mantra and the venerable pādukā according to one's capacity.

The *hetimudrā* consists of the skull, the *jñāna-triśūla*, and the book. Having displayed these mudrās, one should recite the root mantra of the *Prāsāda*—which consists of both the supreme (*parā*) and the non-supreme (*aparā*) *Prāsāda*—as well as the *Śrīgurupādukā*, according to one's capacity; then, one should meditate upon the venerable Guru on the crown of one's head.
And it is said in that very same [text]:
One should contemplate the Goddess upon the crown of the head as the venerable Guru in the form of Śiva,
possessing the luster of the full moon within a thousand-petaled lotus.
With lotus hands bestowing boons and fearlessness, clad in stainless fragrant flowers and garments,
with a serene face and eyes, he embodies the form of all deities.

"One should remember the Guru on the head, preceded by his name. Having thus meditated and prostrated, one should recall the name given by one's own Guru at the *mūlādhāra* and contemplate one's own self as having the form of Śiva.
He states the fruit for the one who performs this ritual placement (*nyāsa*) as follows:
When the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) has been performed in this manner, the practitioner becomes directly the Supreme Śiva;
of this there is no doubt, for he is capable of both restraint and grace.
O Pārvatī, for whoever performs the ritual placement (nyāsa) known as the Great Sixfold (Mahāṣoḍhā),
the area extending ten yojanas in every direction is declared to be a divine field (divyakṣetra).
O beloved, wherever a man goes after performing this nyāsa,
there he shall obtain gain from the twice-born, as well as honor and manly prowess.
If one who has performed the Mahāṣoḍhā nyāsa bows to someone ignorant of it,
he shall meet death within a month, even if Śiva himself were his protector.

Whoever performs this ritual placement (nyāsa) called the Vajrapañjara [will find that] those dwelling in the heavens, the atmosphere, on the earth, in mountains, in water, and in forests [are all protected].
O Kuleśvarī, ghosts, vetālas, gods, rākṣasas, grahas, and the like do not even look upon him with minds terrified by fear.
The deities beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, as well as all the sages, yogis, and lords of munis, perform this ritual placement known as Mahāṣoḍhā.
(135) What is the use of much speaking, O Goddess? This nyāsa is dear to me.
One should not speak of it to one who is not a son, O Goddess, nor should one reveal it to one who is not a disciple.
One attains the accomplishment of command; one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) in secret.
This protection is superior to all others and bestows the accomplishment of the state of divinity.
"There is no doubt that this does not exist in the world; it is the truth, the absolute truth, O fair-faced one!

This entrustment (nyāsa) is obtained through the merits accumulated over many lifetimes; therefore, he says: 'And the entry into the Upper Tradition (ūrdhvāmnāya), as well as the meditation on the Parā-Prāsāda.'"
The thorough knowledge of the Great Sixfold [Yoga] is not the fruit of minor austerity.
Thus concludes the Great Sixfold Deposition (*mahāṣoḍhānyāsa*). May there be an offering to the venerable Sarasvatī.

For this mantra of the venerable Great Sandals (*śrīmahāpādukāmantra*): Haṃsa is the Seer (*ṛṣi*), the unmanifest Gāyatrī is the Metre (*chanda*), the venerable Great Sandals is the Deity (*devatā*), Haṃsa is the Seed-syllable (*bīja*), Saḥ is the Power (*śakti*), and So’ham is the Bolt (*kīlaka*). My application (*viniyoga*) is in recitation for the sake of attaining the grace of the deity of the Great Sandals.
Having performed the *ṛṣyādi-nyāsa*, one performs the six-limbed *nyāsa* (*ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) on the hands beginning with *hsām*. The meditation (*dhyāna*) is as follows:
[One should meditate upon] the thousand-petaled lotus, which bestows the bliss of Brahman and supreme happiness.

Having meditated on the self-luminous form of Śiva and His Śakti, and having displayed the gestures of the boon-granting hand, the gesture of fearlessness, the crown, and the crocodile-shaped earrings, one should worship them with the five offerings.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskhphreṃ Hsauṃ Hasakṣamalavarayaūṃ Sahakṣamalavara Īṃ, [I worship] the Parameṣṭhi Guru,

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskhphreṃ Hsauṃ Hasakṣamalavaraya Ūṃ Sahakṣamalavaraya Īṃ Paramaguru Amukānandanātha (Brahmānanda) Hsauṃ Hskhphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Śrīṃ Amukāmbā Śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi namaḥ.

I worship the Śrīpādukā; I satiate it; obeisance! Oṃ Hrīṃ Vaṃ Ṭhaṃ, to Amṛtarudra: Āṃ Hrīṃ Kroṃ, bring what is adverse to me into subjection, bring it into subjection, Svāhā! Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsauṃḥ Shauṃḥ, obeisance to Śiva, the gracious Pārijāta!

Thus, with two [verses], one [verse] beginning with "tāmadaiteya," and one [verse] beginning with "śroṇāmekā," he should release her from Śukra’s curse.

*svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā pavasva soma dhārayā | indrāya pātave sutaḥ ||* (Flow, O Soma, with your most sweet and most intoxicating stream, being pressed for Indra to drink.)
O Rākṣas, drive away all the seers; strike him down with the wood. May he bestow wide space upon us;
be most gracious, O greatest slayer of Vṛtra, and carry us across the abundance of the waters.

may you bring us glory and fame. O Indu, day by day, through you, our hopes are directed toward you alone.
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb, and may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms.
May Prajāpati place the embryo within you; may he establish the embryo for you. May Nīvārī bestow the embryo upon you; may Sarasvatī bestow the embryo.

O divine Savitṛ, purify us with three most excellent, soma-bearing, and skillful powers, O Agni. Purify us!
Purify me, O divine folk; purify me with your wisdom.

Swell up, O Soma, bestow your power, and with all your rays, become the supreme oblation for the gods.
The Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudrī, and Vitastā—these rivers have heard my hymn of praise.

Having worshipped and gratified [the deity] with the root-mantra, having gazed upon it with the gaze-mudrā, having sprinkled it with the weapon-mantra, having struck it three times with kuśa grass while reciting the weapon-mantra, having sprinkled it with the armor-mantra, and having smelled it, one should cause it to enter through the left nostril, lead it to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), and there,
having merged into the ocean of supreme nectar situated within the lunar orb of consciousness (cic-candramaṇḍala), become one with it.
