*Oṃ namo bhagavati grāmeśvari vāruṇijalamūrte ūrdhvabindugrāhini mahālakṣmīśvari paramadhāmni paramākāśabhāsuri somasūryāgnibhakṣiṇi āgacchāgaccha viśa viśa svabhogadravyaṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa*.

Saying "svāhā," one should take a drop from that jar with the left thumb and ring finger held over the second section [of the vessel] and cast it upward. Then, having performed the worship of the jar, one should cover it with another vessel and take up the vessel for extraction.

Having worshipped with the four powers (*śakticatuṣṭaya*) as follows: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ amoghāyai namaḥ* (four times), *sūkṣmāyai namaḥ* (four times), *oṃ ānandāyai namaḥ* (four times), and *śāntyai namaḥ* (four times), one should place [the vessel] upon the lid-vessel of the water-pot (*kumbha*). (p. 145)

Having performed the ritual installation of the water-pot (*kalaśa*), one should then, on the ground smeared with sandalwood paste, fashion a mandala consisting of a square, a circle, and a triangle at the front of the southern side of the pot using pure water. While reciting the three *tāras*, one should form this with both hands—the right hand with the breath flowing through the nose and the palms joined upwards—and worship the center of the triangle with the root-mantra preceded by the *praṇava* and *tritāra* and ending with *namaḥ*. Then, one should worship the three corners, starting from the tip facing oneself, using the three *kūṭas*.

Having worshipped [the deity] by circumambulation, one should worship the six limbs with the mantras of the Heart and the other four limbs in the southeast, southwest, northwest, and northeast corners of the square; the Eye in the center; and the Weapon in the four directions starting from the east. Having thus worshipped, one should place the base (ādhāra), which has been washed there with the root mantra (mūla-mantra).

Then, having uttered the first *kūṭa*—*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*—[one worships] for the sake of the Fire-mandala, which consists of ten digits (*kalā*) that bestow merit (*dharma*), belonging to the Śrī Parādevatā.

Having worshipped with "Oṃ, obeisance to the support of the general arghya," and having worshipped the ten kalās of Fire there according to the method to be described, one should place the conch washed with the Astra-mantra therein; then, uttering the second kūṭa, [one should worship] with:
"Oṃ, obeisance to the support of the general arghya for the Śrī Parādevatā, which is the solar orb consisting of the twelve kalās that bestow wealth."

Having thus worshipped, and having worshipped the twelve kalās of the Sun there according to the method to be described hereafter, one should fill that vessel with fragrant, pure water scented with perfumes such as sandalwood, while reciting the Praṇava, the three Tāras, the root-vidyā at its end, and the Mātṛkā in reverse order, ending with the third kūṭa.

Having worshipped with "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, obeisance to the general *argha*-nectar of the Supreme Goddess, who is the soul of the sixteen digits (*kalā*) of the lunar orb that bestows desires," one should then worship the sixteen digits of the Moon there in the manner to be described. Therein—

As before, having invoked the *tīrtha* from the solar disc (*savitṛmaṇḍala*) and offered a drop of nectar (*amṛtabindu*) into the jar, one should place perfumes, flowers, and so forth therein with the root mantra.

Having worshipped it with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as before, one should consecrate it three times with the Navātman couple-mantra: *hasakṣamalavarayūṃ sahakṣamalavarayīṃ*. Then, one should consecrate it three times with the Varuṇa couple-mantra: *hsauṃ vāruṇīdevyai namaḥ*, and finally consecrate it eight times with the root mantra.

Having performed the general *argha* offering by displaying the *dhenu-yoni-mudrā*, one should smear the ground near that [offering] with the water of the general *argha* mixed with fragrant substances such as *yakṣakardama*. Then, having fashioned a mandala consisting of a square, a circle, and a hexagon there with the two hands in the *vahannāsā-ūrdhvapuṭa* gesture, one should stabilize that mandala with the left hand marked by the *śaṅkha-mudrā*.

In the center of that, having drawn a triangle with the *kāmakalā*—consisting of the fourth vowel (*turyasvara*) together with the *bindu*—in its middle, one should worship the mandala with the mantra:

"Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to the mandala which is the support for the special *argha* of the Supreme Deity. Then, having worshipped the center of the triangle with the root mantra ending in "namas" preceded by the four [syllables], one worships the first *kūṭa* in the front corner of the triangle.

Having worshipped the triangle in a clockwise direction with "Namaḥ" on the left [corner], "Namaḥ" for the second peak-syllable (*kūṭa*) on the [left], and "Namaḥ" for the third peak-syllable on the right;
and having worshipped the six corners of the hexagon in a clockwise direction starting from its own apex by repeating the three root peak-syllables twice;

and having worshipped the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) in the square as before; [one should worship] in the four directions starting from its own apex within the square and in the center, in a clockwise direction.
Glūṃ, homage to the jewel of the celestial realm; Slūṃ, homage to the jewel of the heavenly realm;
Mlūṃ, homage to the jewel of the mortal realm; Plūṃ, homage to the jewel of the subterranean realm; Nlūṃ, homage to the jewel of the nāga realm.

Having thus worshipped the five jewels, one should again worship the six seats mentioned in the ritual of *nyāsa* within the hexagon, proceeding clockwise starting from the eastern point. Then, upon the square, the circle, the hexagon, and the triangle, one should worship with:
"Oṃ 4 Kāmarūpa-pīṭhāya namaḥ" and "Oṃ 4 Jālandhara-pīṭhāya namaḥ."

4 *pūrṇagiripīṭhāya namaḥ*, 4 *oḍyāṇapīṭhāya namaḥ*, 4— having thus worshipped the four seats (*pīṭha*), if one possesses the *śāmbhava-dīkṣā*, one should worship [the deities] in the square, starting from the southeast and proceeding through the four directions and the center, using five sets of the *praṇava* enclosed by the *praṇava*. It is as follows:
Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hskhphreṃ hsauṃ aiṃ hsauṃ hskhphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ. Thus:
five times hrīṃ, [five times] namaḥ; five times śrīṃ, [five times] namaḥ; five times hskhphreṃ, [five times] namaḥ; five times hsauṃ, [five times] namaḥ.
Thus one should worship. 4. *Mūla-mantra*: Salutation to the argha-maṇḍala consisting of the four seats of the Śrī Paradevatā, who is composed of all powers (*sarvaśaktimayī*).

Having uttered the first *kūṭa*, [one says]: *Oṃ* salutation to the support of the vessel for the special argha (*viśeṣārghapātrādhāra*), which is the maṇḍala of fire (*vahnimaṇḍala*) and whose self consists of the ten digits that bestow dharma.

Having washed [the vessel] and placed it upon the *ādhāramaṇḍala*, one should worship the *ādhāra*. Then, having invoked the ten *kalās* of Fire starting from its own front (east) and proceeding clockwise, one should perform the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* for them.
In that regard, using the previously mentioned *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* mantras, one should substitute the word "of me" (*mama*) with the phrase "of Dhūmrārcirā and the others" (*dhūmrārceyadīnām*).
Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* by reciting the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā-mantra* while touching the support (*ādhāra*), one should recite:
*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ saṃ dhūmrāciṣe namaḥ*,
*4 raṃ uṣmāyai namaḥ*, *4 laṃ jvalinyai namaḥ*.
4 vaṃ, obeisance to Jvālinī; 4 śaṃ, obeisance to Visphuliṅgī;
4 ṣaṃ, obeisance to Suśrī; 4 saṃ, obeisance to Surūpā; 4 haṃ, obeisance to Kapilā; 4 laṃ, obeisance to Havyavāhā.

Having worshipped them with "4 KṢAṂ, obeisance to Kavyavāhā," and having washed a vessel made of gold or other materials with the Astra-mantra, one should place it there with "4, I establish the special arghya-vessel for the Śrī Paradevatā," and then, uttering the second kūṭa, [place] AṂ.

Having worshipped in the center of the vessel with the mantra: "Obeisance to the special arghya-vessel of the Śrī Parādevatā, whose self consists of the twelve digits that bestow wealth upon the solar orb," one should visualize therein the previously mentioned maṇḍala. Having worshipped it as before up to the five jewels, and likewise having honored it with the five *praṇavas*, one should invoke there the twelve digits of the Sun, and as previously [stated], address them by their names.
Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā*, one should worship them in a circular form by proceeding clockwise. It is as follows:
*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kaṃ bhaṃ tapinyai namaḥ*;
4 *khaṃ baṃ tāpinyai namaḥ*; 4 *gaṃ phaṃ dhūmrāyai namaḥ*.
4 ghaṃ paṃ, obeisance to Marīcī; 4 ṅaṃ naṃ, obeisance to Jvālinī; 4 caṃ dhaṃ, obeisance to Ruci; 4 chaṃ daṃ, obeisance to Suṣumnā;
4 jaṃ thaṃ, obeisance to Bhogadā; 4 jhaṃ taṃ, obeisance to Viśvā.
4 ñaṃ ṇaṃ *bodhinyai* namaḥ, 4 ṭaṃ daṃ *dhāriṇyai* namaḥ,
4 ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ *kṣamāyai* namaḥ; having thus worshipped [these], one should draw up the water contained in the jar with a vessel,

recite the reverse *mātṛkā* at the end of the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*), pour that water and other substances from the vessel [into the jar], and [touch it] with the syllable *ram* using the thumb and ring finger.

There, having stirred the water contained in the vessel with a flower and cast that flower away, one should utter "klīm" and cast in a sandalwood flower moistened with the paste of the eight fragrances— namely sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, *coraka*, saffron, *rocanā*, *jaṭāmāṃsī*, and *śilārāsa*— and then gaze upon it with the *gālinī-mudrā* while reciting "sauḥ."

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, [this is] the third *kūṭa*. Oṃ, obeisance to the lunar orb (*somamaṇḍala*), the bestower of desires, whose essence consists of sixteen digits (*kalā*), the fourfold *arghya*-maṇḍala of the venerable Supreme Deity. (Recite this) four times.

Having worshipped the previously mentioned maṇḍala within the vessel containing the cause, with the words "obeisance to the nectar of the special *arghya*," one should worship it in the center of the vessel.
Having visualized [the deity] as before and performed worship up to the five jewels, one who is endowed with the Śāmbhava initiation should likewise worship with the Praṇavas.

Therein, having invoked the sixteen digits (*kalā*) of the Moon and performed the ritual installation of their vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) preceded by their respective names as before, one should worship them in a circular form, proceeding clockwise starting from the eastern point. It is as follows:
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ, obeisance to Amṛtā; 4 āṃ, obeisance to Ānandā; 4 iṃ, obeisance to Pūṣā;
4 īṃ, obeisance to Tuṣṭi; 4 uṃ, obeisance to Puṣṭi.
4 Ūṃ, obeisance to Rati; 4 Ṛṃ, obeisance to Dhṛti;
4 Ṝṃ, obeisance to Śaśinī; 4 Ḷṃ, obeisance to Candrikā;
4 Ḹṃ, obeisance to Kānti; 4 Eṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā.
4 Aiṃ, obeisance to Śrī; 4 Oṃ, obeisance to Prīti; 4 Auṃ, obeisance to Aṅgadā; 4 Aṃ, obeisance to Pūrṇā;
4 Aḥ, obeisance to Pūrṇāmṛtā. Having thus worshipped, [one should worship] the triangle in the center of the previously worshipped maṇḍala, beginning with Akatha... [and so on].

Having visualized the three *kūṭas* of the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*) within its three corners, one should visualize the *Kāmakalā* in its central *bindu*, the syllables *haṃ* and *kṣa* with their *bindus* on its two sides, the letter *la* behind it, and the syllables *haṃsaḥ* on its two sides. Then, having placed flowers and consecrated rice (*akṣata*) all around and having formed the *yonimudrā*, one should raise the *Kuṇḍalinī* from the *mūlādhāra* according to the method instructed by the Guru, piercing the six wheels (*ṣaṭcakra*) in sequence along the path of the *suṣumṇā*.

Having led the lunar orb of consciousness to the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra), bring forth the essence of nectar that fills the great vessel— filled with the entirety of the essences produced from the fragments of the cosmic egg.

Reciting "Aiṃ Plūṃ Hsauṃ Jūṃ Saḥ Amṛte Amṛtodbhave Amṛteśvari Amṛtavarṣiṇi Amṛtaṃ Srāvaya Srāvaya Svāhā," one should join that stream of nectar into the *argha* water by scattering flowers and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and then display the *dhenu-mudrā* while reciting "Vam."

Having consecrated [the object] three times with the eight-syllable mantra of the Self, *oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā*, and having again uttered the *praṇava* (*oṃ*), one should worship in the center of the *hetu* (cause) with the words, "I worship the supreme, partless Śāmbhavī Śrī Pādukā. Then, having consecrated it three times with the mantra *haṃsaḥ*, [one worships] *haṃsaḥ*, the unstruck power (*ajapā-śakti*) Śrī...

Having worshipped with "I worship the *pādukā*," and having consecrated it three times with the *mātṛkā* devoid of the nasal bindu, one should again utter that [mantra] and worship within the causal center (*hetumadhye*) with "I worship the venerable *pādukā* of Sarasvatī, the *mātṛkā*. Then, having consecrated it ten times with the third *kūṭa* of the root mantra, and again uttering that third *kūṭa*, one should worship within the causal center with "I worship the venerable *pādukā* of Tripurāmṛteśvarī."
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasakṣamalavarayūṃ, having worshipped [the deity],
sahakṣamalavarayīṃ.
Having consecrated [the substance] three times with the two vidyās of Ānandabhairava and Bhairavī, and having worshipped and gratified it three times with:
*hasakṣamalavarayūṃ ānandabhairavāya vauṣaṭ; ānandabhairava śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi*.

4. *Sahakṣamalavarayīṃ*, *vaṣaṭ* to the goddess Sudhā; "I worship the *śrīpādukā* of the goddess Sudhā"—having thus worshipped three times and offered libations, [one says]: *Hsauṃ* obeisance to Varuṇa; *Shauṃ* obeisance to the goddess Vāruṇī.

Having thus consecrated it three times with the Varuṇa and Mithuna Vidyās, and on that day having consecrated it nine times (three times each) with the Nityā-vidyā and the respective Tithi-nityā-vidyā,
[one who is] initiated into the Ūrdhvāmnāya [should use] the two mantras Prāsāda-parā and Parā-prāsāda:
*hsauṃḥ* and *shauṃḥ*.

Having consecrated [the water] three times with these two mantras, if [the disciple] has been initiated into the *caraṇa* [tradition], then having consecrated it three times each with the *vidyās* of the *caraṇa-kula-yoginīs*, if he has been initiated into the *saumya* [tradition] by means of the *anuttara-parā-vidyā*, then having consecrated it three times with that; if he has been consecrated with the *pūrṇābhiṣeka*, then having consecrated it three times with the *kāmakalā-vidyā*; if he is endowed with the *ṣaḍanvaya-śāmbhava-dīkṣā*, then having consecrated it three times with those respective *vidyās*, then [the procedure] to be described hereafter...

Having consecrated it three times with the mantras of the five enjoyers (*pañcabhoktṛ*), one should invoke the ten kalās beginning with Sṛṣṭi into the center of the causal [mandala]. As before, having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* for them preceded by their respective names, one should recite the Vidyā:
*oṃ haṃ saḥ śuciṣadvasurantarikṣasaddhotā vedisadatithirduroṇasannṛṣadvarasad*.
The Truth born from the ocean, born from the sky, born from the waters, born from the mountains, born from the cosmic order, born from the beginningless—Truth, the Great.

Having consecrated [the syllables] once with this mantra and recited them again, one should worship the letter *bra* in the middle of the causal [group] with "Obeisance to Brahmā" (*brahmaṇe namaḥ*). Then,
having worshipped the *ka*-group as the *kalā*s according to the method described in the previously mentioned *Kalāmātṛkā-nyāsa* with "Obeisance to Ka for creation" (*kaṃ sṛṣṭyai namaḥ*),
one should thereafter invoke the ten *kalā*s beginning with Old Age (*jarā*) into the *ṭa*-group, and perform the installation of their vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*) for them as before.
Your two strides are praised for their heroic power; like a terrifying wild beast, you move restlessly among the mountains.
Upon whose three wide strides all the worlds abide.

Having consecrated [the object] once with this *ṛc*, reciting it again, one should worship with "Obeisance to Viṣṇu" (*viṣṇave namaḥ*), and then worship the [deities] beginning with "Obeisance to Old Age" (*jarāyai namaḥ*). Then, having invoked the *kalās* beginning with Tīkṣṇā belonging to the *payavarga*, and having performed their *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* as before, one should recite:
"We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity."
May I be released from death, as a cucumber from its stem, into immortality.

Having thus consecrated [the syllable] and recited it again, one should worship with "Obeisance to Rudra" (*rudrāya namaḥ*). Then, having worshipped with "Obeisance to Tīkṣṇā" (*tīkṣṇāyai namaḥ*) and so forth, one should invoke the five-colored *kalās*—beginning with yellow and the rest—corresponding to the letters from *ṣa* to *kṣa*. Having performed the *prāṇapratiṣṭhā* for them as before, one should consecrate [the syllable] with the Gāyatrī and recite it again, worshipping with "Obeisance to Īśvara" (*īśvarāya namaḥ*), and [worship] *ṣaṃ* with "Obeisance to Pītā" (*pītāyai*).
Having worshipped [the deity] with "namaḥ" and so forth, one should then invoke the sixteen digits (kalās), beginning with Nivṛtti, and perform the installation of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā).

Then, for the mantra "Viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu," Tvaṣṭṛ is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), and Śrī Viṣṇu is the deity (devatā); its application (viniyoga) is for the purpose of chanting during the worship of Sadāśiva.
Therein, first, having drawn a triangle, a circle, and a square mandala on one's own left side, one should worship it with the root mantra using perfumes and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*).

Then, within the triangle, one should worship the three segments in clockwise order starting from the front. Within the square, one should worship the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) in the directions of Agni, Śā (South), Āsura (Nairṛta), Vāyu, and the center. Above that, having placed a copper or other vessel containing water, [one should contemplate] the digits of Fire, Sun, and Moon within the waters of the supporting vessel.

Having worshipped [the deity] in its collective form, one should place perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains (*akṣata*), and so forth into that water with the *praṇava*. Having worshipped it with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as before, one should display the *dhenumudrā*. This is the procedure for the worship of the general vessel (*sāmānyakalaśa*).
Now, one should perform the installation of the great vessel (*mahākalaśa*). Having sprinkled the ground on one's right side with the water from that vessel,

Having drawn a mandala consisting of a half-moon, a triangle, a circle, and a square with perfumed paste using the two hands joined in the *matsyamudrā*, and having placed scented substances, flowers, unbroken rice, and food in its center, one should recite:
*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ nārāyaṇyai ca vidmahe mahādevyai ca dhīmahi tanno lakṣmīḥ pracodayāt*.
Having thus worshipped in the center, one should worship the three segments within the triangle by proceeding clockwise from the front; then, in the circle:
*oṃ* 4 *namaḥ kāmarūpapīṭhāya*; in the half-moon: *oṃ* 4 *namaḥ jālandharapīṭhāya*.
In the square: 4 *oḍyāṇapīṭhāya namaḥ* (4). The universe, which exists pervading the unbroken circle, is that *maṇḍala* of Sadāśiva by which the three worlds are adorned.

Having worshipped with "Obeisance to the Pervasive Maṇḍala" (*vyāpakamaṇḍalāya namaḥ*), one should place upon it a support (*ādhāra*) made of gold or other materials, washed with the Weapon-mantra (*astra*).

Having worshipped it with "Obeisance to the Support of the Vessel, which is the Fire-maṇḍala consisting of ten digits (*kalā*) that bestows merit" (*aiṃ vahnimaṇḍalāya dharmaprada-daśakalātmane kalaśādhārāya namaḥ*), one should worship the ten digits of Fire thereon, proceeding clockwise from the front. They are as follows:
4 *yaṃ* to Dhūmrārcis, obeisance; 4 *raṃ* to Uṣmā, obeisance; 4 *laṃ* to Jvalinī, obeisance; 4 *vaṃ* to Jvālinī, obeisance;
4 *śaṃ* to Visphuliṅginī, obeisance; 4 *ṣaṃ* to Suśrī, obeisance.

Having worshipped with "4 saṃ surupāyai namaḥ," "4 haṃ kapilāyai namaḥ," "4 laṃ havyavāhāyai namaḥ," and "4 kṣaṃ kavyavāhāyai namaḥ," one should place upon it a vessel made of gold or other materials, washed with the Astra-mantra and perfumed with excellent incense.

In the center of that, having worshipped with "Oṃ klīṃ, obeisance to the great jar (mahākalaśa), the self of the twelve kalās that bestow wealth, belonging to the solar orb (arkamaṇḍala)," one should worship the twelve kalās of the Sun above it, proceeding clockwise from the front: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kaṃ bhaṃ, obeisance to Tapinī.
4 Khaṃ Baṃ, salutation to Tāpinī; 4 Gaṃ Phaṃ, salutation to Dhūmrā; 4 Ghaṃ Paṃ, salutation to Marīcī; 4 Ḍaṃ Naṃ, salutation to Jvālinī;
4 Caṃ Dhaṃ, salutation to Rūcī; 4 Chaṃ Daṃ, salutation to Suṣumnā.
4 jaṃ thaṃ, obeisance to Bhogadā; 4 jhaṃ taṃ, obeisance to Viśvā; 4 ñaṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to Bodhinī; 4 ṭaṃ ḍhaṃ, obeisance to Dhāriṇī;
4 ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, obeisance to Kṣamā. Having thus worshipped, [one should offer] that which is not stale and is perfumed with camphor and other fragrant substances.
Having brought pure substance, having sprinkled it with the root mantra and the *astra* mantra,

[one should recite]: "O Supreme Goddess, who resides within the wine, I worship You— the one who releases the bonds of the impurities of *āṇava* and the other *mala*s, who awakens the bliss of the Self-Bhairava, and who sports with speech consisting of prose and verse."

Having meditated thus, one should consecrate [the substance] eight times with the root mantra and perform the warding off of the ten defects: *Oṃ hrīṃ grāmacāṇḍālini, ward off, ward off the defect produced by fire, svāhā!* *Oṃ aiṃ kroṃ hsauṃ ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālini, come, come! Make thy presence manifest in this substance, make it manifest! Perform the warding off of the ten defects, perform it, svāhā!* Having struck [the substance] with unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) while forming the *yonimudrā*, [one should proceed].

Having purified [it] with: *saṃśodhya* 4 *paśupāśāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā*, and having worshipped with: 4 *paśupāśāya ānandabhairavāya huṃ phaṭ namaḥ*, one should consecrate it eight times with the root mantra (*mūla*) and recite: *hrāṃ hrīṃ jūṃ saḥ drāṃ drīṃ drūṃ damalavaraya ūṃ aiṃ ka e i ī va? hrīṃ śukraśāpaṃ vimocayāmi namaḥ*.

4 hrāṃ hrīṃ jūṃ saḥ yāṃ yīṃ yūṃ yamalavaraya ūṃ klīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ, I release [him] from the curse of Venus; obeisance. 4 hrāṃ hrīṃ jūṃ saḥ sāṃ sīṃ sūṃ samalavaraya ūṃ sauḥ sakala hrīṃ, I release [him] from the curse of Venus.

Namaḥ, 4 oṃ hrīṃ to Baṭuka, for the removal of calamities, perform, perform! To Baṭuka, hrīṃ, I release the curse of Baṭuka, namaḥ, 4 hasakṣamalavaraya ūṃ, obeisance to Ānandabhairava; 4 sahakṣamalavaraya īṃ, obeisance to Ānandabhairavī. (p.)

157) Having thus worshipped and while reciting the root mantra, one should fill the great jar (*mahākalaśa*) with that nectar and discard that vessel. Then, having worshipped with the mantra: "Oṃ *sauḥ*, obeisance to the nectar of the jar of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, who is the moon-maṇḍala, the bestower of desires, and whose self consists of sixteen digits," one should worship the sixteen digits of the Moon there itself, starting from the front and proceeding clockwise:
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aṃ, salutation to Amṛtā; 4 āṃ, salutation to Ānandā; 4 iṃ, salutation to Pūṣā; 4 īṃ, salutation to Tuṣṭi;
4 uṃ, salutation to Puṣṭi; 4 ūṃ, salutation to Rati.
4 Ṛṃ, salutation to Dhṛti; 4 Ṝṃ, salutation to Śaśinī;
4 Ḷṃ, salutation to Candrikā; 4 Ḹṃ, salutation to Kānti;
4 Eṃ, salutation to Jyotsnā; 4 Aiṃ, salutation to Śrī.
4 Oṃ, obeisance to Prīti; 4 Auṃ, obeisance to Aṅgadā;
4 Aṃ, obeisance to Pūrṇā; 4 Aḥ, obeisance to Pūrṇāmṛtā—having thus worshipped, [one worships] in the east:
4 Glūṃ, obeisance to Gaganalokaratna.
In the south—4 *slūṃ*, obeisance to the jewel of the heavenly realm (*svargaloka*); in the west—4 *plūṃ*, obeisance to the jewel of the subterranean realm (*pātālaloka*);
in the north—4 *mlūṃ*, obeisance to the jewel of the naga realm (*nāgaloka*).

In the center, having worshipped with the five jewels by saying "4 nlūṃ, obeisance to the Jewel of the Mortal World," one should meditate there upon the [triangle] resembling the rising sun, consisting of three lines, with the syllable *halakṣa* on its sides and *haṃsa* in the middle; then, in its center, [one should worship] "4 hasakṣamalavaraya ūṃ, obeisance to Ānandabhairava."
4 *sahakṣamalavaraya īṃ ānandabhairavyai namaḥ*, 4— having thus worshipped and displayed the *dhenumudrā*,
one should recite the *akhaṇḍa* and other mantras. As follows:

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! O you who produce the bliss of the undivided single essence, O Supreme Nectar-Self, O you whose form is Akula, bestow [your presence] through the mere spontaneous vibration of your own will!
O Supreme One, who abides in the non-clan (akula), whose form is nectar, and who brings about the knowledge of accomplishment—
place the state of immortality within this object, which has a moistened form.

Having made yourself one with my own form through the *arghya* offering, and having become that very essence, purify [me] and manifest the vibration of consciousness within me in the form of the nectar of the Kula.

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ hsauṃḥ jūṃ saḥ, O Immortal One, O Source of Nectar, O Mistress of Nectar, O Showerer of Nectar, cause nectar to flow, cause it to flow, svāhā! 4 Aiṃ, speak, speak, O Goddess of Speech! Aiṃ klīṃ, O Wet One, O Moistener, moisten; produce great agitation, produce it! Klīṃ sauḥ, [grant] liberation!
Kuru kuru | Sauṃḥ Hsauṃ 4 Oṃ Klīṃ, O Kula-Kāmadhenu, O Granter of Desires, cause the pure nectar to flow, cause it to flow!
Jūṃ Saḥ Svāhā | Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, [the nectar] produced from the fragments of the cosmic egg, filled with the entirety of essences.
Was the great vessel filled with the essence of nectar in the battle?
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! O Saṃvidā, born of Brahman, daughter of Brahman, ever sinless!
For the sake of the satisfaction of the Bhairavas, be forever pure.
Having displayed the seven mudrās beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*), [one says]: "Be invoked! Be established! Be made present! Be restrained! Be veiled! Be the granter of boons! Be gracious!

Then, having meditated upon the Goddess there, having consecrated her eight times with the root mantra, and having worshipped her with perfumes and other offerings, [one should act] near her as before.

Having placed the vessel of purification upon the mandala, having sprinkled it with the root mantra and the *astra* mantra, and having consecrated it eight times with the root mantra while forming the *dhenumudrā*, one should cast a piece of the purification substance the size of a black gram into the middle of the jar with the mantra *klīṃ namaḥ svāhā*. Then, holding the second piece with the left thumb and ring finger, [recite] *4 oṃ namo bhagavati*.

"O Mistress of the Village, O Daughter of Varuṇa, O You whose form is water, O Seizer of the upward-dripping drop, O Sovereign Mahālakṣmī, O You who dwell in the universal abode, O You who shine in the supreme ether, O Consumer of the Moon, Sun, and Fire! Come, come! Enter, enter! Take, take the substances for Your own enjoyment! Svāhā! With these words, one should cast the drop upward.
Then, having covered the jar with another vessel and holding the vessel for lifting in one's hand—
Having worshipped with "4 aghorāyai namaḥ," "4 sūkṣmāyai namaḥ," "4 ānandāyai namaḥ," and "4 śāntyai namaḥ," one should place [the vessel] upon the covering vessel.
This is the procedure for the installation of the great jar (mahākalaśa).

In front of the *kalaśa*, having drawn a mandala as before and worshipped it as before, one should place upon that mandala a support (*ādhāra*) washed with the *astra-mantra*. Then, having worshipped the support with: "4 *aiṃ* salutation to the support, whose self is the fire-mandala (*vahnimaṇḍala*), the giver of dharma, and the ten kalās," one should place upon it a conch (*śaṅkha*) washed with the *astra-mantra*. Then: "4 *klīṃ* salutation to the sun-mandala (*arkamaṇḍala*)... (p. 160)

Having worshipped with the mantra, "Obeisance to the general *arghya* vessel, whose self consists of twelve digits and bestows wealth," one should fill that vessel with fragrant, pure water. Then, having worshipped it with the mantra, "Obeisance to the lunar orb (*somamaṇḍala*), whose self consists of sixteen digits and bestows desires; obeisance to the nectar of the *arghya*," one should invoke the sacred water (*tīrtha*) from the solar orb (*savitṛmaṇḍala*) into it as before, and cast in sandalwood paste, flowers, and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) while reciting the *praṇava*.

Having poured a drop of nectar from the *kalaśa* and worshipped it with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as before, one should consecrate it eight times with the root mantra and display the conch, cow, and womb mudrās; this is the installation of the general *arghya*.
Now follows the installation of the special *arghya*. Therein, below the *kalaśa*, between one’s own right side and the deity, [one should proceed].

Having drawn seven mandalas either in the shape of a row or in the shape of circles, and having worshipped them as before, one should place there seven supporting vessels (*ādhārapātra*) made of gold or other materials, washed with the weapon-mantra (*astra*). Having filled them with the nectar of the jar (*kalaśāmṛta*), and having worshipped the digits (*kalā*) of Fire, Sun, and Moon within the waters of the supporting vessels, one should worship the digits of the *praṇava* in the *śrīpātra*. It is as follows:
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, and Sadāśiva—
these five deities are proclaimed as the kalās.
First is the *haṃsa* mantra of Prakṛti; immediately after that is *pratadviṣṇu*;
the third should be *tryambakam*; and the fourth begins with *tat-pada*.
The Viṣṇuyoni mantra shall be the fifth; let Manu be fashioned in five ways.
[One should employ] the three *tāras*, the Kumārī, Bhairavī, and the Bhairavī mantra.
One should [recite] Akhaṇḍā, Amṛteśī, Dīpanī, and Mūla respectively one,
two, three, four, five, two, and four times in sequence.
Having touched the vessel of worship, one should worship it with the *dhenumudrā*.

Reciting "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Namaḥ," one should place a piece of pure clay (*śuddhiśakala*) the size of a bean into each of the following: the *śrīpātra*, the *gurupātra*, the *śaktipātra*, the *bhogapātra*, the *śāntipātra*, the *ātmapātra*, and the *balipātra*. Then, having first displayed the *dhenumudrā* over the *śrīpātra*...
One should worship the Kalās beginning with Sṛṣṭi. It is as follows:

one should recite the Ṛgvedic verse, "haṃsaḥ śuciṣad... [RV 4.40.5]. Then: 4 Kaṃ to Sṛṣṭi; 4 Khaṃ to Ṛddhi; 4 Gaṃ to Smṛti; 4 Ghaṃ to Medhā; 4 Ṅaṃ to Kānti; 4 Caṃ to Lakṣmī; 4 Chaṃ to Dyuti; 4 Jaṃ to Sthirā; 4 Jhaṃ to Sthiti; 4 Ñaṃ to Siddhi.
Homage to the digits originating from the syllable *A*.
"May Viṣṇu protect us"—by this heroic power, like a formidable beast, he dwells in the mountains;
in whose three wide strides all the worlds abide.
4 Ṭaṃ to Jarā, 4 Ṭhaṃ to Pālinī, 4 Ḍaṃ to Śānti, 4 Ḍhaṃ to Īśvarī, 4 Ṇaṃ to Rati, 4 Taṃ to Kāmikā,
4 Yaṃ to Varadā, 4 Daṃ to Ahlādinī, 4 Dhaṃ to Prīti, 4 Naṃ to Dīrghā;
salutations to the digits (kalās) of Viṣṇu originating from the syllable *U*.
We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity.
May he deliver us from death as one releases a cucumber from its stem, yet not from immortality.

4 *Paṃ* to Tīkṣṇā, salutation; 4 *Phaṃ* to Raudrā; 4 *Baṃ* to Bhayā; 4 *Bhaṃ* to Nidrā; 4 *Maṃ* to Tandrayā; 4 *Yaṃ* to Kṣudhā; 4 *Raṃ* to Krodhinī; 4 *Laṃ* to Kriyā; 4 *Vaṃ* to Ulkāriṇī; 4 *Śaṃ* to Mṛtyu;
salutation to the Rudra-kalās originating from the letter *Ma*.
We meditate upon that excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he inspire our thoughts.
The wise ever behold that highest step of Viṣṇu,
like an eye fixed in the sky.
The wise, praising it and ever vigilant, kindle that which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu. *Saṃ* to the Yellow One;
*haṃ* to the White One; *laṃ* to the Red One; *kṣaṃ* to the Black One; *binduprabhava* (Obeisance to the powers of Īśvara arising from the Bindu).
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms.
May Prajāpati sprinkle [you]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you.
Conceive a fetus, O Sanī; conceive a fetus, O Vālinī; conceive a fetus for you, O Sarasvatī.
May the two divine Aśvins, who wear lotus-garlands, bestow a fetus upon you.
4 Aṃ, salutation to Nivṛtti; 4 Āṃ, salutation to Pratiṣṭhā; 4 Iṃ, salutation to Vidyā; 4 Īṃ, salutation to Śānti;
4 Uṃ, salutation to Indhikā; 4 Ūṃ, salutation to Dīpikā.
4 Ṛṃ, salutation to Recikā; 4 Ṝṃ, salutation to Mocikā; 4 Ḷṃ, salutation to Parā; 4 Ḹṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmā;
4 Eṃ, salutation to Sūkṣmāmṛtā; 4 Aiṃ, salutation to Jñānāmṛtā.
4 Oṃ, salutation to Āpyāyinī; 4 Oṃ, salutation to Vyāpinī;
4 Aṃ, salutation to Vyomarūpā; 4 Aḥ, salutation to Ānandā;
4, salutation to the Śiva-kalās originating from Nāda—having thus worshipped, and having formed the Dhenu-mudrā over the sequence of letters from 'a' to 'kṣa'.

Having recited the mantras beginning with Ānandabhairava and ending with Dīpinī, and having consecrated [the substance] eight times with the root mantra; then, having consecrated it with "4 klīṃ, O Kula-cow of desire, O granter of desires, pour forth, pour forth pure nectar! jūṃ saḥ svāhā," and having meditated upon the Goddess therein, worshipped her with perfumes and other offerings, displayed the Dhenu and Yoni mudrās, and recited "Born from a fragment of the Cosmic Egg."

Having consecrated the substance contained in another vessel with those drops of nectar (amṛtabindu), one should sprinkle oneself and the articles of worship; this is the procedure for the installation of the Śrīpātra.
To the right of the conch is the Śrīpātra, and to its right are the Gurus’ vessel, the Śakti’s vessel, the Peace vessel, the Enjoyment vessel, and the Bali vessel.

Having placed the *ātmapātra* in front of the *śrīpātra*, one should worship the mandalas of Fire, Sun, and Moon within those substances as a unified whole. Then, having added a measure of *māṣa*-weight of *śuddhi*, one should consecrate the *ātmapātra* eight times with the mantra: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ hrīṃ haṃ saḥ sohaṃ svāhā*. To its right, one should consecrate the *śāntipātra* four times with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).

Having consecrated the Guru-vessel eight times with "4 haṃ saḥ śivaḥ so'haṃ svāhā," having consecrated the Śakti-vessel eight times with "4 sauḥ," having consecrated the Bhoga-vessel eight times with the Vālā-mantra, and having consecrated the Bali-vessel eight times with the Baṭuka-mantra; then, having added a small amount of nectar from the Guru-vessel into one's own vessel, one should perform self-worship (*ātmapūjā*) with that.
One should perform [this].
Thus ends the fifth chapter, titled "The Procedure for the Arrangement of Vessels," in the *Svacchandapaddhati* composed by the illustrious Cidānandanātha. (p.
164) Now, at the entrance of the sacrifice, one should mutter the *tiraskāriṇī* [mantra]:

Of this Śrītiraskariṇī mantra: the venerable Durvāsas is the seer (ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandas), the goddess Śrītiraskariṇyambā is the deity (devatā), *īṃ* is the seed-syllable (bīja), *namaḥ* is the power (śakti), and *svāhā* is the pin (kīlaka). My application (viniyoga) is in recitation for the sake of attaining the grace of Tiraskariṇyambā.
*Namaḥ* to the Seer—on the head; *namaḥ* to the Meter—on the mouth.
Salutation to the Deity—at the heart; salutation to the Seed-syllable—at the right breast;
salutation to the Power—at the left breast; salutation to the Pin—at the navel; the Application—at the feet.

Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ īṃ, salutation to the two thumbs (aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ); 4, salutation to the two index fingers (tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ); 4, O Blessed One (bhagavatī), salutation to the two middle fingers (madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ);

4, O Great Illusion (mahāmāye), salutation to the two ring fingers (anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ); 4, perform, perform the eclipsing of the minds and eyes of all people (sarvajanamanaścakṣustiraskaraṇaṃ kuru kuru), salutation to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhikābhyāṃ).
*Namaḥ*, *svāhā*. Homage to both palms and backs of the hands.
4. Thus are the six limbs, beginning with the heart.
Meditation—
We worship her who has disheveled hair, who is naked yet adorned with all ornaments,
and who causes the multitude of bound souls to swoon upon beholding her own source. (1)
Mounted upon a blue horse, resplendent and adorned with blue garments, ornaments, garlands, and unguents,
veiling the worlds with her veil of sleep and armed with a sword— may that Blessed Lady protect me.
She is dark-complexioned, reeling with intoxication, her eyes clouded by passion;
she holds dates and a water-pot in her two enchanting arms.
Having meditated thus, one should display the mudrās:

*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to the sword-mudrā (khaṅgamudrā); four times, salutation to the jar-mudrā (kumbhamudrā); four times, salutation to the crown-mudrā (kirīṭamudrā); four times, salutation to the makara-tortoise (? mudrā (makarakacchapamudrā). Having worshipped with the five offerings (*pañcopacāra*), one should recite: *Īṃ namo*.
Having recited "O Bhagavatī Mahāmāyā, perform, perform the veiling of the minds and eyes of all people, svāhā," and having offered the recitation,

one should then adorn oneself with perfumes, unbroken rice grains, and flowers; meditating upon oneself in the form of the Goddess, one should prostrate to the Guru, Gaṇapati, and the Supreme Deity as before.
One should properly meditate upon Kuṇḍalinī, who is thinner than a fiber of lotus-stalk, extending from the base (mūlādhāra) to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra),
and resembling ten million moons in brilliance.

Having meditated upon the Guru on one's own head and worshipped him three times with the *pādukā* mantra, and having gratified him; then, having gratified the Goddess in the heart three times with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*);
and having visualized three lines behind the triangle situated at the head, one should worship the first line with:
"Obeisance to the sevenfold divine lineage (*divyaugha*) gurus beginning with Parākhya," and [worship] "the venerable *pādukā* of Paraprakāśānandanātha."
I worship, I satiate; salutations. 4.
I worship, I satiate; salutations to the venerable sandals of Paraśivānandanātha. 4. I worship, I satiate; salutations to the venerable sandals of the goddess Paraśaktidevyambā.
4. I worship the venerable sandals of Kauleśvarānandanātha; I satisfy them; obeisance. 4.
I worship the venerable sandals of Śuklādevyambā; I satisfy them; obeisance. 4. I worship the venerable sandals of Kuleśvarānandanātha; I satisfy them; obeisance.
"4 Kāmeśvarīdevyambā-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi namaḥ"—thus is the Divine Current (divyaugha).
Having worshipped and offered libations from the right to the left, one worships on the central line with:
"4 Parāparākhyebhyaḥ sva-tu-saṃkhyādi-siddhaugha-gurubhyo namaḥ. Thus, having worshipped.
I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Bhogānandanātha; obeisance!
I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Klinnānandanātha; obeisance!
I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Samayānandanātha; obeisance! (x4)
"I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Sahajānandanātha; obeisance. Thus is the Siddhaugha.
On the final line, having worshipped with: "Obeisance to the nine Gurus of the lineage beginning with the one named Apara."

4. I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Gaganānandanātha; salutations. 4. I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Viśvānandanātha; salutations. 4. I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Vimalānandanātha; salutations.

4. I worship, I satiate, I bow to the śrīpādukā of Madanānandanātha. 4. I worship, I satiate, I bow to the śrīpādukā of Bhuvanānandanātha. 4. I worship, I satiate, I bow to the śrīpādukā of Līlānandanātha.
4 Svātmānandanātha-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi namaḥ;
4 Priyānandanātha-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi namaḥ. Having thus worshipped and offered libations, [one says]:
To the cause that is the nature of the *haṃsa* and devoid of qualities, advaitānandanātha-śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi tarpayāmi namaḥ.

I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Paramānandanātha; obeisance! I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Siddhayogīśvarānandanātha; obeisance! I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Kavalīyānandanātha; obeisance! I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Haṃsānandanātha; obeisance!

I worship, I satiate, I bow to the venerable sandals of Amṛtānandanātha. I worship, I satiate, I bow to the venerable sandals of Brahmānandanātha. Haṃsa Śiva So'ham; I worship, I satiate, I bow to the venerable sandals of Vimalānandanātha, whose splendor is dissolved within the cage of the Self-delighting (Svātmārāma).
Therefore, for the sake of the awareness (*vimarśana*) of pure luminosity, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*) of Cidānandanātha; salutations!

Having uttered the Great Sandals (*mahāpādukā*): "I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of Vimalānandanātha, whose nature is the awareness of the supreme luminosity that is completely filled with pure luminosity; salutations!"

Having thus worshipped and offered libations to the three lines, and having worshipped and offered libations once to one's own *pādukā* at the *mūlādhāra*, [one recites] at the end of the root-mantra: *aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ ātmatattvena sthūladehaṃ pariśodhayāmi svāhā*;
*klīṃ ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ vidyātattvena sūkṣmadehaṃ pariśodhayāmi svāhā*.
sauḥ sakalahrīṃ, by means of the Śiva-tattva, I completely purify the causal body, svāhā;
aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ ka e ī la hrīṃ hasakahalahrīṃ sakalahrīṃ, by means of the Sarva-tattva, I completely purify the great causal body, svāhā.

Oṃ! May my prāṇa, apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna breaths be purified; may I become light, stainless, and free from passion—svāhā! Oṃ! May my earth, water, fire, air, and ether elements be purified; may I become light, stainless, and free from passion—svāhā!
Oṃ! May my primordial nature, ego, mind, and ears be purified; may I become light, stainless, and free from passion—svāhā! || 4 ||
Oṃ! May my speech, skin, tongue, nose, and intellect be purified; may I become light, stainless, and free from passion—svāhā! || 5 ||
Oṃ, may my hands, feet, private parts, and speech be purified; may I become light, stainless, and free from passion—svāhā! || 6 ||
Oṃ! May my touch, form, taste, smell, and space be purified; may I become light, stainless, and free from passion—svāhā! || 7 ||
Oṃ! May my wind, fire, water, and earth elements within myself be purified; may I become light, stainless, and free from passion—svāhā! || 8 ||
At the end of the root-mantra,

with the mind as the sacrificial ladle, I perpetually offer the functions of the senses as oblations into the fire of the Self, which is kindled by the fuel of dharma and adharma, via the path of the suṣumnā.

"Offer the substance accompanied by the mantra 'svāhā' into that which resides in the triangle at the root of one's own self, which possesses a brilliance equal to ten million suns and has the form of *kuṇḍalinī* consisting of consciousness (*cid-rūpa*).

Having thus offered the vessel of one's own self into the fire of consciousness through this visualization, one should contemplate the bliss of one's own self for a moment; such is the procedure for the worship of the self (*ātma-pūjā-vidhi*)."
Now, the worship of the Guru:

having meditated upon one’s own Guru in the center of the wheel— which consists of a square with four gates, an eight-petalled lotus, a circle, a hexagon, a triangle, and a point at the *dvādaśānta*— and having worshipped him with perfumes and other offerings and prostrated, [one offers] the substance contained in the Guru-vessel.
Having taken [the offering] in another vessel and having gratified it three times with the *pādukā* mantra, [one should offer it] with:
*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ klīṃ ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ sauḥ sakala hrīṃ*,
while supporting [the ladle] with the hands of light and space (*prakāśākāśa*) using the *unmanī* as the sacrificial spoon (*sruc*).
I offer the oil of the subtle parts of dharma and adharma into the full fire; svāhā!
Being of the nature of Śiva, I offer this supreme nectar—the "this-ness" (idantā) filled within the vessel of "I-ness" (ahantā)—into the fire that is supreme I-ness (parāhantā).

Thus, through this contemplation, having offered the substance into the fire whose nature is the supreme *ahantā* (I-consciousness) preceded by the remembrance of the venerable Guru, one should contemplate one's own self as transcending the universe; such is the procedure for the worship of the Guru.
O Lord of Devas, O Master Guru, O Teacher, O Leader of my own self!
Save me, save me, O ocean of compassion; make my recitation fully complete.
Having prayed thus and received permission from the venerable Guru, one should commence the Kula-worship:
"O venerable Guru, Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whose form is the grace bestowed upon devotees!
O Blessed One, grant me permission for the worship of the Śrīcakra."
By worshipping her according to the prescribed rite, one attains some incomparable success in action in this world and the granting of boons;
she fulfills every thought and the mental disposition of all practitioners.
I bow to Cintāmaṇi, the lord of the hosts of gods.
Holding a skull in his hand, wearing earrings, with a staff in his grasp, and having a young snake dark as twilight as his sacred thread—
he is the cause for severing obstacles during the worship at the time of sacrifice.
Victorious is Baṭukanātha, the bestower of accomplishments upon practitioners.
With hands adorned by skulls of black serpents, wearing a multitude of garlands of snakes and bees, with the deadly *kālākūṭa* poison situated upon his neck, and holding a lute made of skeletons;
he who is solely devoted to protecting the lineage's doctrine and who punishes those who oppose it— [I bow to him].
I bow to that venerable Kṣetrapāla in the form of a youth, who bestows the ornament of the crest-jewels upon the gods.
Clad in red garments, with a mass of tawny matted hair like molten gold, wielding a fierce, crooked staff encircled by a row of serpents,
and white as the shimmering peaks washed by the rays of the sun—
I bow to Baṭukanātha, the son of Gaurī.
Salutation to Rudra in the form of a Śarabha, who possesses eight feet, whose fierce and terrible form quivers, and who has cast aside the mountains with his wings.
In the ocean of nectar, on the island of jewels, radiant with groves of wish-fulfilling trees,
one should visualize a ruby pavilion illuminated by a perimeter of vajra-walls.

Having meditated with an undistracted mind upon oneself standing at the front of the pavilion— richly adorned with canopies of flower garlands, covered with fine cloths, radiant with camphor lamps, and fragrant with the scent of incense.

Having meditated thus, one should thereafter perform *prāṇāyāma*. Having recited the root mantra (*mūlavidyā*), one should draw in the breath through the left nostril; then, holding the nostrils with the little finger, the ring finger, and the thumb, while performing *kumbhaka* (retention), one should recite the root mantra four times. Meditating on the *kuṇḍalinī*, which is thinner than a lotus fiber, extending from the base up to the *brahmarandhra*, one should again recite and chant it twice. That...

One method is to exhale the air through the *piṅgalā* [nāḍī]. Another is to draw in the air through the *piṅgalā* in the same manner, perform *kumbhaka*, and then exhale through the *iḍā*. In this way, one should practice sixteen, thirty-two, sixty-four, or as many repetitions as possible, alternating the sequence.
Prāṇāyāma. Now, one should perform the worship of the Yoga-pīṭha:
at the Mūlādhāra—Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to the support of the Great Maṇḍūka.
At Svādhiṣṭhāna—4 oṃ kālāgnirudrāya namaḥ; at Maṇipūra—4 oṃ mūlaprakṛtyai namaḥ;
at the heart—4 oṃ ādhāraśaktayai namaḥ.
4. Homage to Kūrma; 4. Homage to Ananta; 4. Homage to Sārāha; 4. Homage to Pṛthivī; 4. Homage to the ocean of nectar, extending for a thousand koṭis of yojanas.

Homage to the one adorned with nine islands of nine jewels, shining with nine divisions extending for four hundred koṭis of yojanas; homage to the one with a rampart of puṣparāga gems; homage to the one with a rampart of padmarāga gems.
4. Homage to the perimeter wall of gomedaka jewels; 4. Homage to the perimeter wall of vajra jewels;
4. Homage to the perimeter wall of vaiḍūrya jewels.
4. Homage to the wall of sapphire gems; 4. Homage to the wall of pearl gems;
4. Homage to the wall of emerald gems.
4. Homage to the one whose rampart is made of coral jewels; 4. Homage to Kālacakreśvarī; 4. Homage to Mudrācakreśvarī;
4. Homage to Mātṛcakreśvarī; 4. Homage to Ratnacakreśvarī.
4. Obeisance to Deśacakreśvarī; 4. Obeisance to Tattvacakreśvarī;
4. Obeisance to Graha cakreśvarī; 4. Obeisance to Gurucakreśvarī;
4. Obeisance to Mūrticakreśvarī; 4. Obeisance to Svarṇaparvata.
4. Homage to Nandanodyāna; 4. Homage to Nānāvṛkṣamahodyāna; 4. Homage to Santānavāṭikā; (p. 173) 4. Homage to Kalpavṛkṣavāṭikā; 4.
Homage to Haricandanavāṭikā; 4. Homage to Pārijātavāṭikā.

4. Homage to Kadambavāṭikā; 4. Homage to Bilvavāṭikā; 4. Homage to the Seasons (Ṛtus); 4. Homage to the Horses of the Senses (Indriyāśvas); 4. Homage to the Elephants of the Objects of the Senses (Indriyārthaga jas); homage to the Great Moat of Ornamentation (Mahāśṛṅgāraparikhā).
4. Salutation to the Māṇḍikya pavilion; 4. Salutation to the pavilion of a thousand pillars; 4.
Salutation to the power (śakti) in the form of Time; 4. Salutation to the power in the form of Space;
4. Salutation to the power in the form of Ether; 4. Salutation to the power in the form of Sound.
4. Homage to the Saṅgita-yoginīs; 4. Homage to the Samastaprakaṭasiddhi-yoginīs; 4. Homage to Amṛtavāpikā; 4. Homage to Ānandavāpikā;
4. Homage to Vimarśavāpikā; 4. Homage to Bālātapodgara.
4. Homage to Candrikodgārā; 4. Homage to Mahāśṛṅgāraparikhā; 4. Homage to the goddess Mahāpadmā, who is three hundred thousand yojanas in extent;
4. Homage to Cintāmaṇigraharāja, who is one thousand yojanas in extent.

4. Salutation to the eastern gate consisting of the Eastern Tradition (Pūrvāmnāya). 4. Salutation to the southern gate consisting of the Southern Tradition (Dakṣiṇāmnāya). 4. Salutation to the western gate consisting of the Western Tradition (Paścimāmnāya).
4. Homage to the northern gate consisting of the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya). 4. Homage to the upper pinnacle consisting of the Upper Tradition (Ūrdhvāmnāya).
4. Homage to the altar-platform made of great jewels (mahāmaṇi).
4. Homage to the Jewel Lion Throne; 4. Homage to the White Parasol; 4. Homage to the Two White Whisks. On its four legs, in the four corners starting from the southeast (āgneya), [one should place]:
4. Homage to Dharma; 4. Homage to Jñāna.
4. Homage to Dispassion; 4. Homage to Sovereignty.
In the four directions starting from the east: 4. Homage to Unrighteousness; 4. Homage to Ignorance.
4. Salutation to Avairāgya (Non-detachment). 4. Salutation to Anaiśvarya (Lack of Sovereignty). 4. Salutation to Māyā. 4. Salutation to Vidyā. 4.
Salutation to Śeṣa, who is endowed with seventy coils and adorned with a thousand hoods.
4. Homage to the Root of Bliss (Ānandakanda). 4. Homage to the Stem of Consciousness (Saṃvinnāla). 4. Homage to the Great Lotus consisting of the thirty-six principles (Tattvas).
4. Homage to the petals composed of Primordial Nature (Prakṛti). 4. Homage to the filaments composed of the Transformations (Vikāra).
4 *Namaḥ* to the pericarp (*karṇikā*), which is enriched with the seed-syllables of the fifty letters and is the embodiment of all principles (*sarvatattva*).

4 *Aṃ*, *namaḥ* to the solar mandala (*arkamaṇḍala*). 4 *Uṃ*, *namaḥ* to the lunar mandala (*somamaṇḍala*). 4 *Maṃ*, *namaḥ* to the fire mandala (*vahni-maṇḍala*). 4 *Saṃ*, *namaḥ* to the quality of purity (*sattva*).
4 Raṃ, obeisance to Rajas; 4 Taṃ, obeisance to Tamas; 4 Āṃ, obeisance to the Self (Ātman); 4 Aṃ, obeisance to the Inner Self (Antarātman);
4 Paṃ, obeisance to the Supreme Self (Parātman); 4 Hrīṃ, obeisance to the Knowledge-Self (Jñānātman).
4 *vidyātattvātmane namaḥ*, 4 *paratattvātmane namaḥ*, 4.
Upon that seat of yoga (*yogapīṭha*), upon the filaments in the eight directions and in the center—
one should first contemplate one's own body in the form of the Śrīcakra.
Free from the forms of skin and the other [elements], it resembles the blazing fire of cosmic destruction.
The baindava [cakra] is at the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra), and by its contraction it becomes a triangle;
the eight-spoked wheel is on the forehead, and the ten-spoked wheel is between the eyebrows.
There is a twelve-petaled lotus at the throat, a sixteen-petaled lotus at the heart,
an eight-petaled lotus at the navel, and a six-petaled lotus at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*.

One should contemplate the Śrīcakra upon its foundation as being square; it is endowed with the Bindu, the Triangle, the eight directions, the descent of the four, the world-enclosures, the lotus-petals, the two circles,
the eight petals, the sixteen-fold circle, and the three earth-abodes— such is the Cakra I worship.

I worship and satisfy with libations the Śrīpādukā of all the deities residing within the Śrīcakra— the most secret of all manifest and hidden traditions, the Kula, Kaula, Nigarbha, and the secrets, supreme secrets, and ultra-secrets of the Yoginīs; salutations!
Having meditated upon a circle, a square, and a lotus pericarp within that drop, and having visualized a six-cornered figure containing a square at its center:
"Lāṃ, salutation to Brahmā, the lord of the earth, whose essence is the Nivṛtti-kalā; I worship and satiate the venerable sandal of the Brahman-preta-throne; salutation."
4 Vāṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu, the lord of waters, whose self is the *pratiṣṭhā*-kalā; I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*) upon the Rudra-preta-throne; salutation.
(p. 176) 4 Rāṃ, salutation to Rudra, the lord of fire, whose self is the *vidyā*-kalā; [I worship] the Rudra-preta-throne.
I worship the venerable sandals; I satiate them; obeisance.
(4 times) Obeisance to Īśvara, the lord of the northwest, whose nature is the power of peace; I worship the venerable sandals on the throne of the Īśvara-preta; I satiate them; obeisance.
4 Hsauṃḥ! Salutation to Sadāśiva, the lord of the ether, whose self is the Kalā beyond peace (Śāntyatīta).
I worship and satiate the Śrī-pādukā of the great ghost (Mahāpreta) seat of Sadāśiva; salutation!
Above that, on the six-cornered pedestal (Ṣaṭkoṇapīṭha), starting from the front and proceeding clockwise—
4 aṃ āṃ sauḥ, I worship the venerable sandals of Tripurāsudhārṇavāsanā; I satisfy them; obeisance!
4 aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ, I worship the venerable sandals of Tripureśvarī, whose seat is the lotus of the womb.
I satiate; salutation.
4 Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā of the self-seat of the Goddess Tripurasundarī; salutation.
4 HAIṂ HKLĪṂ HSAUḤ, I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā of Tripuravāsinī, seated upon all the cakras; obeisance.
4 HSAIṂ HSKLĪṂ HSAUḤ, I worship the Śrīpādukā of Tripurāśrī, seated upon all mantras.
I satisfy [you], obeisance!
4 Hrīṃ Klīṃ Bleṃ, I worship and satisfy with libations the venerable sandals of Tripuramālinī on the Sādhya-Siddha seat; obeisance!
Then, in the square of the central seat (*madhyapīṭha*), one should worship the four seats together with the four seats [of the other directions].

In the northeast: *Aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ*, [you who reside] in the fire-wheel (*agnicakra*) at the abode of Kāmagiri, whose essence is Lord Mitrīśanātha, who preside over the waking state (*jāgraddaśā*), and whose nature is the power of will (*icchāśakti*), the Śakti of Rudra.
Kāmeśvarī Devī, Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, Tripurasundarī; I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā of the Self-seat of the Goddess; obeisance!
In the northwest—4 Klīṃ Hasakahalahrīṃ—in the Sūrya-cakra at the Jālandhara-pīṭha.

O Goddess Vajreśvarī, whose essence is Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha, who presides over the state of dreaming, whose nature is the power of knowledge (jñānaśakti), and whose self is the power of Viṣṇu; HAIṂ HKLĪṂ HSAUṂḤ Tripuravāsinī, I worship and satiate the Śrī-pādukā seated upon all the wheels (cakras); obeisance!

In the southwest: *Sauḥ*, *sakalahrīṃ*. In the lunar wheel (*somacakra*) at the cave of Pūrṇagiri, whose essence is Oḍḍīśanātha and which presides over the state of deep sleep (*suṣupti*), I worship the Goddess Bhagamālinī—the Śakti who is the Brahman-self consisting of the power of action (*kriyāśakti*)—*hsaiṃ hsklīṃ hsauṃḥ*; the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*) of Tripurāśrī, the seat of all mantras. I worship.
I offer libation; obeisance!

To Agneyi: 4 Aiṃ Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ Klīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Sauḥ Sakala Hrīṃ, in the wheel of the Supreme Brahman (parabrahmacakra), at the seat of Mahoḍyāṇa (mahoḍyāṇapīṭha), O you whose essence is Śrī Caryānātha, the presiding deity of the fourth state (turyadaśādhiṣṭhāyaka).

I worship and satiate with offerings the venerable goddess Tripurasundarī, who transcends the four states of waking, dreaming, deep sleep, and the fourth (turya), who is beyond the cessation of the powers of will, knowledge, and action, and whose essence is power; Hrīṃ Klīṃ Bleṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable goddess Tripuramālinī, the Śrī-pādukā upon the Sādhya-siddha seat; obeisance!
In the middle of the *Mantramahodadhi*, he states a specific detail (p.

178): having uttered [the letters] from *a* to *kṣa* along with the bindu (*m*), at the end of the root-vidyā, [one recites] Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, Śuddhavidyā, Māyā, Kalā, Vidyā, Rāga, Kāla, Niyati, Puruṣa, and Prakṛti.

I worship and satiate with offerings the Śrīpādukā of the Yogapīṭha of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who consists of ego, intellect, mind, hearing, touch, sight, taste, smell, speech, hands, feet, anus, genitals, sound, touch, form, taste, smell, ether, air, fire, water, and earth; obeisance!
In the *Mantramahodadhi*:

having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) starting with *aiṃ* for the Supreme Goddess (*parā*) as before, and then having taken flowers with the *trikhaṇḍā* mudrā, [one should visualize] the Goddess, thinner than a lotus fiber, from the root [of the feet] up to the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*).
One should visualize her as having arrived among the flowers placed upon the tips of the three segments: "Obeisance to the Blessed One, Śrī Mahātripurasundarī!
Come, come, O Goddess of the lords of gods, O Tripurā, worshipped by the gods!"
O you who delight in wine and meat, quickly grant your presence for the sake of accomplishment.
O Supreme Goddess, who dwells within the Great Lotus Grove, whose form is the bliss of the cause, and who exists for the welfare of all beings, come, please come!

Aiṃ, may we know Vāgīśvarī; Klīṃ, may we meditate on Kāmeśvarī; Sauḥ, may that Śakti inspire us. Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Sa Ka La Hrīṃ Sauḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ha Sa Ka La Ra Ḍaiṃ Ha Sa Ka La Ra.

Ḍīṃ Ha Sa Ka La Ra Ḍauṃ Hsraiṃ Hsklīṃ Hsrauḥ Śrīṃ Bhagavatī Śrīmahātripurasundarī āgaccha āgaccha asmin śrīcakramadhye sānnidhyaṃ kuru kuru svāhā. Having uttered each individual segment [of the mantra], one should cast a flower placed upon each respective segment.
O Goddess of gods, easily accessible through devotion, endowed with all protective enclosures—
remain steadfast here as long as I worship you.
Having displayed the seven mudrās beginning with the invocation (*āvāhana*), having performed the ritual of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) as before,

having established the binding of the ten directions (*daśadigbandhana*) with the *astra* mantra, and having performed the three pervasive applications (*vyāpakatraya*) from the head down to the feet with the root mantra, one should consecrate [the deity] with nectar (*amṛtīkṛta*) by means of the cow-mudrā (*dhenumudrā*) upon the head of the deity.

One should perfect [the deity] by means of the Mahāmudrā. Having recited the *Mūlavidyādīpinīmālinī*, one should sprinkle [the image] with the water of the general *arghya* offering; this is the purification of the deity (*devaśuddhi*).
Now, the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*): ĀṂ HRĪṂ KRAUṂ YA RA LA VA ŚA ṢA SA HO HAṂSAḤ SOHAṂ.

Svāhā! May all the senses of Tripurasundarī come here; may they remain happily for a long time, Svāhā! Ya Ra La Va Śa Ṣa Sa Hoṃ Svāhā! Kroṃ Hrīṃ Āṃ—having touched the heart, one should recite this three times.
One should meditate upon Bhavānī as ruddy-hued, her eyes rippling with compassion, holding a noose, a goad, a flower-arrow, and a bow,
and surrounded by the rays of powers such as *aṇimā* and the rest— perceiving her simply as "I."
Thus, having meditated on the unity of oneself, one should display the thirteen mudrās beginning with Saṃkṣobhiṇī:
"4 Drāṃ, I display the Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī mudrā; 4 Drīṃ, I display the Sarvavidrāviṇī mudrā."
4 *klīṃ*, I display the Sarvākarṣiṇī mudrā; 4 *blūṃ*, I display the Sarvavaśaṅkarī mudrā; 4 *saḥ*, I display the Sarvonmādinī mudrā.
4 *Kroṃ*, I display the seal of the Great Goad of All; 4 *Hskhphreṃ*, I display the seal of the Sky-Wanderer of All; (p. 181) 4 *Hsauḥ*, I display the seed-syllable seal of All.
4 Aiṃ, I display the Sarvayonimudrā;
Kroṃ Hrīṃ, I display the Aṅkuśamudrā to Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, who are the embodiments of hatred.
4 Āṃ Hrīṃ! To Rāgātmābhyām, Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, I display the Pāśa-mudrā.
4 Drāṃ Drīṃ Klīṃ Blūṃ Saḥ Yāṃ Rāṃ Lāṃ Vāṃ Śāṃ.
By means of the two [deities] whose nature consists of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, I display the flower-arrow mudrā; 4.
by means of the two [deities] whose nature consists of wind and fire, Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, [I display] the sugarcane-bow mudrā.
I display it; I display the crown mudrā;
I display the makara-earring mudrā.
Having thrice satiated [the deity] with the nectar from the Śrīpātra using the root mantra,
one should meditate upon Lalitāmbā, who is red in hue, holding a bow, a noose, and a goad in her hands, joyful, and restrained within the lap of Kāmarāja.
I offer a seat to the sandals of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī.
I offer a welcome; I offer water for the feet;
I offer the respectful offering (arghya); I offer water for sipping (ācamana).

4. I prepare the madhuparka; 4. I prepare the water for sipping again; 4. I prepare the bath with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta); 4. I prepare the bath with pure water; 4. I prepare the garment; 4. I prepare the sacred thread (yajñopavīta).

I arrange all ornaments, such as the auspicious thread (*maṅgalasūtra*) and so forth; I arrange the crown; I arrange the crocodile earrings (*makarakuṇḍala*); I arrange perfume; I arrange unbroken grains (*akṣata*); I arrange flowers.

Having placed charcoal into the incense-holder with the mantra *klīṃ tat tejase namaḥ*, and having cast aloeswood, guggulu, and the ten-ingredient incense (*daśāṅga*) [into it], one should worship the bell with the *astra-mantra*. Then,
having consecrated it with the mantra *jagadhvanimandramātaḥ svāhā*, one should [recite] softly while ringing the bell.

Having placed [the incense] on the left side of the Goddess with the words "I prepare the incense," and having inserted a camphor-filled wick soaked in ghee into the hand of the lamp-bearer while reciting the root mantra,
one should place it on the right side of the Goddess with the words "I prepare the lamp for Śrī Mahātripurasundarī."
In front of the Goddess, having drawn a square mandala with the Astra-mantra using water from the general arghya vessel,

and having placed upon it various kinds of food— eatables, chewables, lickables, drinkables, and suckables, such as grains, fruits, cakes, and so forth— in a vessel made of gold or other materials along with its stand, one should sprinkle the food offering (naivedya) with the Astra-mantra and the water from the general arghya.

O Deva Savitṛ, by your impulsion, I sprinkle [the water] with truth through the Ṛta; having protected it with the Cakra-mudrā and rendered it poisonless with the Tārkṣya-mudrā, one should consecrate it eight times with the root mantra, bind the Dhenu-mudrā, and recite:
*klīṃ kāmadughe varade vicce sphura sphura amṛteśvarī*.

Having rendered the food offering (*naivedya*) immortal by means of the *vidyā*, and having rendered it supreme by means of the *mahāmudrā*, one should perform the water for the feet (*pādya*) and so forth, as well as the sipping of water (*ācamana*), for the Goddess as before. Then, taking water in the hollowed palms, reciting the root mantra, and saying,
"I offer the food offering to the venerable Mahāsundarī," one should pour out the water from the hollowed palms over the food offering.
Having touched with both hands the divine, excellently prepared supreme rice-milk (paramānna) contained in the golden vessel—
endowed with five textures and six flavors— accept it, O Supreme Goddess!

Having recited this, and having consecrated the water as nectar (amṛta) with another vessel, having offered it with the mantra "amṛtopastaraṇam asi svāhā," and having displayed the five mudrās beginning with Prāṇa, one should take a flower and [offer it] into the excellent vessel: "The excellent oblation, bliss, and various manifold foods."
I offer this to you, O Goddess, together with your attendants; may you accept it.

Having thus offered the flower to the Goddess and having satiated the Goddess three times with the root mantra, [one recites]: *Aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ*, "I worship and satiate the Śrīpādukā of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades the Ātmatattva;
obeisance. *Klīṃ ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ*, [to her] who pervades the Vidyātattva...

I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī; obeisance! Sauḥ, sakalahrīṃ, I worship and satisfy the venerable sandals of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, who pervades the principle of Śiva (śivatattva); obeisance!

Having consecrated the water in another vessel as nectar: "Homage to you, O God, O Goddess of gods! This supreme drink, which brings total satisfaction, is pure, natural, and very cool; it is now offered."
"Accept this excellent water, filled with supreme bliss.
Having thus offered the water, performed the binding of the ten directions with the *astra-mantra*,
and veiled the path of vision with a cloth, he should ring the bell with his left hand while the Goddess is eating.
One should meditate [on her] as she is being fanned on all sides by her friends, who are seated comfortably around her with Brahmā, Śiva, and others,
and who are waving a multitude of yak-tail fans that produce a pleasant sound.
The Source of the Universe, smiling as He plays with His armor, eats the six flavors from a golden vessel in a row.
Having thus meditated after eating, having recited the root mantra ten times and offered the recitation,
and having consecrated the water as nectar as before, he gives the *uttarāpośana* with the mantra "Thou art the covering of nectar" (*amṛtāpidhānam asi*).
Having completed the remaining rites with the root mantra, he offers betel-leaf with the root mantra using the *yonimudrā*.
One should prostrate.

Having performed the six-limbed placement (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) as before, and having displayed the fifteen mudrās beginning with Saṃkṣobhiṇī, one should satisfy [the deity] three times with the root mantra and perform [the rite]: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*.
O Supreme Goddess, composed of consciousness, O Beloved who delights in the essence of supreme nectar,
O Tripurā, grant me permission to worship your retinue.
Having meditated upon that very [energy] of one's own as having transformed into the form of the deities of the Śrīcakra in the form of rays,
one should worship those deities.
Thus, in the *Svacchandapaddhati* composed by the venerable Cidānandanātha.
The sixth spanda, titled "The Brief Ritual of Worship. || 6 ||

The three *tāras*—*oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*—should be joined at the beginning of every mantra. Having recited the root-vidyā as *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aḥ*, one should offer libations three times with the formula: "I worship and satisfy the sandals of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī;
obeisance. Then, regarding the worship of the *tithi-nityās* upon the lines of the triangle therein:

Beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight (śukla-pratipad) until the full moon (paurṇimā), one should worship each of the fifteen Nityās— starting with Kāmeśvarī and ending with Citrā— as the Tithinityā within their respective mandalas, dedicating one Nityā to each lunar day. Therein, one should worship the Tithinityā according to the prescribed rite during the dark fortnight (kṛṣṇapakṣa).

In the same manner, one should worship [the deities] in direct order (anuloma), beginning with Citrā and ending with Kāmeśvarī. In this regard, when there is an increase in lunar days (tithi-vṛddhi), one should worship two Nityās on a single lunar day; when there is a decrease in lunar days (tithi-kṣaya), one should worship two Nityās on a single lunar day. Herein lies the established Tantric doctrine: that the lunar day which extends across sunrise alone is what truly pervades the entire day and night (ahorātra).
Having performed the worship of the *tithinityās* within that *bindu*, one should worship as follows in the triangle by moving counter-clockwise:
on the right line—*aṃ, āṃ, iṃ, īṃ, uṃ*; on the eastern line—*ūṃ, ṛṃ, ṝṃ, ḷṃ, ḹṃ*; and on the northern line—*eṃ, aiṃ, oṃ, auṃ, aṃ*. Thus [the five vowels].
Having visualized the fifteen vowels within three lines, one should worship the fifteen Nityās, beginning with Kāmeśvarī, upon those vowels with their respective Vidyās. It is as follows:
Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Aṃ Aiṃ Sakala Hrīṃ Nityaklinne Madadrave Sauḥ Aṃ.
I worship and satiate the Śrīpāduka of the Nityā Śrī Kāmeśvarī; obeisance.
(p. 187) 4 ĀṂ AIṂ Bhaga-bhüge bhagini bhagodari bhagamāle bhagāvahe bhagaguhye bhagayoni bhaganipātini sarvabhagavaśaṅkari bhagarūpe nityaklinne bhagasvarūpe.
O Bestower of Boons, bring all my *bhagas* here; O Excellent One, O Beautiful One, O She who moistens the *bhaga*, O She whose fluid is moist, make them wet, make them flow!

O Infallible One, O Goddess of the *bhaga*, agitate, cause all living beings to tremble, O Mistress of the *bhaga*! Aiṃ Blūṃ Jaṃ Blūṃ Bheṃ Moṃ Blūṃ Heṃ! O Moist One, bring all my *bhagas* under my control!
Strīṃ hrīṃ āṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of the Nityā Bhagamālinī; namaḥ. (4 times) Iṃ hrīṃ nityaklinne madadrave svāhā, I worship the venerable sandals of the Nityā Nityaklinnā.
I worship, I satisfy, obeisance!

4 uṃ ūṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to Vahnivāsinī; uṃ, I worship and satiate the Śrī-pādukā of the Nityā Vahnivāsinī, obeisance. 4 ūṃ hrīṃ klinne aiṃ kroṃ nityamadadrave hrīṃ ūṃ, [obeisance to] Mahāvajreśvarī Nityā.
I worship and satiate the venerable sandals; salutation.
(4 times) *Ṛṃ hrīṃ* salutation to Śivadūtī. *Ṛṃ*, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of the Nityā Śivadūtī; salutation.

Namaḥ,

4 Aiṃ Bhamarayūṃ Aiṃ, I worship and satiate the venerable sandals of the eternal Vijayā.

4 Oṃ ūṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, Jvālāmālinī, Goddess of gods, you who cause the destruction of all beings, O Jātavedasī! Blaze, blaze, blaze; flare up, flare up! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! Ra ra ra ra ra ra ra!
O Jvālāmālinī, huṃ phaṭ svāhā! Oṃ, the eternal Jvālāmālinī, the venerable pādukā.
I worship, I satiate; *namaḥ*.
(4 times) *Aṃ* *kauṃ* *aṃ*, I worship, I satiate, *namaḥ* to the venerable sandals of the eternal goddess Citrā Nityā. (4 times).
Having thus worshipped the fifteen eternal goddesses (*nityās*) by circling counter-clockwise and having satiated them with drops from the *śrīpātra*, [one recites] *aḥ*.
With the root mantra: "I worship and satiate the *śrīpādukā* of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī; obeisance.

Having thus worshipped and satiated the fifteen *nityās* by circling counter-clockwise, one should utter the fourth Vidyā (*turyavidyā*)—namely, *aḥ*—in the *bindu* in their center, followed by *ha sa ka la ha sa ka ha la sa ka la hrīṃ*, [and then] Śrī Mahātripurasundarī.
I worship the venerable sandals; I satiate them; obeisance! (p.

189) Again, as before, one should offer and satiate the lunar-day Nityā with perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings, presenting the specific food offering appropriate for that particular lunar day.

Then one should worship the lineage of gurus (*gurupaṅkti*). It is as follows: on the head, within the space behind the triangle, between Vimalā and Jayinī, one should visualize three lines along the front line [of the triangle].
Having satiated the three currents (*ogha*) and the gurus of the tradition (*sampradāya*) as before, one should satiate the Goddess three times with the root mantra (*mūla*).

Following the lineage of the Gurus of Kāmarāja, one should worship and satisfy the six-limbed young maidens (ṣaḍaṅgayuvatī), beginning with Sarvajñā, in the directions— namely Agni, Īśāna, Asura, Vāyu, and the center— outside the triangle; [here,
instead of "śrī," one should say] "I worship and satisfy the Śrīpādukā, obeisance."
4 Aiṃ, the Goddess Sarvajñā Śrī; 4 Klīṃ, the Goddess Nityatṛptā Śrī.
4 Sauḥ, O Goddess Śrī Anādibodhā;
4 Sauḥ, O Goddess Śrī Sthatantrā(?);
4 Klīṃ, O Goddess Śrī Nityamaluptā.

4 Aiṃ Anantā Devī Śrī... Having thrice satiated the Goddess with the root mantra (mūla), and having offered a handful of flowers while reciting "Samasta-prakaṭa," [one should offer] 4 Aṃ Āṃ Sauḥ: "Salutation to the Trailokyamohana-cakra."
Having worshipped with "Oṃ, salutation to the line beginning with the square," then follows the Eastern Tradition (Pūrvāmnāya):
4 Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, Bālā Śrī; 4 Hsaiṃ Hsklīṃ Hsauḥ, Sampatpradā Bhairavī Śrī.
4 SHAṂ SAKALAHRĪṂ SRHAUṂḤ CAITANYABHAIRAVĪ ŚRĪ0; 4 SHAṂ SAKALAHRĪṂ NITYAKLINNE MADADRAVE SRHAUṂḤ KĀMEŚVARĪ RUDRĀṆĪ ŚRĪ0;
4 HSRAĪṂ SRHĪṂ ŚRĪṂ SAKALAHRĪṂ ŪRMIṆĪ ŚRĪ0.
In the wheel that deludes the three worlds, which fulfills all hopes,
and in the wheel that agitates all, one should worship the Eastern Tradition.
Now, the Dakṣiṇāmnāya: 4 HSKHPHREṂ HSKLĪṂ HSAUṂ RUDRABHAIRAVĪ ŚRĪ0;
4 AGHORE AIṂ AGHORE HRĪṂ GHORA GHORATAREBHYE SARVE SARVĀDHIDEVATE NAMASTE.
In the form of *drā*, *hsauṃ* Aghorabhairavī Śrī;
4 *aiṃ klīnne klīṃ madadrave kule hsauṃ* Bhoginī Śrī.
In the wheel that bestows all prosperity (*sarvasaubhāgyada*) and likewise in the wheel that accomplishes all aims (*sarvārthasādhaka*).
One should worship the Wheel that Produces All Protection according to the Southern Tradition.
Now, the Western Tradition (Paścimāmnāya):
4 Ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-haiṃ Ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-hīṃ Ḍa-ra-la-ka-sa-hauṃḥ Śrī Ṣaṭkūṭabhairavī;
4 Ha-sa-ka-la-ra-ḍaiṃ Ha-sa-ka-la-ra-ḍīṃ Ha-sa-ka-la-ra-ḍauṃḥ Śrī Nityābhairavī.
4 Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Bhagavatyamba Hsphreṃ Hskhphreṃ Kubjike Hsrīṃ Srhīṃ Hsrūṃ Srhūṃ Aghore Ghore Aghoramukhi Chrāṃ Chrīṃ Kiṇi Kiṇi Vicce Hsrauṃ Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Kubjikā Śrī.
In the middle wheel, now follows the Northern Tradition (Uttarāmnāya):
4 hsaiṃ ha sa ka la hrīṃ hsauṃ Bhuvaneśvarabhairavī Śrī0;
(p. 191) 4 oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namo bhagavatī māheśvari annapūrṇe svāhā.
Aṇṇapūrṇā Śrī,
4 ŚAIṂ Sakalahrīṃ ŚAUṂ Sakaleśvarabhairavī Śrī, SRAHEṂ (? ŚAUṂ Siddhakauleśvarabhairavī Śrī.

O Goddess, one should worship the Kaubera-āmnāya within the nine wheels (*navacakra*). Now follows the Ūrdhva-āmnāya:
Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauḥ ūṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ sauḥ aiṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ. This is the Śrī Kāmarāja-vidyā. Śrī. || 1 ||
Śrīṃ ha sa ka la hrīṃ ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ sakalahrīṃ sauḥ Lopāmudrā Śrī. || 2 ||
Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauḥ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ka ha e ī la hrīṃ ha ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ sa sa sa sa ka ha la hrīṃ sauḥ aiṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ; this is the Śrī-manuvidyā. || 3 ||
4 Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sa Ha Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ Sa Ha Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Sa Ha Sa Ka La Hrīṃ Sauḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ. This is the Candravidyā of Śrī. || 4 ||
4. Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauḥ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ha sa ka e ī la hrīṃ ha sa ka ha ha la hrīṃ ha sa sa ka la hrīṃ sauḥ aiṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ. This is the Kubera-vidyā, Śrī. || 5 ||
4 Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ka E Ī La Hrīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Sa Ha Sa Ka La Hrīṃ Sauḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ. This is the Agastyavidyā, Śrī. 6.
4 Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sa E Ī La Hrīṃ Sa Ha Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Sakala Hrīṃ Sauḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ. This is the Nandikeśvara-vidyā, Śrī. || 7 ||
(p. 192) 4 Śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ aiṃ sauḥ oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ ha sa ka ha la hrīṃ sakalahrīṃ sauḥ aiṃ klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ. This is the Indravidyā of Śrī. || 8 ||

4 Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ha Sa Ka La Hrīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Sa Ka La Hrīṃ Sa E Ī La Hrīṃ Sa Ha Ka Ha La Hrīṃ Sa Ka La Hrīṃ Sauḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Viṣṇu-vidyā Śrī. || 11 ||
Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Aiṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ka E Ī La Ha Rīṃ Ha Sa Ka Ha La Ha Rīṃ Sa Ka La Ha Rīṃ Sauḥ Aiṃ Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ. This is the Durvāsas-vidyā, O Śrī. 12.
Thus ends the division of the twelve root-mantras (mūlavidyā). One should worship the central lion-throne within the point (bindu).
There should be incense, lamps, and food offerings (naivedya). Furthermore, on the first line [of the diagram] are Aṇimā and the others;
on the middle line are Brāhmī and the others; and on the third line are Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī and the others.
And the sequence of worship:
having thus worshipped [the deities] in the wheel of persistence (*sthiticakra*), one should satisfy the entirety of Śrīvidyā.
Furthermore, one should offer libations three times with the root mantra.
Then one should perform the limb-consecration (*aṅgāvaraṇa*) arising from the Śrīvidyā mantra:
*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ ka e ī la hrīṃ*, *namaḥ* to the heart; [one should place] the Goddess Śrī in the heart, in the southeast (*āgneya*).
4 *klīṃ* *ha sa ka ha la* *hrīṃ* *śirase svāhā*; Śirodevī Śrī—[in] the Īśānya [direction]. 4 *sauḥ* *sakala hrīṃ* *śikhāyai vaṣaṭ*; Śikhādevī Śrī—[in] the Nairṛtya [direction].

Having offered incense and lamps, [proceed] by circumambulating the right side of the door.

4 Āṃ Brāhmī Śrī, 4 Īṃ Māheśvarī Śrī,

4 Drāṃ, the goddess of the Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī Mudrā, Śrī; 4 Drīṃ, the goddess of the Sarvavidrāviṇī Mudrā, Śrī;
4 Klīṃ, the goddess of the Sarvākarṣaṇī Mudrā, Śrī.
4 blūṃ, O Goddess of the Sarvavaśaṅkari Mudrā, Śrī; 4 saḥ, O Goddess of the Sarvonmādinī Mudrā, Śrī;
4 kroṃ, O Goddess of the Sarvamahāṅkuśā Mudrā, Śrī.
4 HSKHPHREṂ, Śrī Sarvakhecarīmudrādevī; 4 HSAUḤ, Śrī Sarvabījamudrādevī;
4 AIṂ, Śrī Sarvayonimudrādevī.
4 Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, the Goddess Sarvatrikhaṇḍāmudrā, Śrī [Oṃ]. To her right—4 Aṃ Āṃ Sauḥ, Tripurācakreśvarī, Śrī. To her right—4 Aṇimāsiddhi, Śrī.
On the left: 4 drāṃ, the goddess of the Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇīmudrā, Śrī;
