Having satiated the Goddess three times with the root mantra, and having displayed the *drāṃ*— the *sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī* mudrā— one should take the water of the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*) together with perfumes, unbroken rice grains, and flowers, and recite: "These manifest Yoginīs in the *trailokyamohana* wheel, together with their mudrās, their siddhis, and their śaktis..."

"May the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, together with her weapons, vehicles, retinues, and the Mistress of the Cakra (Cakreśvarī), be worshipped and gratified with all ritual offerings; *namaḥ*. Having thus offered the worship by pouring that water into the left hand for the Mistress of the Cakra, [one should proceed].
O You who are affectionate toward those who have come for refuge, grant me the fulfillment of my desired goal;
with devotion, I offer to You the worship of the first enclosure.

One should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*, saying: "Obeisance to the illustrious Mahātripurasundarī, who consists of the rays of the manifest Yoginīs. Thus ends the first enclosure (*prathamāvaraṇa*).
Then, having offered a handful of flowers while reciting: "Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, obeisance to the wheel that fulfills all desires (*sarvāśāparipūraka-cakra*)."
Beginning from the foremost petal of the Goddess and proceeding counter-clockwise, one should worship the sixteen digits (kalās) of the Nityās:
4 AṂ Kāmākarṣaṇī Nityākalā Śrī,
4 ĀṂ Buddhyākarṣaṇī Nityākalā Śrī.

4 *Uṃ* Sparśākarṣiṇī Nityākalā Śrī.

4 eṃ Smṛtyākarṣaṇī Nityākalā Śrī.
4 Aiṃ, the eternal digit Śrī Nāmākarṣaṇī;
4 Oṃ, the eternal digit Śrī Bījākarṣaṇī;
4 Auṃ, the eternal digit Śrī Ātmākarṣaṇī.
4 Aṃ Amṛtākarṣaṇī Nityākalā Śrī, 4 Aḥ Śarīrākarṣaṇī Nityākalā Śrī— having thus worshipped and offered libations, [worship] 4 Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Tripureśvarī Cakreśvarī Śrī.
To her right: 4 Laghimā-siddhi Śrī; to her left: 4 Drīṃ Sarvavidrāviṇī Mudrādevī Śrī, 4 Kalādyā Śrī.
4. Having thrice gratified the Goddess with the root mantra (mūla), 4. drīṃ, and having displayed the Sarvavidrāviṇī mudrā; Śrī Brāhmyadarśana, Śrī Sauradarśana.

Taking the general *arghya* water mixed with fragrance, unbroken rice, and flowers, one offers worship with the words: "O you Guptayoginīs, who possess the mudrās in the wheel that fulfills all hopes," and so forth, [concluding with]:
"Grant me the attainment of my desired goal, O you who are compassionate toward those who have come for refuge."
With devotion, I offer to you this worship of the second enclosure.
One should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*, saying: "Obeisance to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who consists of the rays of the Guptayoginīs. This concludes the second enclosure (*āvaraṇa*).
One should offer a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) saying: "Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, obeisance to the wheel that agitates all (*sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇacakra*)."
Having deposited [the syllables], starting from the petal in front of the Goddess and proceeding through the four petals of the directions:
4 kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ, O Goddess Anaṅgakusumā, Śrī...; 4 caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ, O Goddess Anaṅgamekhalā, Śrī...;

[in the four corners starting from the southeast].

to her right—4 Mahimāsiddhi Śrī...

Having satiated the Goddess three times with the root mantra (mūla), and having displayed the *sarvākarṣaṇī* mudrā while reciting "klīṃ," one should take the water of the general offering (*sāmānyārghya*) together with scents, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and flowers; then,
having offered the worship beginning with "These most secret Yoginīs are present in the wheel that causes all agitation" (*etā guptatarayoginyaḥ sarvakṣobhaṇakārakacakre samudrā...*) and so forth.
O You who are affectionate toward those who have come for refuge, grant me the fulfillment of my desires;
with devotion, I offer to You the worship of the third enclosure.
[Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ] "Salutation to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who consists of the rays of the most secret Yoginīs.
Thus one should prostrate with the Yonimudrā.
This is the third enclosure (āvaraṇa).
Having offered a handful of flowers with "4 HSKLĪM HSAUḤ SARVASAUBHĀGYADĀYAKACAKRĀYA NAMAḤ," one begins from the front corner of the Goddess and proceeds counter-clockwise:
4 KAṂ SARVASAṂKṢOBHIṆĪŚAKTI ŚRĪ... [etc.]
4 Khaṃ, the power that causes all to flee, Śrī; 4 Gaṃ, the power that attracts all, Śrī; 4 Ghaṃ, the power that gladdens all, Śrī.
4 ṄAṂ, the power that deludes all, Śrī; 4 CAṂ, the power that paralyzes all, Śrī; 4 CHAṂ, the power that causes all to yawn, Śrī.
4 JAṂ Śrī Sarvavaśaṅkarī-śakti, 4 JHAṂ Śrī Sarvarañjanī-śakti,

One should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*, saying: "Obeisance to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who consists of the rays of the secret Yoginīs. This concludes the seventh enclosure.

4 Aiṃ, [I offer] the Yonimudrā to the Mother Goddess Śrī; having thus gratified her with drops from the Śrīpātra, and having displayed the Yonimudrā, one should take the water of the general offering (sāmānyārghya) together with fragrance, unbroken rice, and flowers, and [recite]: 4 These [are for] the Parāpara-Rahasya Yoginīs in the Bindu-cakra, which consists of all-bliss.

Meditating on the nine wheels as a single form, having displayed the thirteen mudrās beginning with Saṃkṣobhiṇī, and having gratified them with drops from the special *arghya*, one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*; thus, the ninth enclosure is always mandatory.

Then, having recited the thousand-syllable *Āvaraṇa*, [one says]: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ haṃ saḥ oṃ namo bhagavati akṣobhye rukṣakarṇi rākṣasi kṣapaṇe kṣape piṅgalākṣi huṅkāri vaḍavāmukhi hāhārāve mahākrodhe krodhini kharāsye sarvajñe tarale tāre*.
O Hṛṣṭā, Hṛllekhā, Daśakandharā, Sārasī, Rasasaṃgrāhiṇī, Tālajaṅghā, Raktākṣī, Vidyujjihvā, Karaṅkiṇī, Meghanādā, Pracaṇḍogrā, Kālākarṣiṇī, Kaṃbalapradā, Campā, Campāvalī,
Prapañcā, Pralayāntakā, Picuvaktrā, Piśitākṣī, Piśitākṣiṇī, Lolupā, and Vāmanā!
O Vānari, O Vāsavi, O you with a mutilated face, O Vāyuvega, O Bṛhatkukṣivikṛta, O Viśvarūpiṇī, O Yamajihvā, O Durjayi, O Yamāntaki, O Biḍāli, O Revati, O Pūjanā, O Vijayā, O Anantā, O Krandinī,
O Caṇḍā, O Ṭaṅkiṇī, O Taruṇī, O Parāruṇī, O you who are at the end of the eon, O Śāntā, O Aṇimā, O Laghimā, O Mahimā, O Īśitva!

O Mistress of mastery, O source of desire, O bestower of enjoyment, O giver of liberation, O mercury that brings about the dissolution of all things, O agitator of all, O subduer of all, O attractor of all, O bringer of all under control, O maddener of all,
O great goad of all, O sky-walker, O bearer of the wheel of the sky, O you whose form is the seed of all, O you whose form is the great womb, O three-sectioned one!

O Anaṅgabrahmāṇī, O Anaṅgamāheśī, O Anaṅgakaumārī, O Anaṅgavaiṣṇavī, O Anaṅgavārāhī, O Anaṅgendrāṇī, O Anaṅgacāmuṇḍā, O Anaṅgamahālakṣmī, O manifest Mistress of the Yoginīs, O you whose limbs are the Buddhist philosophy, O Sovereign of the Wheel that Enchants the Three Worlds, O Attractor of Desire!
O attractor of intellect, attractor of ego, attractor of sound, attractor of touch, attractor of form, attractor of taste,
attractor of smell, attractor of mind, attractor of fortitude, attractor of memory, attractor of name, attractor of seed-syllables, attractor of the self, attractor of nectar, attractor of the body!

O Guptayogeśī, whose body is the Vedic philosophy; O Mistress of the Wheel that fulfills all desires; O Anaṅgakusumā, Anaṅgamekhalā, Anaṅgamadanā, Anaṅgamadanāturā, Anaṅgarekhā, Anaṅgaveginī, Anaṅgāṅkuśā, and Anaṅgamālinī; O most secret Guptatarayogeśī, whose body is the Śaiva philosophy!
O Sovereign of the Wheel that Agitates All, Mistress of the Eastern Tradition, Bestower of Emanation, O Thou who Agitates All,
who Subdues All, who Attracts All, who Delights All, who Infatuates All,
who Paralyses All, who Expands All, O Thou who Brings All Under Control, who Enchants All, who Intoxicates All!
O accomplisher of all aims, fulfiller of all prosperity, composed of all mantras, destroyer of all duality;
O Yoginī of the lineage-wheel, whose limbs are the solar vision, sovereign of the wheel that bestows all good fortune,
granter of all attainments, granter of all wealth, maker of all dear things, and performer of all auspiciousness!
O bestower of all desires, liberator from all suffering, pacifier of all death, remover of all obstacles, beautiful in every limb, giver of all good fortune, Mistress of the Kula and Kaula Yoga,
Sovereign of the wheel that accomplishes all aims, omniscient one, omnipotent one, bestower of all sovereignty!

O You who consist of all-knowledge, O Destroyer of all diseases, O You whose very nature is the support of all, O Remover of all sins, O You who consist of all-bliss, O You whose very nature is the protection of all, O Bestower of the fruits of all desires, O Mistress of the Nigarbha Yoga, O Embodiment of the Vaiṣṇava vision, O Sovereign of the Cakra that grants all protection, O Mistress of the Dakṣiṇāmnāya, O Bestower of stability!

Rablūṃ Vaśinī, Klhrīṃ Kāmeśī, Nklīṃ Modinī, Ylūṃ Vimalā, Jmrīṃ Aruṇā, Hslryūṃ Jayinī, Jhmryūṃ Sarveśvarī, Kṣmrīṃ Kaulinī, O Mistress of the Secret Yoga, O You whose limbs are the Śākta vision, O Sovereign of the Wheel that removes all diseases, Drāṃ Klinne, O You with the arrow of desire that deludes!

O Mistress of the Yoga of the Supreme and the Non-Supreme Secret, O Embodiment of the Śāmbhava Vision, O Sovereign of the Wheel Consisting of All Bliss, O Mistress of the Western Tradition, O You who abide in Withdrawal! Aṃ Āṃ Sauḥ! O Tripurā! Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ! O Tripureśvarī!

O you whose meaning is the supreme transcendence of all conceptual proliferation; O bestower of knowledge; O you who are the body of all philosophical systems; O you whose essential nature transcends all philosophical systems;

I worship the sandals of the Mother Ghorakapālinī: *haṃsaḥ so'haṃ hsauṃḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ*. Thus, this thousand-syllable [mantra] of the enclosure (*varaṇa*) is to be known as belonging to that internal sequence. Next, one should worship the five pentads (*pañcapañcikā*). It is as follows:
O Supreme Goddess, likewise in the Bindu, in the central throne, and in the center,
the northeast, the southeast, the southwest, and the northwest, in due order.
In this very manner, one should worship the five Pañcikās,
as well as the five Lakṣmīs, the five Kośas, and the five Kalpalatās.
Likewise, the five single jewels are known as the five wish-fulfilling cows;
and so too are Śrīvidyā, Lakṣmī, and Mahālakṣmī.
The Triśakti, Sarvasāmrājya, Pañcalakṣmī, Śrīvidyā, Paraṃjyotis, Parā, Niṣkalā, and Śāmbhavī are proclaimed [as the eight forms].
The Ajapā and the Mātṛkā—these are proclaimed as the five sheaths (kośas).
Likewise, Śrīvidyā, Tvaritā, and Pārijāteśvarī.
Tripurā, Pañcabāṇeśī, Śrīvidyā, Siddhalakṣmī, Mātaṅgī, and Bhuvaneśvarī are remembered as the five Kalpalatās.
And Vārāhī—these are proclaimed as the five jewels (pañcaratna).

[worship] the Five Lakṣmīs (*pañcalakṣmī*)— the Goddess Tripurasundarī, who is the Sovereign Fortune of All (*sarvasāmrājyalakṣmī*), seated upon a throne adorned by the multitude of Sovereign Fortunes (*vṛndamaṇḍitāsanasaṃsthitā*)— by reciting the Śrīvidyā mantra and worshipping her in the center.
One should satisfy [the deity] with drops of the special *arghya* offering. (p.
211) Now, regarding the five sheaths (*pañcakośa*): having uttered the *Śrīvidyā* in the center, [one offers to] Śrī Mahākāmeśvarī Mahātripurasundarī, Śrī... [etc. 0.
In the northeast: *Oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā*, [I bow to] Śrī Pañcakośeśvarī, adorned by the multitude [of attendants], the Mother Kośāmbā of supreme light, Tripurasundarī.
In the southeast: *Oṃ* (four times), [I bow to] Śrī Pañcakośeśvarī, adorned by the multitude [of attendants], the Mother Kauśāmbā of the supreme partless reality (*niṣkala*).
In the southwest (Nairṛtya): 4 Oṃ hrīṃ haṃsaḥ sohaṃ svāhā. Pañcakośeśvarī, adorned by the multitude [of goddesses], Ajapākośāmbā, Tripurasundarī, Śrī 0.
In the northwest (Vāyavya): 4 aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḹṃ eṃ aiṃ oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ.

Kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ; the Mother (Mātṛkā), adorned by the multitude [of deities], is the sovereign of the five sheaths.
Kośāmbā Tripurasundarī Śrī.
In the center—having worshipped the Goddess with the root mantra (mūla) four times, one should offer libations; thus are the five sheaths (pañcakośa).
Now, the five Kalpalatās: having uttered the Śrīvidyā in the center, [one worships] the five Kalpalatās.
Vṛndamaṇḍitā Kalpalateśvarī Tripurasundarī, Śrī. In the northeast: 4 Oṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ Khe Ca Che Kṣa Strīṃ Huṃ Kṣeṃ Hrīṃ Phaṭ.
Pañcakalpalatā Vṛndamaṇḍitā Tvaritā Kalpalatā Tripurasundarī, Śrī.
In the southeast: 4 Oṃ Hrīṃ Hsklāiṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī; Hrīṃ Oṃ, [obeisance to] Tripurasundarī, the Mistress of the Five Kalpalatās, adorned by the multitude of creepers, Śrī.
In the southwest: 4 Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ, [obeisance to] the Five Kalpalatās, adorned by the multitude.

Tripurakalpalatā, Tripurasundarī, Śrī. In the northwest—4 drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ; having uttered the root-vidyā: Pañcakalpalatāvṛndamaṇḍitā, Pañcabāṇeśvarī, Kalpalatā, Tripurasundarī, Śrī. 4 [With] the root-mantra.
"Having fully worshipped the Goddess, one should satisfy her"—thus [it is said in] the *Pañcakalpalatās*.

Now, regarding the *Pañcakāmadudhās*: having uttered the *Śrīvidyā* in the center [with the syllable] "4," [one worships] the assembly of the five wish-fulfilling cows (*pañcakāmadudhāvṛnda*) as the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, the Sovereign of the Wish-Fulfilling Cows (*kāmadudheśvarī*); [the mantra is: *Śrī*.
In the northeast: 4 Oṃ hrīṃ jūṃ saḥ, O Sañjīvinī, make the life-force (jīva) situated in the knot of breath (prāṇa-granthi) [firm], do so, svāhā!
O host of the five wish-fulfilling cows, O Mistress of the Seat of Nectar, O Wish-Fulfilling Cow, O Tripurasundarī, Śrī!
In the southeast: Oṃ śrīṃ vadavāgvādini hsauṃḥ klinne kledini mahākṣobhaṃ kuru kuru hsauḥ pañcakāmadudhāvṛnda sudhākāmadudheśvarī tripurasundarī śrī.
In the southwest: Oṃ hrīṃ aiṃ amṛte amṛtodbhave amṛteśvarī amṛtavarṣiṇi amṛtaṃ.
Srāvaya srāvaya hrīṃ jūṃ saḥ svāhā! O assembly of the five wish-fulfilling cows, O Ameśvarī, O Kāmadudheśvarī, O Tripurasundarī, Śrī!
[In the northwest]—4 oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ namo bhagavati māheśvari annapūrṇe svāhā.
The group of five wish-fulfilling cows (*pañcakāmadudhāvṛnda*): Śrī Tripurasundarī, who is Annapūrṇā and the Wish-Fulfilling Cow (*kāmadudhā*).
Having worshipped the Goddess with the root mantra (*mūla*), one should satisfy her. Thus ends the five wish-fulfilling cows.
Now, the five jewels (*pañcaratna*): In the center—having uttered the *Śrīvidyā*, [one worships] Pañcaratneśvarī.

Vṛndamaṇḍitā — Pañcaranteśvarī Tripurasundarī Śrī. In the northeast: 4 Oṃ phreṃ phreṃ hsraiṃ aiṃ klīṃ mahācaṇḍatejasaṅkarṣiṇi hrīṃ hsrīṃ saḥ svāhā phreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sarvasiddhiyoginyai hskhphreṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ.

Omnisiddhi-mantra: HSKHPHREṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ! Salutation to the Goddess Caṇḍakālī, the eternally arisen one, who is delighted by bliss, the sovereign of the entire wheel of families (sakalakulacakranāyikā), HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HRUṂ PHREṂ OṂ HRĀṂ HRĪṂ HRUṂ PHREṂ KROṂ NAMAḤ KLINNE PHREṂ PARAMAHAṂSĪ.

O supreme one who reveals the path to nirvāṇa, [subdue] me... [bring them] under control... come, come! Strike, strike! O you who consume strength, blood, entrails, and fat, devour my enemies, devour them! Eat them, eat them!

Pierce, pierce with the trident! Cut, cut with the sword! O Tārkṣya, Tārkṣya, rend, rend! Lead away, devour! Hrīṃ Ha Sa Kṣa Ma La Va Ra Ya-Ūṃ! O most compassionate Goddess, Blessed One, accomplish, accomplish all my desires until they are fulfilled!

O you who assume the form of Mahābhairava, who are saluted by the best of the thirty [gods], O Mother of all mantras, O Goddess Mahākālī, who are affectionate toward those who bow before you, O destroyer of Time! Hrūṃ hrūṃ hrūṃ! Be gracious, O you who are afflicted by passion!
Āṃ hrīṃ kroṃ! Act, act! O daughter of the gods and asuras! Hrīṃ śrīṃ kroṃ huṃ!
*phaṭ svāhā*. *Hskhphreṃ phreṃ*, Pañcaranteśvarī adorned by the host [of goddesses], Siddhalakṣmī, Ratneśvarī, Tripurasundarī, Śrī.
In the southeast: 4 *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, obeisance to the Blessed One, Rājamātaṅgeśvarī, who captivates the minds of all people.

O you who delight all faces! *klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, O you who bring all kings under control! O you who bring all women and men under control! O you who bring all wicked beasts under control! O you who bring all beings under control! O you who bring all the worlds under control! Bring all people under my control, *svāhā*! *srauḥ? klīṃ? aiṃ śrīṃ*.
Hrīṃ Klīṃ, Pañcaratneśvarī adorned by the assembly [of deities], Rājamātaṅgīśvarī, Tripurasundarī, Śrī.
In the southwest: 4 Oṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Pañcaratneśvarī adorned by the assembly [of deities].

Bhuvaneśvarīśvarī Tripurasundarī Śrī. In the northwest: 4 Oṃ Aiṃ Glauṃ Oṃ. Salutations, O Blessed One, Vārtāli-Vārāhi! O Vārāhi, O boar-faced one! Salutations to Andhā, O Andhinī; salutations to Rundhā, O Rundhinī; salutations to Jambhā, O Jambhinī; salutations to Mohā, O Mohinī.

Homage to the pillar! Homage to the one who paralyzes! Homage to all those who are wicked and malicious! Paralyze, paralyze quickly the speech, mind, eyes, mouth, gait, and tongue of them all! Bring them under control, bring them under control!
Ṭhaḥ Ṭhaḥ Ṭhaḥ! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Glauṃ Aiṃ, O Mistress of the Five Jewels, adorned by the Vṛnda! (p. 215) — Vārāhī, Mistress of the Five Jewels, Tripurasundarī, Śrī!
— Aiṃ Glauṃ Aiṃ, salutations, O Blessed One, Vārtālī, Vārāhī, O Boar-faced One! Aiṃ Glauṃ Aiṃ.

Homage to Andhe! Homage to Andhini! Homage to Rundhe! Homage to Rudhini! Homage to Jambhe! Homage to Jambhini! Homage to Mohe! Homage to Mohini! Homage to Stambhe! Homage to Stambhini! Aiṃ Glauṃ Aiṃ! Paralyze the speech, mind, eyes, face, movement, and tongue of all those who are wicked or extremely wicked; perform, perform this paralyzing!
"Quickly bring [him] under control, kuru kuru! Aiṃ glauṃ aiṃ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ ṭhaḥ huṃ phaṭ svāhā! O Vārāhī, Pañcaratneśvarī, Tripurasundarī, Śrī! Thus are the five jewels.
This is the procedure for the worship of the five pentads (pañcapañcikā).

Now, if one is initiated according to the *Āmnāya*, having written out the *Krama* and performed the worship of the *Śrīcakra*, at its conclusion, one should perform the *ṛṣi*-application and the six-limbed (*ṣaḍaṅga*) application for the *Prāsāda-parāparā* mantra.
Then, having meditated upon her as "rising from the midst of the ocean of nectar" and displayed the ten mudrās, [one proceeds] as before.
Having meditated upon Tripurasundarī herself as the supreme form (Parā), one should satisfy her three times with the substance contained in the Śrīpātra vessel; then,
having satisfied her twenty-eight times with the root-mantra of Prāsāda (the Parāparā),
one should [visualize] the first Anuttara lotus of eight petals around those drops, outside of which are sixteen petals and then twenty-six petals.

Having meditated upon the great wheel (*mahācakra*) consisting of six lotuses—namely, one with thirty-eight petals, one with fourteen petals, and one with fifty-one petals—one should worship it in the form of a cycle (*vṛtti*). It is as follows:
*Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsauḥ shauṃḥ aṃ, salutation to the one whose form is the manifold world (*prapañca*); [to the] venerable sandals.*
I worship; salutation!

6 Āṃ, to Mayā, who is the form of the island, salutation; I worship the venerable sandals; salutation! 6 Iṃ, to Kamalā, who is the form of the ocean, salutation; I worship the venerable sandals; salutation!
6 *Īṃ*, obeisance to the one whose form is the mountain, the bearer of the lotus; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

6 *Uṃ*, obeisance to the one whose form is the city, the bearer of the lotus; [I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance]. 6 *Ūṃ*, obeisance to the one whose form is the sacred seat (*pīṭha*), the daughter of the ocean; [I worship the venerable sandals].
Namaḥ!
6. Ṛṃ, obeisance to Lokamātā, who is the form of the sacred field (kṣetra). The seed-syllable of Prasāda should be joined at the beginning; she is the supreme and non-supreme grace (prasāda).

6 Ṛṃ, obeisance to her whose form is the forest-dweller, the resident of the lotus; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Ḷṃ, obeisance to Indirā, whose form is the hermitage; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 Ḹṃ, obeisance to Māyā, whose form is the cave; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

6 Eṃ, obeisance to Ramā in the form of a river; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Aiṃ, obeisance to Padmā in the form of a crossroads; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Oṃ, obeisance to Nārāyaṇapriyā in the form of that which is born from the earth; I worship the venerable sandals.
*Namaḥ*, 6 *Oṃ* to the Royal Fortune (*Rājalakṣmī*) in the form of moisture-born beings, *namaḥ*; I worship the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*), *namaḥ*.
6 *Aṃ* to the Royal Fortune (*Rājalakṣmī*) in the form of egg-born beings, *namaḥ*; I worship the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*), *namaḥ*.

6 Aḥ, obeisance to Mahālakṣmī in the form of the viviparous; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Kaṃ, obeisance to Āryā in the form of Time; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Khaṃ, obeisance to Umā in the form of the *truṭi* (unit of time); I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 Gaṃ, salutation to Candrikā in the form of a digit (kalā); I worship the venerable sandals, salutation.
6 Ghaṃ, salutation to Durgā in the form of a measure of time (kāṣṭhā); I worship the venerable sandals, salutation.
6 Ṅaṃ, salutation to Śivā in the form of a moment (nimiṣa); I worship the venerable sandals, salutation.
6 Caṃ, obeisance to Aparṇā in the form of breath; I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 Chaṃ, obeisance to Ambikā in the form of the ghaṭikā; I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 Jaṃ, obeisance to Satī in the form of the muhūrta; I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 Jhaṃ, obeisance to the Śrīpādukā of Īśvarī, who is the form of the watch (prahara); I worship her, obeisance.

6 Ñaṃ, obeisance to the Śrīpādukā of Śāmbhavī, who is the form of the day; I worship her, obeisance. 6 Ṭaṃ, obeisance to the Śrīpādukā of Īśānī, who is the form of the twilight (sandhyā); I worship her, obeisance.
6 Ṭhaṃ, obeisance to Pārvatī in the form of the night; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 Ḍaṃ, obeisance to Sarvamaṅgalā in the form of the lunar day (tithi); I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 Ḍhaṃ, obeisance to Dākṣāyaṇī in the form of the day of the week (vāra); I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 ṇaṃ, salutations to Haimavatī in the form of the lunar mansions; I worship the venerable sandals, salutations.

6 taṃ, salutations to Mahāmāyā in the form of Yoga; I worship the venerable sandals, salutations. 6 thaṃ, salutations to Māheśvarī in the form of the ear; I worship the venerable sandals, salutations.
6 daṃ, obeisance to Mṛḍānī in the form of the lunar fortnight; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 dhaṃ, obeisance to Rudrāṇī in the form of the month; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 naṃ, obeisance to Śarvāṇī in the form of the zodiac sign; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

6 Paṃ, obeisance to the Supreme Sovereign in the form of the Seasons; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Phaṃ, obeisance to Kālī in the form of the Solar Transits; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Baṃ, obeisance to Kātyāyanī in the form of the Year; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 Bhaṃ, obeisance to Gaurī, whose form is the Yuga; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

6 Maṃ, obeisance to Bhavānī, whose form is dissolution; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Yaṃ, obeisance to Brāhmī, whose form is the five elements; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

6 RAṂ, salutation to Vāgīśvarī, who is the form of the five subtle elements (tanmātras); I worship the Śrīpādukā, salutation. 6 LAṂ, salutation to Vāṇī, who is the form of the five organs of action (karmendriyas); I worship the Śrīpādukā.
Namaḥ,
6 Vaṃ, obeisance to Sāvitrī, who is the form of the five faculties of knowledge; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

6 Śaṃ, obeisance to Sarasvatī in the form of the five vital breaths; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 Ṣaṃ, obeisance to Gāyatrī in the form of the three qualities (guṇas); I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 Saṃ, obeisance to Vākpradā in the form of the fourfold internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa-catuṣṭaya); I worship the venerable sandals.
I worship; salutations!
(p. 218) 6. Haṃ, to Bhāratī, who is the form of the three states, salutations; I worship the venerable sandals, salutations!
6 Laṃ, obeisance to Bhāratī, whose form consists of the seven constituent elements (dhātus); I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 Kṣaṃ, obeisance to her whose form consists of the three humors (doṣas) and who is of the nature of knowledge (vidyā); I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 O Parāmbā, who embodies all the deities and is adorned with fifty petals; [I worship] the Śrīpādukā.
I worship; obeisance!

Having displayed the *yonimudrā*, [one says]: "O You who are affectionate toward those who have come for refuge, grant me the attainment of my desired goal with these perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers."
With devotion, I offer to you this worship of the first enclosure.

Having thus worshipped, one should display the *yonimudrā* while reciting: "Obeisance to the venerable Goddess Parāmbā, who consists of the rays of all the deities of the phenomenal universe (*sakalaprapañcadevatāmayūkhāyai śrīparāmbādevyai namaḥ*). This concludes the first enclosure (*prathamāvaraṇa*).
One should offer a handful of flowers (*puṣpāñjali*) while reciting: "Obeisance to the fourteen-petaled wheel (*caturdaśadalacakrāya namaḥ*)."
Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ:
Salutation to the Mother, the Supportive Power (Ādhāraśakti), who is joined with the primordial deities (Mūladevatās) and hundreds of millions of Yoginīs dwelling in the netherworld (Atalaloka);
I worship the Śrīpādukā, salutation! Salutation!

Īṃ Ūṃ Ūṃ! Ombā, the Mother, the Supportive Power (Ādhāraśakti) who resides in the Vitala world, joined with the primordial deity (Mūladevatā), the infinite Yoginīs, and the hundred million most secret [deities]; salutation to the Goddess!
I worship the Śrīpādukā; salutation!

Salutation to the Mother, the foundational power (*ādhāraśakti*), who is joined with the root deity (*mūladevatā*), the inconceivable Yoginī, and the hundreds of millions of most secret ones residing in the world of Suta; I worship the Śrīpādukā, salutation!
(p. 219) 6. *Ḷṃ Eṃ Aiṃ*, [salutation to] the Mahāguhya-svatantra-yoginī residing in the hundreds of millions [of worlds] in the world of Mahātala.
Salutation to the Mother, the Support-Power (Ādhāra-Śakti) united with the Root Deity; I worship the Śrīpādukā, salutation.
6 Oṃ Auṃ, to the one whose abode is the Talātala world, the hundred crores of supreme secrets.
Salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, united with the root deity of the Icchā-yoginīs; I worship the Śrī-pādukā, salutation!
6. Aṃ Aḥ, salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, united with the root deity of the hundred million secret-knowledge Yoginīs residing in the world of Rasātala.
Salutation to Śakti Ambā Devī; I worship the Śrīpādukā, salutation.

(6) Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ; salutation to the Śrīpādukā of the support Śakti Ambā Devī, who is joined with the root deity of the hundred crore most secret Kriyāyoginīs residing in the world of Pātāla. I worship [it].

Namaḥ, 6 caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ; salutations to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti Ambādevī, who dwells in the Bhūrloka, who is accompanied by hundreds of millions of most secret Ḍākinīs and Yoginīs, and who is the primordial deity— *namaḥ*, I worship the Śrīpādukā.
Namaḥ.

6 Ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ. Salutations to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti Ambā, who is joined with the root deity, the Yoginīs, and the Rākinīs of the hundred million great secrets residing in the Bhuvarloka; I worship her Śrīpādukā.

Namaḥ, 6 taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ, salutations to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti Ambādevī, who is accompanied by the primordial deity Lākinī, the Yoginī, the supreme secret of the hundreds of millions of inhabitants of Svarloka; I worship her Śrīpādukā.
Namaḥ!

6 Paṃ Phaṃ Baṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ, salutations to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti Ambādevī, who resides in Maharloka, is accompanied by hundreds of millions of Guptakākinīs and Yoginīs, and is the primordial deity; I worship her venerable sandals (śrīpādukā).

Namaḥ, 6 yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ, salutations to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti Ambādevī, together with the root deity, the Śākinīs, and Yoginīs, who are more secret than the hundreds of millions residing in Janaloka; I worship the Śrīpādukā, namaḥ.

6 Śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ, salutation to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who is united with the root deity, the Yoginī Hākinī, who is the most secret among hundreds of millions dwelling in the world of Tapas; I worship the Śrīpādukā, salutation.
6 Laṃ kṣaṃ, [salutation to the Mother Goddess] who is united with the root deity, the Yoginī Mahāguptayākinī, who dwells in Satyaloka among hundreds of millions...
Salutation to the Goddess Śakti Ambā, the support of the Yugas; I worship the Śrīpādukā, salutation.

(6) Having uttered the Mātṛkā from the letter *A* to the letter *Kṣa*: Salutation to the venerable Parāmbā Devī, the sovereign of the fourteen worlds. (6) Adorned with fourteen petals, consisting of the fourteen worlds.
I worship the Śrīpādukā of the venerable Śrīparāmbā; salutations!

Having displayed the Liṅgamudrā, [one says]: "O You who are affectionate toward those who have come for refuge, grant me the attainment of my desired goal with these perfumes, unbroken grains, and flowers."
With devotion, I offer to you this worship of the second enclosure.
6. "Salutation to Parāmbā, whose rays consist of the fourteen worlds"—thus one should prostrate with the *yonimudrā*.
This is the second enclosure (*āvaraṇa*).
6. "I worship the venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*) of the thirty-eight-petaled wheel; salutation."
6 Aṃ Keśava-Akṣaryābhyāṃ namaḥ, I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 Āṃ Nārāyaṇa-Ādyābhyāṃ namaḥ, I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance. 6 Iṃ Mādhava-Iṣṭadābhyāṃ namaḥ, I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 *Īṃ*, obeisance to Govinda and Īśānī; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 *Uṃ*, obeisance to Viṣṇu and Ugrā; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 *Ūṃ*, obeisance to Madhusūdana and Ūrdhvanayanā; I worship the venerable sandals.
Namaḥ, 6 Ṛṃ, obeisance to Trivikrama and Ṛddhi; I worship the Śrīpādukā, namaḥ. 6 Ṝṃ, obeisance to Vāmana and Rūpiṇī; I worship the Śrīpādukā, namaḥ.
6 ḶṂ, obeisance to Śrīdhara and Lupta; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance. 6 ḸṂ, obeisance to Hṛṣīkeśa and Doṣa; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 EṂ, obeisance to Padmanābha and Ekanāyaka; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

6 Aiṃ, obeisance to Vāmodara and Aiṅkāriṇī; I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance. 6 Oṃ, obeisance to Vāsudeva and Oghavatī; I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance. 6 Auṃ, obeisance to Saṅkarṣaṇa and Arkamālā; I worship the Śrīpādukā, obeisance.
6 Aṃ, obeisance to Pradyumna and Añjanaprabhā; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.
6 Aḥ, obeisance to Aniruddha and Asthimālādhara; I worship the venerable sandals, obeisance.

One should contemplate the wheel-deities, the Guru, and the Self as non-different. [The mantra is: "The thousand-petaled lotus..."

Having meditated and worshipped one's own guru with the *pādukā* mantra, and having offered libations, one should worship the lineage of gurus of the *ūrdhvāmnāya* upon the head. That is to say: the row of venerable gurus (*śrīgurupaṅkti*) should be remembered on the crown of the head, and one's own *pādukā* at the *mūlādhāra*.
First the sandals, then the feet, and after that the Mother, the nine Lords, the sixteen Root-Vidyās,
the six supports, O Mistress of the Gods, and again the two feet— this is the sequence.
She holds the *cinmudrā* and a skull-cup filled with honey in her two hands;
she possesses a complexion like molten gold, is adorned with red flowers, unguents, and garments;
her side-glances are full of compassion, her eyes are crimson, and her hair is like a shower of rain.
Having fixed his mind on the lineage of gurus, he worshipped them with divine streams [of offerings].
